# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)

</details>



This document provides a high-level introduction to PINDER (Protein INteraction Dataset and Evaluation Resource), explaining its purpose, architecture, and key components. PINDER is a comprehensive dataset and evaluation resource for training and evaluating protein-protein docking algorithms, providing approximately 700GB of structural data with 2.4M+ training pairs.

For specific details about the dataset structure, see [Dataset Structure](#1.3). For information about installing PINDER, see [Installation](#1.2). For hands-on tutorials, see [Quick Start Guide](#2).

---

## Purpose and Scope

PINDER addresses the challenge of flexible protein-protein docking by providing the first large-scale dataset that includes paired predicted and apo (unbound) structures alongside holo (bound) structures. The dataset is approximately 500x larger than previous state-of-the-art datasets and enables comprehensive evaluation of both rigid and flexible docking methods.

**Key capabilities:**
- Training machine learning models on 2.4M+ protein-protein interaction pairs
- Evaluating docking methods on multiple benchmark test sets (PINDER-XL, PINDER-S, PINDER-AF2)
- Loading and filtering protein structures with various quality criteria
- Computing standard CAPRI docking evaluation metrics
- Accessing extensive structural annotations and metadata

Sources: [README.md:14-17](), [README.md:245-286]()

---

## System Architecture

The PINDER ecosystem consists of four main packages organized as a namespace package structure:

| Package | Purpose | Key Modules |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `pinder-core` | Data structures, loading, and dataset access | `pinder.core.index`, `pinder.core.loader`, `pinder.core.structure` |
| `pinder-data` | Dataset generation pipeline from RCSB PDB | `pinder.data.pipeline`, `pinder.data.annotation` |
| `pinder-eval` | Evaluation harness and CAPRI metrics | `pinder.eval.dockq`, `pinder.eval.metrics` |
| `pinder-methods` | Reference docking method implementations | `pinder.methods` |

Sources: [README.md:689-696](), [pyproject.toml:1-158]()

This diagram shows how data flows from RCSB through the generation pipeline to cloud storage, and then how the core package provides access layers that feed into machine learning workflows and evaluation.

## Core Data Structures

PINDER provides three primary abstractions for working with protein structures:

### Data Structure Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "High-Level Abstraction"
        PSYS["PinderSystem<br/>src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py<br/>Manages complete complex"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Component Structures"
        NATIVE["native<br/>Structure instance<br/>Ground truth complex"]
        HOLO_R["holo_receptor<br/>Structure instance<br/>Bound receptor"]
        HOLO_L["holo_ligand<br/>Structure instance<br/>Bound ligand"]
        APO_R["apo_receptor<br/>Structure instance<br/>Unbound receptor"]
        APO_L["apo_ligand<br/>Structure instance<br/>Unbound ligand"]
        PRED_R["pred_receptor<br/>Structure instance<br/>AlphaFold2 receptor"]
        PRED_L["pred_ligand<br/>Structure instance<br/>AlphaFold2 ligand"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Low-Level Structure"
        STRUCT["Structure<br/>src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/structure.py<br/>Wraps biotite.AtomArray"]
        ATOMS["AtomArray<br/>biotite.structure<br/>Atomic coordinates"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Metadata"
        IENTRY["IndexEntry<br/>58 annotation fields"]
        MENTRY["MetadataEntry<br/>45+ annotation fields"]
    end
    
    PSYS --> NATIVE
    PSYS --> HOLO_R
    PSYS --> HOLO_L
    PSYS --> APO_R
    PSYS --> APO_L
    PSYS --> PRED_R
    PSYS --> PRED_L
    
    NATIVE -.->|"instance of"| STRUCT
    HOLO_R -.->|"instance of"| STRUCT
    HOLO_L -.->|"instance of"| STRUCT
    APO_R -.->|"instance of"| STRUCT
    APO_L -.->|"instance of"| STRUCT
    PRED_R -.->|"instance of"| STRUCT
    PRED_L -.->|"instance of"| STRUCT
    
    STRUCT --> ATOMS
    
    PSYS --> IENTRY
    PSYS --> MENTRY
```

Each `PinderSystem` manages multiple `Structure` instances representing different conformational states (bound/unbound) and sources (experimental/predicted). All structures are backed by `biotite.AtomArray` objects for efficient atomic operations.

Sources: [README.md:395-408](), [README.md:529-623]()

## Dataset Scale and Splits

PINDER provides multiple dataset splits optimized for different use cases:

| Split | Size | Clusters | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| **PINDER-Train** | 2,456,152 pairs | 42,220 | Training set with holo/apo/predicted variants |
| **PINDER-Val** | 1,958 pairs | 1,958 | Validation set matching test distribution |
| **PINDER-XL** | 1,955 pairs | 1,955 | Full test set, cluster representatives |
| **PINDER-S** | 250 pairs | 250 | Fast evaluation subset with diverse annotations |
| **PINDER-AF2** | 180 pairs | 180 | AlphaFold2-Multimer deleaked test set |

### Structure Type Availability

| Dataset | Holo Pairs | Apo Pairs | AF2 Pairs | At Least One Apo | At Least One AF2 |
|---------|------------|-----------|-----------|------------------|------------------|
| Train | 2,456,152 | 136,498 | 566,171 | 274,194 | 621,276 |
| Val | 1,958 | 342 | 1,789 | 441 | 1,817 |
| XL | 1,955 | 342 | 1,747 | 436 | 1,775 |
| S | 250 | 93 | 250 | 143 | 250 |
| AF2 | 180 | 30 | 127 | - | 131 |

The training set provides up to **25,130,994 unique training examples** when combining different monomer types (holo-receptor + apo-ligand, etc.).

Sources: [README.md:245-286](), [README.md:757-785]()

## Data Access Patterns

PINDER provides multiple levels of abstraction for accessing data, from low-level structure manipulation to high-level PyTorch dataloaders:

### Data Loading Pipeline

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Storage Layer"
        FILES["Parquet Files<br/>index.parquet<br/>metadata.parquet"]
        PDB_DIR["PDB Files<br/>pdbs/ directory"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Loading"
        LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>pinder.core.loader.loader.PinderLoader<br/>Iterator with filtering"]
        FILTER_BASE["Base Filters<br/>FilterByMissingHolo<br/>FilterMetadataFields"]
        FILTER_SUB["Sub Filters<br/>FilterSubByAtomTypes<br/>FilterByHoloSeqIdentity"]
        FILTER_STRUCT["Structure Filters<br/>SelectAtomTypes<br/>StructureFilter"]
    end
    
    subgraph "System Management"
        PSYSTEM["PinderSystem<br/>pinder.core.index.system.PinderSystem<br/>loads() method"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dataset Implementations"
        TORCH_DS["PinderDataset<br/>torch.utils.data.Dataset<br/>dict of tensors"]
        GEO_DS["PPIDataset<br/>torch_geometric.data.Dataset<br/>HeteroData graphs"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Batch Processing"
        TORCH_DL["torch.DataLoader<br/>get_torch_loader()<br/>Mini-batch training"]
        GEO_DL["torch_geometric.DataLoader<br/>get_geo_loader()<br/>Graph batch training"]
    end
    
    FILES --> LOADER
    PDB_DIR --> PSYSTEM
    
    FILTER_BASE --> LOADER
    FILTER_SUB --> LOADER
    FILTER_STRUCT --> LOADER
    
    LOADER -->|"yields"| PSYSTEM
    
    PSYSTEM --> TORCH_DS
    PSYSTEM --> GEO_DS
    
    TORCH_DS --> TORCH_DL
    GEO_DS --> GEO_DL
```

The `PinderLoader` class ([src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py]()) orchestrates the entire loading pipeline, applying three-tier filtering and yielding `PinderSystem` objects. These can be consumed directly or wrapped in PyTorch dataset classes for training.

Sources: [README.md:410-432](), [README.md:433-514]()

---

## Key Features

### 1. Multi-State Structure Management

Each protein complex in PINDER is represented by up to 7 structures:

- **Native complex**: Ground-truth crystal structure of the complex
- **Holo monomers**: Bound receptor and ligand (extracted from native)
- **Apo monomers**: Unbound receptor and ligand (from separate PDB entries)
- **Predicted monomers**: AlphaFold2-predicted receptor and ligand structures

All monomers follow a consistent chain naming convention: **R** for receptor, **L** for ligand.

Sources: [README.md:395-408]()

### 2. Flexible Filtering System

PINDER implements a three-tier filtering system:

| Tier | Class Hierarchy | Purpose |
|------|----------------|---------|
| **Base Filters** | `PinderFilterBase` | System-level criteria (e.g., missing structures, metadata fields) |
| **Sub Filters** | `PinderFilterSubBase` | Monomer-level criteria (e.g., sequence identity, RMSD, length) |
| **Structure Filters** | `StructureFilter` | Atom/residue-level properties (e.g., atom types, contact counts) |

Sources: [README.md:410-432](), [README.md:517-670]()

### 3. Comprehensive Annotations

Each system includes 58 index fields and 45+ metadata fields covering:

- **Quality metrics**: Resolution, R-free, experimental method
- **Interface properties**: Buried SASA, contact types, planarity
- **Structural features**: Elongation, gaps, number of components
- **Biological context**: Antibody/antigen/enzyme annotations, UniProt IDs
- **Domain annotations**: ECOD, Pfam, SCOP, CATH

Sources: [README.md:529-623]()

### 4. Evaluation Harness

The `pinder-eval` package provides standardized evaluation using CAPRI metrics:

- **DockQ**: Overall quality score combining multiple metrics
- **iRMS**: Interface RMSD (backbone atoms)
- **LRMS**: Ligand RMSD (all atoms)
- **Fnat**: Fraction of native contacts preserved

The `pinder_eval` CLI script ([pyproject.toml:41]()) processes prediction directories and generates leaderboard-ready results.

Sources: [README.md:300-381]()

---

## Entry Points and CLI Tools

PINDER provides several command-line tools for common operations:

| Command | Module | Purpose |
|---------|--------|---------|
| `pinder_download` | `pinder.core.index.utils` | Download complete dataset from GCS |
| `pinder_update_index` | `pinder.core.index.utils` | Sync index files with latest version |
| `pinder_sync_data` | `pinder.core.index.utils` | Sync modified structure files |
| `pinder_eval` | `pinder.eval.run` | Evaluate docking predictions |
| `pinder_data` | `pinder.data.run` | Run data generation pipeline |
| `pinder_methods` | `pinder.methods.main` | Run reference docking methods |

Sources: [pyproject.toml:38-47](), [README.md:146-239]()

---

## Versioning and Updates

PINDER uses independent versioning for dataset and code:

### Dataset Versioning

- Format: `year-month` (e.g., `2024-02`)
- Current version: `2024-02`
- Location: `~/.local/share/pinder/<version>` by default
- Can be overridden with `PINDER_BASE_DIR` environment variable

### Code Versioning

- Format: Semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)
- Managed via `setuptools_scm` ([pyproject.toml:135-136]())
- Git tag-based version generation

**Update types:**
- **Minor**: Index/metadata changes without test set invalidation
- **Major**: Structural changes requiring re-clustering (announced in advance)

Sources: [README.md:788-801](), [README.md:122-144]()

# Page: What is PINDER

# What is PINDER

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page provides an overview of the PINDER dataset - its composition, scale, structure types, and organization. For installation instructions, see [Installation](#1.2). For details on dataset splits and benchmarks, see [Dataset Splits and Benchmarks](#1.4). For information on how to load and work with PINDER data programmatically, see [Core Data Structures](#3).

---

## Dataset Overview

**PINDER** (Protein INteraction Dataset and Evaluation Resource) is a large-scale protein-protein interaction dataset designed for training and evaluating flexible docking methods. It is approximately 500x larger than previous state-of-the-art datasets and is the first to systematically pair holo (bound) structures with both apo (unbound) and predicted structures from AlphaFold for flexible docking scenarios.

The dataset contains **2,456,152 training pairs** derived from **62,706 PDB entries** organized into **42,220 interface clusters**. Test and validation sets provide carefully deleaked benchmarks with **1,955**, **250**, and **180** systems in the PINDER-XL, PINDER-S, and PINDER-AF2 test sets respectively.

The complete dataset is approximately **700GB** and is hosted on Google Cloud Storage at `gs://pinder/2024-02/`.

Sources: [README.md:14-18](), [README.md:242-286]()

---

## Dataset Composition

The PINDER dataset consists of multiple carefully curated splits designed for different training and evaluation purposes:

| Dataset | # PDB IDs | # Clusters | # Holo Pairs | # Apo Pairs | # AF2 Pairs | Description |
|---------|-----------|------------|--------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| **PINDER-Train** | 62,706 | 42,220 | 2,456,152 | 136,498 | 566,171 | Training set with extensive examples including paired apo and predicted structures |
| **PINDER-Val** | 1,958 | 1,958 | 1,958 | 342 | 1,789 | Validation holdout set for monitoring training performance |
| **PINDER-XL** | 1,955 | 1,955 | 1,955 | 342 | 1,747 | Full test set with cluster representatives |
| **PINDER-S** | 250 | 250 | 250 | 93 | 250 | Smaller subset of PINDER-XL for fast evaluation with diverse annotations |
| **PINDER-AF2** | 180 | 180 | 180 | 30 | 127 | Subset deleaked against AF2-Multimer training set using iAlign |

Sources: [README.md:244-278]()

---

## Structure Types in PINDER

PINDER provides multiple structural representations for each protein-protein interaction, enabling flexible docking evaluation. Each system can include up to seven distinct structures organized through the `PinderSystem` abstraction.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "PinderSystem Data Structure"
        PS["PinderSystem<br/>(core/index/system.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Native Complex"
        NATIVE["native<br/>Ground-truth dimer<br/>Chains: R, L"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Holo Structures (Bound)"
        HOLO_R["holo_receptor<br/>Receptor in bound state<br/>Chain: R"]
        HOLO_L["holo_ligand<br/>Ligand in bound state<br/>Chain: L"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Apo Structures (Unbound)"
        APO_R["apo_receptor<br/>Receptor in unbound state<br/>Chain: A (stored)<br/>Chain: R (when loaded)"]
        APO_L["apo_ligand<br/>Ligand in unbound state<br/>Chain: A (stored)<br/>Chain: R (when loaded)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Predicted Structures"
        PRED_R["predicted_receptor<br/>AlphaFold prediction<br/>Chain: A (stored)<br/>Chain: R (when loaded)"]
        PRED_L["predicted_ligand<br/>AlphaFold prediction<br/>Chain: A (stored)<br/>Chain: L (when loaded)"]
    end
    
    PS -->|"property: native"| NATIVE
    PS -->|"property: holo_receptor"| HOLO_R
    PS -->|"property: holo_ligand"| HOLO_L
    PS -->|"property: apo_receptor"| APO_R
    PS -->|"property: apo_ligand"| APO_L
    PS -->|"property: predicted_receptor"| PRED_R
    PS -->|"property: predicted_ligand"| PRED_L
```

### Structure Type Definitions

**Native Complex**: The ground-truth crystal structure showing both proteins in their bound conformation. This serves as the target for docking evaluation.

**Holo Structures**: Monomers extracted from the bound complex. These represent the proteins in their bound conformations and are the easiest case for docking since they are already in the correct conformation.

**Apo Structures**: Unbound monomers matched from other PDB entries with the same UniProt ID. These structures represent the proteins in conformations different from the bound state, requiring conformational sampling during docking. Available for **44,330** unique structures (41,630 receptor and 36,910 ligand monomers).

**Predicted Structures**: AlphaFold2 predictions matched by UniProt ID. These represent computationally predicted structures and are available for **42,827** unique structures (37,095 receptor and 38,801 ligand monomers).

Each structure is represented as a `Structure` object that wraps a biotite `AtomArray` with additional functionality for filtering, alignment, and property access.

Sources: [README.md:398-408](), [README.md:707-709](), [README.md:773-778](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py]()

---

## Dataset Organization on Disk

PINDER data is organized in a hierarchical directory structure designed for efficient access and storage:

```mermaid
graph TB
    ROOT["~/.local/share/pinder/2024-02/<br/>(Default location)"]
    
    subgraph "Structure Files"
        PDBS["pdbs/<br/>672GB unpacked"]
        TEST_PDBS["test_set_pdbs/<br/>705MB unpacked"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Mapping Files"
        MAPPINGS["mappings/<br/>25GB unpacked<br/>PDB↔UniProt mappings"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Index Files"
        INDEX["index.parquet<br/>Master index<br/>IndexEntry schema<br/>58 annotation fields"]
        METADATA["metadata.parquet<br/>Detailed metadata<br/>MetadataEntry schema<br/>45+ annotation fields"]
    end
    
    ROOT --> PDBS
    ROOT --> TEST_PDBS
    ROOT --> MAPPINGS
    ROOT --> INDEX
    ROOT --> METADATA
    
    PDBS --> PDB_FILES["*.pdb files<br/>Native dimers<br/>Holo monomers<br/>Apo monomers<br/>Predicted monomers"]
    
    INDEX --> LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>(core/loader/loader.py)"]
    METADATA --> LOADER
    PDBS --> SYSTEM["PinderSystem<br/>(core/index/system.py)"]
```

### Directory Contents

**`pdbs/`**: Contains all protein structures including native dimers, holo monomers, apo monomers, and predicted monomers. Individual PDB files follow naming conventions that encode system IDs and chain information.

**`test_set_pdbs/`**: Pre-rotated and translated monomer structures for test sets, ready for direct use in docking evaluation without additional preprocessing.

**`mappings/`**: Contains mapping information between PDB and UniProt coordinate systems, as well as original PDB assembly information used by various utilities.

**`index.parquet`**: The master index containing one row per protein-protein interaction system. Each entry includes 58 annotation fields covering cluster assignments, split membership, structure availability flags, and quality metrics. This file is read by `PinderLoader` to filter and sample systems.

**`metadata.parquet`**: Extended metadata with 45+ additional fields including experimental method, resolution, interface characteristics (planarity, buried SASA, contact types), oligomeric state, and structural quality metrics.

The default location is `~/.local/share/pinder/<release_version>` on Mac and Linux. This can be customized by setting the `PINDER_BASE_DIR` environment variable.

Sources: [README.md:162-208](), [README.md:529-624]()

---

## Data Access Through Code

PINDER provides a Python API for accessing the dataset through several key abstractions:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "User Code"
        USER["Your Code"]
    end
    
    subgraph "High-Level Access"
        GET_LOC["get_pinder_location()<br/>(core/__init__.py)"]
        LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>(core/loader/loader.py)"]
        DATASET["PinderDataset<br/>(core/loader/dataset.py)"]
        GEO_DS["PPIDataset<br/>(core/loader/geodata.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Abstractions"
        SYSTEM["PinderSystem<br/>(core/index/system.py)"]
        STRUCTURE["Structure<br/>(core/loader/structure.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Files"
        INDEX[("index.parquet")]
        PDBS[("pdbs/")]
    end
    
    USER --> GET_LOC
    USER --> LOADER
    USER --> DATASET
    USER --> GEO_DS
    
    GET_LOC --> INDEX
    LOADER --> INDEX
    LOADER --> SYSTEM
    DATASET --> LOADER
    GEO_DS --> LOADER
    
    SYSTEM --> STRUCTURE
    SYSTEM --> PDBS
```

**`get_pinder_location()`**: Returns the current dataset location on disk. Used to verify where PINDER data is stored.

**`PinderLoader`**: Iterator-based loader that provides filtered access to `PinderSystem` objects. Supports multi-stage filtering (base, sub, structure), monomer selection strategies, and transforms.

**`PinderDataset`**: PyTorch `Dataset` implementation that converts `PinderSystem` objects into dictionaries of tensors for standard neural networks.

**`PPIDataset`**: PyTorch Geometric `Dataset` implementation that converts `PinderSystem` objects into `HeteroData` graph representations for graph neural networks.

**`PinderSystem`**: Core abstraction representing a single protein-protein interaction with all associated structures (native, holo, apo, predicted).

**`Structure`**: Wraps biotite's `AtomArray` with additional methods for filtering, alignment, sequence operations, and coordinate manipulation.

Sources: [README.md:137-140](), [README.md:392-427](), [README.md:437-514]()

---

## Use Cases for Flexible Docking

PINDER enables multiple docking scenarios by providing different structural starting points:

| Docking Scenario | Input Structures | Difficulty | Training Examples |
|-----------------|------------------|------------|-------------------|
| **Bound Docking** | Holo receptor + Holo ligand | Easiest | 2,456,152 in train |
| **Unbound Docking** | Apo receptor + Apo ligand | Hard | 136,498 pairs in train |
| **Predicted Docking** | Predicted receptor + Predicted ligand | Moderate-Hard | 566,171 pairs in train |
| **Mixed Docking** | Combinations (e.g., Holo + Apo) | Variable | 25,130,994 theoretical combinations |

The `PinderLoader` supports different **monomer selection strategies** to construct these scenarios:

- `monomer_priority="holo"`: Use bound structures only
- `monomer_priority="apo"`: Prefer unbound structures when available
- `monomer_priority="pred"`: Prefer predicted structures when available  
- `monomer_priority="random"`: Randomly select from available structure types
- `monomer_priority="random_mixed"`: Randomly mix structure types between receptor and ligand

These strategies are implemented in [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py]() and allow training methods that can handle conformational flexibility.

Sources: [README.md:14-18](), [README.md:266-282](), [README.md:444-462]()

---

## Dataset Download and Location

The dataset is automatically downloaded on first use when accessed through the Python API. Manual download is also supported through the `pinder_download` command-line tool.

The complete dataset requires approximately **700GB** of disk space unpacked:

| Component | Compressed Size | Unpacked Size |
|-----------|----------------|---------------|
| `pdbs.zip` | 144GB | 672GB |
| `test_set_pdbs.zip` | 149MB | 705MB |
| `mappings.zip` | 6.8GB | 25GB |
| `index.parquet` | N/A | ~100MB |
| `metadata.parquet` | N/A | ~200MB |

The dataset is hosted on Google Cloud Storage at `gs://pinder/2024-02/` and is accessed automatically by the Python API through authenticated requests. No manual GCS setup is required.

Sources: [README.md:122-208]()

---

## Key Features

PINDER provides several unique capabilities:

1. **Scale**: ~500x larger than previous datasets with 2.4M+ training pairs
2. **Flexibility**: First dataset with paired apo and predicted structures for flexible docking
3. **Quality**: Rigorous filtering, clustering, and deleaking ensures test set integrity
4. **Diversity**: 44,330 apo structures and 42,827 predicted structures provide conformational diversity
5. **Annotations**: 58 index fields and 45+ metadata fields for fine-grained data selection
6. **Integration**: Native PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric support with filtering and transforms
7. **Evaluation**: Complete evaluation harness with CAPRI metrics (DockQ, iRMS, LRMS, Fnat)
8. **Benchmarks**: Multiple test sets (XL/S/AF2) for comprehensive method comparison

For details on working with these features programmatically, see [Loading Your First System](#2.1) and [Working with Filters](#2.3).

Sources: [README.md:14-18](), [README.md:392-432](), [README.md:517-624]()

---

# Page: Installation

# Installation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)

</details>



This page provides comprehensive instructions for installing PINDER and its dependencies. PINDER consists of multiple packages that can be installed together or separately depending on your use case. For information about downloading the dataset itself, see [Dataset Structure](#1.3).

## System Requirements

PINDER requires Python 3.10 or higher. The package has been tested on the following platforms:

| Platform | Python Versions | Notes |
|----------|----------------|-------|
| Linux (glibc≥2.34) | 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 | Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9, etc. |
| macOS (≥10.12) | 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 | Pre-built wheels available |
| Windows | 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 | Pre-built wheels available |

Sources: [README.md:22-42]()

## Installation Workflow

```mermaid
graph TB
    Start["Start Installation"]
    CheckPlatform{"Platform needs<br/>rust toolchain?"}
    InstallRust["Install rust toolchain<br/>curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh"]
    CreateEnv["Create virtual/conda environment"]
    InstallCore["Install pinder<br/>pip install pinder"]
    InstallExtras{"Install optional<br/>dependencies?"}
    InstallEval["Install eval extras<br/>pip install pinder[eval]"]
    InstallAll["Install all extras<br/>pip install pinder[all]"]
    OptionalDeps{"Install additional<br/>optional deps?"}
    InstallCluster["Install torch-cluster"]
    InstallProdigy["Install PRODIGY-cryst"]
    Done["Installation Complete"]
    
    Start --> CheckPlatform
    CheckPlatform -->|"Linux glibc<2.34 or<br/>building from source"| InstallRust
    CheckPlatform -->|"Pre-built wheel<br/>available"| CreateEnv
    InstallRust --> CreateEnv
    CreateEnv --> InstallCore
    InstallCore --> InstallExtras
    InstallExtras -->|"Need eval package"| InstallEval
    InstallExtras -->|"Need all packages"| InstallAll
    InstallExtras -->|"Core only"| OptionalDeps
    InstallEval --> OptionalDeps
    InstallAll --> OptionalDeps
    OptionalDeps -->|"Need graph features"| InstallCluster
    OptionalDeps -->|"Need data generation"| InstallProdigy
    OptionalDeps -->|"No"| Done
    InstallCluster --> Done
    InstallProdigy --> Done
```

**Installation Flow Diagram**: Shows the decision tree for installing PINDER based on platform requirements and desired features.

Sources: [README.md:22-119]()

## Prerequisites

### fastpdb Dependency

PINDER uses `fastpdb` to accelerate PDB I/O operations. Pre-built wheels are available for most platforms, but some systems require building from source.

**Platforms with pre-built wheels:**
- Linux with `glibc>=2.34` (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9, etc.)
- macOS Sierra (10.12) or newer
- Windows

**Building from source:**

If your platform doesn't match these conditions, install the rust toolchain before installing PINDER:

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
```

Sources: [README.md:24-42]()

## Setting Up Environment

### Option 1: Using Conda/Mamba

```bash
mamba create --name pinder python=3.11
mamba activate pinder
```

You can substitute `conda` for `mamba` if preferred.

### Option 2: Using Python venv

```bash
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
```

Sources: [README.md:46-66]()

## Installing PINDER Packages

```mermaid

    AllExtra -.-> Prodigy
```

### Minimal Installation (pinder-core only)

For basic dataset loading and interaction:

```bash
pip install pinder
```

This installs the `pinder-core` package with minimal dependencies needed to use `PinderSystem`, `PinderLoader`, `Structure`, and basic data loading functionality.

### With Evaluation Package

To include the evaluation harness (`pinder-eval`):

```bash
pip install pinder[eval]
```

### All Extras

To install all optional packages:

```bash
pip install pinder[all]
```

Sources: [README.md:101-118]()

## Optional Dependencies

### torch-cluster

The `torch-cluster` package is required for certain graph-based features but is not automatically installed. Installation varies by platform:

**From wheel (Linux/Windows):**

```bash
pip install torch-cluster -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html
```

Replace `${TORCH}` with your PyTorch version (e.g., `2.0.0`) and `${CUDA}` with either `cpu`, `cu118`, or `cu121` depending on your CUDA installation.

**From source (all platforms):**

```bash
pip install torch  # Ensure PyTorch is installed first
pip install torch-cluster
```

**Note:** On Apple Silicon macOS machines, installation from source is required.

Sources: [README.md:70-91]()

### PRODIGY-cryst

PRODIGY-cryst is used in the data ingestion pipeline to predict interface biological relevance. It's an optional dependency of `pinder-data`:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/yusuf1759/prodigy-cryst.git
```

Sources: [README.md:93-99]()

## Development Installation

For contributing to PINDER or running tests:

### Clone the Repository

**Using HTTPS:**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder.git
cd pinder
```

**Using SSH:**
```bash
git clone git@github.com:pinder-org/pinder.git
cd pinder
```

### Install in Development Mode

```bash
mamba create --name pinder python=3.11
mamba activate pinder
pip install -e '.[dev]'
```

The `dev` extra includes:
- `lint`: ruff linter and pre-commit hooks
- `test`: pytest, tox, codecov
- `type`: mypy for type checking
- `leaderboard`: Tools for leaderboard generation
- `data`: Dependencies for dataset generation

### Install Pre-commit Hooks

```bash
pre-commit install
```

This ensures code passes linting before being committed.

Sources: [README.md:820-853]()

| `eval` | `pip install pinder[eval]` | Evaluation harness and metrics |
| `all` | `pip install pinder[all]` | All optional packages |
| `dev` | `pip install -e '.[dev]'` | Development tools (lint, test, type, leaderboard, data) |
| `lint` | `pip install pinder[lint]` | ruff==0.4.9, pre-commit==3.6.0 |
| `test` | `pip install pinder[test]` | tox>=4, pytest==7.2.0, pytest-cov==4.0.0 |

| `leaderboard` | `pip install pinder[leaderboard]` | Quarto, matplotlib, seaborn |

## Verification

After installation, verify that PINDER is correctly installed:

```python
import pinder
from pinder.core import PinderSystem, get_pinder_location

# Check installation location
print(get_pinder_location())

# Verify core functionality
print(f"PINDER version: {pinder.__version__}")
```

For a complete quick start guide on loading your first system, see [Loading Your First System](#2.1).

## Troubleshooting

### fastpdb Build Failures

If `fastpdb` fails to build on Linux systems:

1. Check glibc version: `ldd --version`
2. If glibc < 2.34, install rust toolchain as described in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)
3. Retry installation

### torch-cluster Installation Issues

On Apple Silicon macOS:
- Pre-built wheels are not available
- Ensure PyTorch is installed before attempting torch-cluster installation
- Build from source using: `pip install torch-cluster`

### Import Errors

If you encounter import errors:

1. Verify environment activation: `which python`
2. Check installed packages: `pip list | grep pinder`
3. Ensure dependencies are installed: `pip install --upgrade pinder[all]`

### Dataset Download Issues

For dataset download problems, see [Dataset Structure](#1.3) for detailed download instructions and troubleshooting.

Sources: [README.md:22-42](), [README.md:70-91]()

# Page: Dataset Structure

# Dataset Structure

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



This page describes the physical organization of the PINDER dataset on disk, including directory layout, file naming conventions, and storage requirements. For information about how to load and access this data programmatically, see [Loading Your First System](#2.1). For details on the dataset splits and benchmarks, see [Dataset Splits and Benchmarks](#1.4).

## Dataset Location

The PINDER dataset is stored in a version-specific directory determined by the following hierarchy:

1. `PINDER_BASE_DIR` environment variable (if set)
2. `$XDG_DATA_HOME/pinder` (typically `~/.local/share/pinder` on Mac and Linux)
3. Default fallback location

The complete path follows the pattern: `<base_dir>/<release_version>/`, where `<release_version>` is in `YYYY-MM` format (e.g., `2024-02`).

```mermaid
graph TB
    ENV["PINDER_BASE_DIR env var"]
    XDG["$XDG_DATA_HOME/pinder"]
    DEFAULT["Default location"]
    
    CHECK1{"PINDER_BASE_DIR<br/>set?"}
    CHECK2{"XDG_DATA_HOME<br/>set?"}
    
    BASE["Base Directory"]
    VERSION["/<release_version>/"]
    FINAL["Final Dataset Path"]
    
    ENV --> CHECK1
    CHECK1 -->|Yes| BASE
    CHECK1 -->|No| CHECK2
    CHECK2 -->|Yes| XDG
    CHECK2 -->|No| DEFAULT
    XDG --> BASE
    DEFAULT --> BASE
    
    BASE --> VERSION
    VERSION --> FINAL
```

**Diagram: Dataset location resolution logic**

The current location can be queried programmatically using `get_pinder_location()` from [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/utils/paths.py]().

Sources: [README.md:122-145]()

## Root Directory Structure

The dataset root contains five main components organized as follows:

```mermaid
graph TB
    ROOT["Dataset Root<br/>~/.local/share/pinder/2024-02/"]
    
    PDBS["pdbs/<br/>~672GB"]
    TEST_PDBS["test_set_pdbs/<br/>~705MB"]
    MAPPINGS["mappings/<br/>~25GB"]
    INDEX["index.parquet<br/>~50MB"]
    METADATA["metadata.parquet<br/>~100MB"]
    
    ROOT --> PDBS
    ROOT --> TEST_PDBS
    ROOT --> MAPPINGS
    ROOT --> INDEX
    ROOT --> METADATA
    
    PDBS_DESC["Individual monomer and<br/>ground-truth dimer PDBs"]
    TEST_DESC["Pre-transformed test<br/>set structures"]
    MAP_DESC["PDB↔UniProt mappings<br/>Assembly information"]
    IDX_DESC["Master index of<br/>2.4M+ entries"]
    META_DESC["Detailed metadata<br/>45+ annotation fields"]
    
    PDBS -.-> PDBS_DESC
    TEST_PDBS -.-> TEST_DESC
    MAPPINGS -.-> MAP_DESC
    INDEX -.-> IDX_DESC
    METADATA -.-> META_DESC
```

**Diagram: Root directory structure and component sizes**

Sources: [README.md:162-177](), [README.md:198-208]()

## Storage Requirements

| Component | Compressed | Unpacked | Description |
|-----------|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `pdbs.zip` | 144 GB | 672 GB | Structural data files |
| `test_set_pdbs.zip` | 149 MB | 705 MB | Test set structures |
| `mappings.zip` | 6.8 GB | 25 GB | Mapping files |
| `index.parquet` | - | ~50 MB | Master index |
| `metadata.parquet` | - | ~100 MB | Detailed annotations |
| **Total** | **~151 GB** | **~698 GB** | Complete dataset |

Sources: [README.md:198-208]()

## pdbs/ Directory

The `pdbs/` directory contains individual PDB files for monomers and native complexes. Files are organized by two-character PDB ID prefixes:

```mermaid
graph TB
    PDBS["pdbs/"]
    
    subgraph "Two-character prefix directories"
        DIR_1A["1a/"]
        DIR_1B["1b/"]
        DIR_XX["xx/"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structure types"
        NATIVE["Native complexes<br/>&lt;id&gt;.pdb"]
        HOLO_R["Holo receptors<br/>&lt;id&gt;-R.pdb"]
        HOLO_L["Holo ligands<br/>&lt;id&gt;-L.pdb"]
        APO["Apo monomers<br/>&lt;uniprot&gt;--&lt;pdb&gt;__&lt;chain&gt;.pdb"]
        PRED["Predicted monomers<br/>&lt;uniprot&gt;.pdb"]
    end
    
    PDBS --> DIR_1A
    PDBS --> DIR_1B
    PDBS --> DIR_XX
    
    DIR_1A --> NATIVE
    DIR_1A --> HOLO_R
    DIR_1A --> HOLO_L
    DIR_1A --> APO
    DIR_1A --> PRED
```

**Diagram: pdbs/ directory organization**

### File Naming Conventions

The `pdbs/` directory uses specific naming patterns for different structure types:

| Structure Type | Naming Pattern | Example | Chain ID |
|---------------|----------------|---------|----------|
| Native complex | `<pdb_id>.pdb` | `1a2k.pdb` | Multiple chains |
| Holo receptor | `<pdb_id>-R.pdb` | `1a2k-R.pdb` | R |
| Holo ligand | `<pdb_id>-L.pdb` | `1a2k-L.pdb` | L |
| Apo monomer | `<uniprot>--<pdb_id>__<chain>_<uniprot>.pdb` | `P12345--2xyz__A1_P12345.pdb` | A |
| Predicted monomer | `<uniprot>.pdb` | `P12345.pdb` | A |

**Note:** Apo and predicted monomers are stored with chain ID `A` to reduce duplication when the same structure maps to both receptor and ligand roles across multiple systems. The `PinderSystem` class automatically re-chains these to `R` or `L` as needed.

Sources: [README.md:173-176](), [README.md:404-405]()

## test_set_pdbs/ Directory

The `test_set_pdbs/` directory contains pre-rotated and pre-translated monomer structures for test sets, ready for immediate use in evaluation:

```mermaid
graph TB
    TEST_ROOT["test_set_pdbs/"]
    
    SPLIT_S["pinder_s/"]
    SPLIT_XL["pinder_xl/"]
    SPLIT_AF2["pinder_af2/"]
    
    TEST_ROOT --> SPLIT_S
    TEST_ROOT --> SPLIT_XL
    TEST_ROOT --> SPLIT_AF2
    
    subgraph "Per-system directories"
        SYS_DIR["&lt;system_id&gt;/"]
        HOLO_R["holo_receptor.pdb"]
        HOLO_L["holo_ligand.pdb"]
        APO_R["apo_receptor.pdb"]
        APO_L["apo_ligand.pdb"]
        PRED_R["predicted_receptor.pdb"]
        PRED_L["predicted_ligand.pdb"]
    end
    
    SPLIT_XL --> SYS_DIR
    SYS_DIR --> HOLO_R
    SYS_DIR --> HOLO_L
    SYS_DIR --> APO_R
    SYS_DIR --> APO_L
    SYS_DIR --> PRED_R
    SYS_DIR --> PRED_L
```

**Diagram: test_set_pdbs/ directory structure for benchmark evaluation**

Each test set subdirectory (`pinder_s/`, `pinder_xl/`, `pinder_af2/`) contains system-specific folders with all available structure variants pre-transformed for direct use.

Sources: [README.md:162-177](), [README.md:244-252]()

## mappings/ Directory

The `mappings/` directory stores alignment and mapping information between different coordinate systems and databases:

```mermaid
graph TB
    MAPPINGS["mappings/"]
    
    subgraph "Mapping types"
        UNIPROT_MAP["UniProt mappings<br/>PDB ↔ UniProt coordinates"]
        ASSEMBLY_MAP["Assembly information<br/>Original PDB assemblies"]
        CHAIN_MAP["Chain mappings<br/>Author chains ↔ Entity IDs"]
    end
    
    subgraph "File organization"
        PREFIX_DIR["&lt;two-char-prefix&gt;/"]
        SYSTEM_FILES["Mapping files per system"]
    end
    
    MAPPINGS --> UNIPROT_MAP
    MAPPINGS --> ASSEMBLY_MAP
    MAPPINGS --> CHAIN_MAP
    
    MAPPINGS --> PREFIX_DIR
    PREFIX_DIR --> SYSTEM_FILES
    
    UNIPROT_MAP -.->|"Used by"| RESIDUE_NUMBERING["Residue numbering<br/>alignment"]
    ASSEMBLY_MAP -.->|"Used by"| STRUCTURE_UTILS["Structure utilities<br/>and validation"]
```

**Diagram: mappings/ directory contents and usage**

These mappings enable:
- Conversion between PDB residue numbering and UniProt canonical sequences
- Tracking of biological assembly transformations
- Resolution of author chain IDs to structural entities

Sources: [README.md:173-176]()

## index.parquet File

The `index.parquet` file is the master index containing one row per PINDER entry. It defines which structures are available for each system and their dataset split assignment.

### Index Schema Overview

The index contains 58 fields organized into several categories:

```mermaid
graph LR
    INDEX["index.parquet"]
    
    subgraph "Core identification"
        ID_FIELDS["id<br/>pdb_id<br/>cluster_id"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Split assignment"
        SPLIT_FIELDS["split<br/>pinder_xl<br/>pinder_s<br/>pinder_af2"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structure availability"
        STRUCT_FIELDS["holo_R/L<br/>apo_R/L<br/>predicted_R/L"]
    end
    
    subgraph "File paths"
        PATH_FIELDS["holo_R_pdb<br/>apo_R_pdbs<br/>predicted_R_pdb"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Quality metrics"
        QUAL_FIELDS["apo_R_quality<br/>apo_L_quality<br/>chain1_neff<br/>chain2_neff"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Annotations"
        ANNOT_FIELDS["contains_antibody<br/>contains_antigen<br/>contains_enzyme"]
    end
    
    INDEX --> ID_FIELDS
    INDEX --> SPLIT_FIELDS
    INDEX --> STRUCT_FIELDS
    INDEX --> PATH_FIELDS
    INDEX --> QUAL_FIELDS
    INDEX --> ANNOT_FIELDS
```

**Diagram: index.parquet field categories**

### Key Index Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Unique system identifier: `<receptor_spec>--<ligand_spec>` |
| `pdb_id` | string | Source PDB entry identifier |
| `split` | string | Dataset split: `train`, `val`, `test`, `invalid` |
| `cluster_id` | string | Interface cluster identifier for redundancy control |
| `holo_R` / `holo_L` | boolean | Availability of holo receptor/ligand structures |
| `apo_R` / `apo_L` | boolean | Availability of apo receptor/ligand structures |
| `predicted_R` / `predicted_L` | boolean | Availability of AlphaFold2 predicted structures |
| `apo_R_pdbs` / `apo_L_pdbs` | string | Pipe-delimited list of alternate apo structure IDs |
| `apo_R_quality` / `apo_L_quality` | string | Apo pairing quality: `high`, `low`, or empty string |

The index is accessed via the `PinderLoader` class and `get_index()` function from [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/utils.py]().

Sources: [README.md:173-176](), [README.md:529-567]()

## metadata.parquet File

The `metadata.parquet` file provides detailed structural and biophysical annotations with 45+ fields per entry:

```mermaid
graph TB
    METADATA["metadata.parquet"]
    
    subgraph "Experimental details"
        EXP["method<br/>resolution<br/>date<br/>release_date"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structural properties"
        STRUCT["length1/2<br/>length_resolved_1/2<br/>number_of_components_1/2<br/>num_atom_types"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Interface characteristics"
        INTERFACE["buried_sasa<br/>intermolecular_contacts<br/>n_residue_pairs<br/>planarity<br/>link_density"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Contact types"
        CONTACTS["charged_charged_contacts<br/>charged_polar_contacts<br/>polar_polar_contacts<br/>apolar_apolar_contacts"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Quality indicators"
        QUALITY["interface_atom_gaps_4A/8A<br/>missing_interface_residues_4A/8A<br/>max_var_1/2"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Biological relevance"
        BIO["label<br/>probability<br/>complex_type<br/>oligomeric_count"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Domain annotations"
        DOMAIN["ECOD_names_R/L<br/>entity_id_R/L<br/>pdb_strand_id_R/L"]
    end
    
    METADATA --> EXP
    METADATA --> STRUCT
    METADATA --> INTERFACE
    METADATA --> CONTACTS
    METADATA --> QUALITY
    METADATA --> BIO
    METADATA --> DOMAIN
```

**Diagram: metadata.parquet field categories and relationships**

### Critical Metadata Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `resolution` | float | Experimental resolution in Ångströms |
| `method` | string | Structure determination method (X-RAY, CRYO-EM, NMR) |
| `label` | string | PRODIGY-cryst classification: biological vs crystal contact |
| `probability` | float | Probability of being a true biological complex |
| `buried_sasa` | float | Buried solvent-accessible surface area (Ų) |
| `intermolecular_contacts` | int | Number of inter-chain contacts (≤5Å cutoff) |
| `interface_atom_gaps_4A` | int | Interface atoms within 4Å of structural gaps |
| `num_atom_types` | int | Number of distinct atom types (detects CA-only structures) |
| `planarity` | float | Interface shape complementarity measure |

The metadata is accessed via `system.metadata` on any `PinderSystem` instance or directly through `get_metadata()` from [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/utils.py]().

Sources: [README.md:173-177](), [README.md:569-624]()

## Download and Synchronization

The dataset can be downloaded using command-line utilities:

| Command | Purpose | Options |
|---------|---------|---------|
| `pinder_download` | Download complete dataset | `--pinder_base_dir`, `--pinder_release`, `--skip_inflation` |
| `pinder_update_index` | Sync index/metadata only | `--pinder_base_dir`, `--pinder_release` |
| `pinder_sync_data` | Sync changed structure files | `--pinder_base_dir`, `--pinder_release` |

These utilities handle downloading from Google Cloud Storage (`gs://pinder` bucket) and automatic decompression.

# Page: Dataset Splits and Benchmarks

# Dataset Splits and Benchmarks

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



This page documents the PINDER dataset splits and benchmark test sets, including the clustering methodology, deleaking procedures, and quality filters used to create train/validation/test splits. For information about loading and filtering these splits programmatically, see [Data Loading System](#4).

## Overview

The PINDER dataset is organized into multiple splits designed for training and comprehensive evaluation of protein-protein docking methods. The dataset uses interface-based clustering via FoldSeek to create non-redundant splits and employs rigorous deleaking procedures to prevent information leakage between training and test sets.

All splits are stored in the `index.parquet` file with the following key fields: `split`, `pinder_xl`, `pinder_s`, and `pinder_af2` boolean flags.

## Dataset Splits Summary

| Split | # PDB IDs | # Clusters | # Total Pairs | # Holo Pairs | # Apo Pairs | # AF2 Pairs |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **PINDER-Train** | 62,706 | 42,220 | 2,456,152<sup>1</sup> | 1,560,682 | 136,498 | 566,171 |
| **PINDER-Val** | 1,958 | 1,958 | 1,958 | 1,958 | 342 | 1,789 |
| **PINDER-XL** | 1,955 | 1,955 | 1,955 | 1,955 | 342 | 1,747 |
| **PINDER-S** | 250 | 250 | 250 | 250 | 93 | 250 |
| **PINDER-AF2** | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 | 30 | 127 |

<sup>1</sup> Training size includes 274,194 pairs with at least one apo monomer and 621,276 pairs with at least one AF2 monomer. Theoretical size considering all monomer combinations is 25,130,994.

**Sources:** [README.md:244-283]()

## Split Organization Diagram

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "RCSB PDB Source"
        RCSB["RCSB PDB Database<br/>01.29.2024 snapshot<br/>~200K structures"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Clustering Pipeline"
        FOLDSEEK["FoldSeek Clustering<br/>Interface similarity<br/>>50% coverage threshold"]
        COMMUNITIES["Community Clustering<br/>Asynchronous label propagation<br/>42,220 + 1,958 + 1,955 clusters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Quality Filtering"
        PROTO_TEST["Proto-test Pool<br/>32,775 PPIs<br/>5,047 clusters"]
        TEST_FILTERS["Test Filters Applied<br/>Resolution ≤3.5Å<br/>Physiological contacts<br/>Dimers only"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Deleaking"
        TRANSITIVE["Transitive Neighbor Search<br/>Depth=2 in FoldSeek graph<br/>Removes leaky systems"]
        IALIGN["iAlign Deleaking<br/>For PINDER-AF2<br/>Against AF2MM training"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Final Splits"
        TRAIN["PINDER-Train<br/>42,220 clusters<br/>2.4M+ pairs"]
        VAL["PINDER-Val<br/>1,958 clusters<br/>Validation set"]
        XL["PINDER-XL<br/>1,955 clusters<br/>Full test set"]
        S["PINDER-S<br/>250 clusters<br/>Fast evaluation subset"]
        AF2["PINDER-AF2<br/>180 clusters<br/>AF2MM deleaked"]
    end
    
    RCSB --> FOLDSEEK
    FOLDSEEK --> COMMUNITIES
    COMMUNITIES --> TEST_FILTERS
    TEST_FILTERS --> PROTO_TEST
    PROTO_TEST --> TRANSITIVE
    TRANSITIVE --> XL
    TRANSITIVE --> VAL
    TRANSITIVE --> TRAIN
    XL --> S
    XL --> IALIGN
    IALIGN --> AF2
    
    style TRAIN fill:#f9f9f9
    style XL fill:#f9f9f9
    style S fill:#f9f9f9
    style AF2 fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [README.md:698-786]()

## Clustering Methodology

The PINDER clustering approach groups protein-protein interfaces by structural and sequence similarity using FoldSeek. This ensures that similar interfaces are kept together, enabling non-redundant sampling and rigorous train/test splits.

### Clustering Process

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input: PDB Chains"
        CHAINS["All PDB Chains<br/>≤10Å backbone distance<br/>defines interaction"]
    end
    
    subgraph "FoldSeek Alignment"
        FOLDSEEK_ALN["All-vs-all FoldSeek<br/>BLOSUM + 3Di matrices<br/>Structure + sequence similarity"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Graph Construction"
        CHAIN_GRAPH["Chain Graph<br/>Nodes: individual chains<br/>Edges: >50% interface coverage"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Community Detection"
        LABEL_PROP["Asynchronous Label Propagation<br/>Groups similar interfaces"]
        CHAIN_CLUSTERS["Chain-level Clusters<br/>c_a, c_b for each chain"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Interface Pairing"
        PAIRED_CLUSTERS["Paired Interface Clusters<br/>{c_a, c_b} tuples<br/>Unique cluster IDs"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Applications"
        SAMPLING["Non-redundant Sampling<br/>Diversity weighting"]
        TEST_SEL["Test/Val Selection<br/>Cluster representatives"]
        DELEAK["Deleaking<br/>Remove cluster neighbors"]
    end
    
    CHAINS --> FOLDSEEK_ALN
    FOLDSEEK_ALN --> CHAIN_GRAPH
    CHAIN_GRAPH --> LABEL_PROP
    LABEL_PROP --> CHAIN_CLUSTERS
    CHAIN_CLUSTERS --> PAIRED_CLUSTERS
    
    PAIRED_CLUSTERS --> SAMPLING
    PAIRED_CLUSTERS --> TEST_SEL
    PAIRED_CLUSTERS --> DELEAK
```

**Implementation Details:**

1. **Interface Definition**: Chains with any residues within 10Å backbone atom distance
2. **Alignment Coverage**: Edge added if >50% of interface residues covered by FoldSeek alignment
3. **Similarity Metrics**: FoldSeek uses both sequence (BLOSUM) and structure (3Di) matrices
4. **Cluster Assignment**: Each PPI assigned paired-interface cluster ID `{cluster_id_R, cluster_id_L}`

**Sources:** [README.md:732-744]()

## Test Set Quality Filters

Test and validation sets are filtered to ensure high-quality, biologically relevant protein complexes suitable for benchmarking.

### Filter Criteria Table

| Filter | Threshold | Purpose |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Contact Type | Physiological (PRODIGY-cryst) | Exclude crystal contacts |
| Oligomeric State | Dimers only | Ensure complete bioassembly |
| Experimental Method | X-RAY DIFFRACTION | Consistent structure quality |
| Resolution | ≤ 3.5Å | High structural accuracy |
| Chain Length | ≥ 40 residues | Exclude small peptides |
| Atom Types | ≥ 3 distinct elements | Exclude Cα-only structures |
| Interface Gaps (4Å) | = 0 atoms | Complete interface |
| Max Variance | ≤ 0.98 | Exclude elongated stacks |
| Components | Single component | Exclude detached domains |

**Proto-test Pool**: These filters produce 32,775 PPIs across 5,047 clusters, from which final test/validation sets are sampled.

**Sources:** [README.md:746-760]()

### Code Implementation

The filter criteria are implemented in the `PinderFilterBase` and `FilterMetadataFields` classes:

```python
# Example filter configuration
base_filters = [
    filters.FilterByMissingHolo(),
    filters.FilterSubByContacts(min_contacts=5, radius=10.0, calpha_only=True),
    filters.FilterByHoloElongation(max_var_contribution=0.92),
    filters.FilterDetachedHolo(radius=12, max_components=2),
    filters.FilterMetadataFields(
        resolution=('<=', 3.5),
        method=('==', 'X-RAY DIFFRACTION'),
    ),
]
```

**Sources:** [README.md:627-667](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/filters.py]()

## Deleaking Procedures

PINDER employs two deleaking strategies to prevent information leakage from training into test sets.

### Standard Deleaking (PINDER-XL, PINDER-Val)

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Cluster Selection"
        PROTO["Proto-test PPIs<br/>32,775 systems<br/>5,047 clusters"]
        SAMPLE["Sample 1 per cluster<br/>Rank by criteria"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transitive Neighbor Search"
        FOLDSEEK_GRAPH["FoldSeek Graph<br/>Interface similarity edges"]
        DEPTH2["Depth-2 Traversal<br/>Find transitive neighbors"]
        CHECK_CLUSTER["Check cluster IDs<br/>Different cluster = leak"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Classification"
        CLEAN["Clean Systems<br/>No transitive hits<br/>Eligible for test/val"]
        LEAKY["Leaky Systems<br/>Transitive hits found<br/>Assigned split='invalid'"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Final Selection"
        RANK["Ranking Criteria:<br/>1. Heterodimer preferred<br/>2. PINDER-AF2 eligible<br/>3. Apo availability<br/>4. AFDB availability"]
        ASSIGN["Assign to splits<br/>XL: 1,955<br/>Val: 1,958"]
    end
    
    PROTO --> SAMPLE
    SAMPLE --> FOLDSEEK_GRAPH
    FOLDSEEK_GRAPH --> DEPTH2
    DEPTH2 --> CHECK_CLUSTER
    CHECK_CLUSTER --> CLEAN
    CHECK_CLUSTER --> LEAKY
    CLEAN --> RANK
    RANK --> ASSIGN
```

**Sources:** [README.md:762-763]()

### AF2MM-Specific Deleaking (PINDER-AF2)

The PINDER-AF2 subset undergoes additional deleaking to ensure compatibility with AlphaFold2-Multimer evaluation:

1. **Time-based Filter**: Only structures released after 2021-10-01 (AF2MM cutoff date) are considered
2. **Initial Pool**: 675 clusters meeting the time criteria  
3. **iAlign Deleaking**: Remove systems with similar interfaces to AF2MM training set using iAlign structural alignment
4. **Final Set**: 180 clusters guaranteed structurally distinct from AF2MM 2.3 training data

**Sources:** [README.md:783-786]()

## PINDER-XL: Full Test Set

PINDER-XL is the primary benchmark containing 1,955 cluster representatives selected for maximum diversity and quality.

### Characteristics

- **Size**: 1,955 systems from 1,955 unique clusters
- **Structure Types**: All have holo pairs, 342 with apo pairs, 1,747 with AF2 predicted pairs
- **Quality**: All systems pass strict quality filters
- **Diversity**: One representative per cluster ensures interface diversity
- **Deleaking**: Depth-2 transitive neighbor removal

### Usage in Code

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

# Load PINDER-XL test set
xl_loader = PinderLoader(
    split="test",
    subset="pinder_xl"
)

for system in xl_loader:
    # system.entry.pinder_xl == True
    # system has native, holo_receptor, holo_ligand
    # may have apo_receptor, apo_ligand
    # may have pred_receptor, pred_ligand
    pass
```

**Sources:** [README.md:247-251]()

## PINDER-S: Fast Evaluation Subset

PINDER-S is a carefully curated 250-system subset of PINDER-XL designed for rapid method evaluation.

### Selection Criteria

- **Diversity Sampling**: 188 heterodimers, 62 homodimers
- **Annotation Coverage**: Diverse UniProt and PFAM annotations
- **Apo Structures**: 93 systems with paired apo structures (143 with at least one apo monomer)
- **AF2 Coverage**: All 250 systems have paired AFDB structures
- **Use Case**: Methods where full PINDER-XL evaluation is too computationally expensive

### Subset Composition

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "PINDER-XL 1,955 systems"
        XL_ALL["Full XL Set"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PINDER-S 250 systems"
        S_HETERO["Heterodimers<br/>188 systems"]
        S_HOMO["Homodimers<br/>62 systems"]
        S_APO["With Apo Pairs<br/>93 systems"]
        S_AF2["With AF2 Pairs<br/>250 systems"]
    end
    
    XL_ALL --> S_HETERO
    XL_ALL --> S_HOMO
    S_HETERO --> S_APO
    S_HOMO --> S_APO
    S_HETERO --> S_AF2
    S_HOMO --> S_AF2
```

### Usage in Code

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

# Load PINDER-S subset
s_loader = PinderLoader(
    split="test",
    subset="pinder_s"
)

# All systems have system.entry.pinder_s == True
print(f"PINDER-S size: {len(s_loader)}")  # 250
```

**Sources:** [README.md:250-251](), [README.md:781]()

## PINDER-AF2: AlphaFold2-Deleaked Test Set

PINDER-AF2 contains 180 systems rigorously deleaked against the AlphaFold2-Multimer training set.

### Deleaking Strategy

1. **Time Filter**: Structures released after 2021-10-01
2. **Structural Deleaking**: iAlign used to detect similar interfaces
3. **Training Set**: Deleaked against AF2MM 2.3 training data
4. **Guarantee**: No structural similarity to AF2MM training examples

### Test Set Characteristics

- **Size**: 180 systems from 180 clusters
- **Apo Pairs**: 30 systems with paired apo structures
- **AF2 Pairs**: 127 systems with paired AFDB structures
- **Primary Use**: Fair comparison with AlphaFold2-Multimer and methods trained on AF2 data

### Time-split vs Structure-deleaked

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Post-AF2MM Clusters"
        POST_CUTOFF["675 Clusters<br/>Released after 2021-10-01"]
    end
    
    subgraph "iAlign Deleaking"
        IALIGN_CHECK["Compare to AF2MM training<br/>iAlign structural similarity"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Classification"
        AF2_SET["PINDER-AF2<br/>180 clusters<br/>Structurally distinct"]
        TIME_ONLY["Time-split Only<br/>495 clusters<br/>Not in PINDER-AF2<br/>May have structural similarity"]
    end
    
    POST_CUTOFF --> IALIGN_CHECK
    IALIGN_CHECK --> AF2_SET
    IALIGN_CHECK --> TIME_ONLY
```

### Usage in Code

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

# Load PINDER-AF2 for AF2MM comparison
af2_loader = PinderLoader(
    split="test",
    subset="pinder_af2"
)

for system in af2_loader:
    assert system.entry.pinder_af2 == True
    # Guaranteed no AF2MM training leakage
```

**Sources:** [README.md:251](), [README.md:783-786]()

## PINDER-Val: Validation Set

The validation set provides 1,958 systems for monitoring training performance.

### Design Principles

- **Size**: 1,958 systems from 1,958 clusters (one per cluster)
- **Distribution**: Identical preparation and quality filters as test set
- **Apo Structures**: 342 systems with paired apo structures  
- **AF2 Structures**: 1,789 systems with paired AFDB structures
- **Purpose**: Representative validation during training

### Usage in Code

```python
from pinder.core import PinderDataset

# Create validation dataset
val_dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="val",
    monomer_priority="holo"
)

# Use with PyTorch DataLoader
from pinder.core import get_torch_loader
val_loader = get_torch_loader(val_dataset, batch_size=4, shuffle=False)
```

**Sources:** [README.md:257-261](), [README.md:388]()

## PINDER-Train: Training Set

The training set provides extensive protein-protein interaction examples for model training.

### Scale and Composition

| Metric | Count |
|:---|---:|
| Total Clusters | 42,220 |
| Unique PDB IDs | 62,706 |
| Holo Pairs | 1,560,682 |
| Pairs with ≥1 Apo Monomer | 274,194 |
| Pairs with ≥1 AF2 Monomer | 621,276 |
| Paired Apo Structures | 136,498 |
| Paired AF2 Structures | 566,171 |
| **Total Training Pairs** | **2,456,152** |
| **Theoretical Max Combinations** | **25,130,994** |

### Structure Type Availability

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Training Set Components"
        HOLO["Holo Structures<br/>1,560,682 pairs<br/>All have holo monomers"]
        APO["Apo Structures<br/>44,330 unique<br/>41,630 receptor<br/>36,910 ligand"]
        AF2["AFDB Structures<br/>42,827 unique<br/>37,095 receptor<br/>38,801 ligand"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Combinations"
        HOLO_ONLY["Holo-Holo Pairs<br/>Base training pairs"]
        HOLO_APO["Holo + Apo Pairs<br/>274,194 with ≥1 apo"]
        HOLO_AF2["Holo + AF2 Pairs<br/>621,276 with ≥1 AF2"]
        APO_APO["Apo-Apo Pairs<br/>136,498 paired apo"]
        AF2_AF2["AF2-AF2 Pairs<br/>566,171 paired AF2"]
        MIXED["Mixed Combinations<br/>Holo-Apo-AF2<br/>Up to 25M combinations"]
    end
    
    HOLO --> HOLO_ONLY
    APO --> HOLO_APO
    AF2 --> HOLO_AF2
    APO --> APO_APO
    AF2 --> AF2_AF2
    HOLO --> MIXED
    APO --> MIXED
    AF2 --> MIXED
```

### Diversity Sampling

The training set uses cluster IDs for non-redundant sampling:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

# Load training set with diversity sampling
train_loader = PinderLoader(
    split="train",
    # Sample inversely proportional to cluster size
    sample_by_cluster=True,
    monomer_priority="random_mixed"  # Mix holo/apo/pred
)

# Each iteration samples different monomer combinations
for system in train_loader:
    # system.entry.cluster_id used for weighting
    # Ensures diverse interface coverage
    pass
```

**Sources:** [README.md:264-282](), [README.md:383-389](), [README.md:773-779]()

## Monomer Structure Types Across Splits

All splits provide multiple structure types for flexible docking evaluation.

### Structure Type Mapping

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Native Complex"
        NATIVE["native.pdb<br/>Ground truth<br/>Chains R+L"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Holo Monomers"
        HOLO_R["holo_receptor.pdb<br/>Bound state<br/>Chain R"]
        HOLO_L["holo_ligand.pdb<br/>Bound state<br/>Chain L"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Apo Monomers"
        APO_R["apo_receptor.pdb<br/>Unbound state<br/>Chain A"]
        APO_L["apo_ligand.pdb<br/>Unbound state<br/>Chain A"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Predicted Monomers"
        PRED_R["pred_receptor.pdb<br/>AlphaFold2<br/>Chain A"]
        PRED_L["pred_ligand.pdb<br/>AlphaFold2<br/>Chain A"]
    end
    
    NATIVE --> HOLO_R
    NATIVE --> HOLO_L
    HOLO_R -.->|"Aligned via<br/>UniProt"| APO_R
    HOLO_L -.->|"Aligned via<br/>UniProt"| APO_L
    HOLO_R -.->|"Aligned via<br/>UniProt"| PRED_R
    HOLO_L -.->|"Aligned via<br/>UniProt"| PRED_L
```

### Availability by Split

| Split | Holo Receptor | Holo Ligand | Apo Receptor | Apo Ligand | Pred Receptor | Pred Ligand |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Train | 100% | 100% | 17.5% | 15.8% | 39.8% | 36.2% |
| Val | 100% | 100% | 17.5% | 17.5% | 91.3% | 91.3% |
| PINDER-XL | 100% | 100% | 17.5% | 17.5% | 89.4% | 89.4% |
| PINDER-S | 100% | 100% | 37.2% | 37.2% | 100% | 100% |
| PINDER-AF2 | 100% | 100% | 16.7% | 16.7% | 70.6% | 70.6% |

**Note**: Apo and predicted monomers use chain ID 'A' in PDB files to avoid duplication across systems. When accessed via `PinderSystem`, chains are automatically renamed to 'R' or 'L' as appropriate.

**Sources:** [README.md:398-406]()

## Accessing Splits in Code

### Using Index Flags

The `index.parquet` file contains boolean flags for split membership:

```python
import pandas as pd
from pinder.core import get_index

# Load index with split information
index = get_index()

# Filter by split
train_df = index[index['split'] == 'train']
test_xl_df = index[index['pinder_xl'] == True]
test_s_df = index[index['pinder_s'] == True]
test_af2_df = index[index['pinder_af2'] == True]

# Count systems per split
print(f"Train: {len(train_df)}")          # 2,456,152
print(f"Val: {len(index[index['split'] == 'val'])}")  # 1,958
print(f"PINDER-XL: {len(test_xl_df)}")    # 1,955
print(f"PINDER-S: {len(test_s_df)}")      # 250
print(f"PINDER-AF2: {len(test_af2_df)}")  # 180
```

### Using PinderLoader

The `PinderLoader` provides a high-level interface for iterating over splits:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

# Load specific split and subset
loader = PinderLoader(
    split="test",           # 'train', 'val', 'test'
    subset="pinder_xl"      # 'pinder_xl', 'pinder_s', 'pinder_af2', None
)

# Access split information from each system
for system in loader:
    entry = system.entry
    print(f"System ID: {entry.id}")
    print(f"Split: {entry.split}")
    print(f"In XL: {entry.pinder_xl}")
    print(f"In S: {entry.pinder_s}")
    print(f"In AF2: {entry.pinder_af2}")
    print(f"Cluster: {entry.cluster_id}")
```

### Using PinderDataset for Training

```python
from pinder.core import PinderDataset, get_torch_loader

# Training dataset
train_dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    monomer_priority="random_mixed",  # Mix holo/apo/pred
    limit_by=10000  # Optionally limit size
)

# Validation dataset
val_dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="val",
    monomer_priority="holo"  # Use only holo for validation
)

# Test dataset
test_dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="test",
    subset="pinder_s",  # Use fast subset
    monomer_priority="apo"  # Evaluate on apo structures
)

# Create dataloaders
train_loader = get_torch_loader(train_dataset, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
val_loader = get_torch_loader(val_dataset, batch_size=32, shuffle=False)
test_loader = get_torch_loader(test_dataset, batch_size=1, shuffle=False)
```

**Sources:** [README.md:443-463](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py]()

## IndexEntry Fields for Splits

The `IndexEntry` class defines the schema for split-related fields in the index:

| Field | Type | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `split` | string | Split assignment: 'train', 'val', 'test', or 'invalid' |
| `cluster_id` | string | Paired-interface cluster identifier |
| `cluster_id_R` | string | Receptor chain cluster identifier |
| `cluster_id_L` | string | Ligand chain cluster identifier |
| `pinder_xl` | boolean | Member of PINDER-XL test set |
| `pinder_s` | boolean | Member of PINDER-S subset |
| `pinder_af2` | boolean | Member of PINDER-AF2 subset |

**Sources:** [README.md:529-567](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/utils.py]()

## Split Versioning and Updates

Dataset splits are versioned independently from the codebase using `YYYY-MM` format.

### Update Types

**Minor Updates** (do not invalidate leaderboard):
- Index field corrections
- Metadata additions
- Structure additions to training set only
- No re-clustering required

**Major Updates** (invalidate leaderboard):
- Re-clustering with new threshold parameters
- Test/validation set changes
- Deleaking procedure modifications
- Require method re-evaluation

### Current Version

- **Release**: `2024-02`
- **Snapshot Date**: 2024-01-29
- **Location**: `gs://pinder/2024-02/`

### Checking Dataset Version

```python
from pinder.core import get_pinder_location

# Returns path including version
location = get_pinder_location()
print(location)  # ~/.local/share/pinder/2024-02
```

**Sources:** [README.md:788-801](), [README.md:142-144]()

# Page: Quick Start Guide

# Quick Start Guide

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb](examples/pinder-loader.ipynb)
- [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb](examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb)

</details>



This guide provides hands-on tutorials for new users to quickly start working with PINDER data. It walks through the essential workflow from loading your first protein system to creating production-ready dataloaders for machine learning.

This guide covers basic data access patterns and loader setup. For comprehensive coverage of specific topics, see:
- For detailed system structure and properties, see [PinderSystem](#3.1)
- For advanced filtering strategies, see [Filtering System](#4.4)
- For data generation pipeline details, see [Dataset Generation Pipeline](#5)
- For MLSB challenge-specific requirements, see [MLSB Challenge Tutorial](#2.4)

## Overview of the Quick Start Workflow

The typical workflow for working with PINDER involves five main steps, progressing from raw data access to ML-ready batches:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Install["Install pinder package<br/>pip install pinder"]
    Download["Download dataset<br/>~700GB total"]
    Index["Load index with get_index()<br/>Filter by split='train'"]
    System["Create PinderSystem objects<br/>Access structures"]
    Loader["Configure PinderLoader<br/>Apply filters & transforms"]
    Dataset["Wrap in PinderDataset<br/>Convert to tensors"]
    DataLoader["Create torch.DataLoader<br/>Batch & iterate"]
    
    Install --> Download
    Download --> Index
    Index --> System
    System --> Loader
    Loader --> Dataset
    Dataset --> DataLoader
    
    style Index fill:#f9f9f9
    style System fill:#f9f9f9
    style Loader fill:#f9f9f9
    style Dataset fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Workflow: From Installation to Training-Ready Batches**

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:105-118]()

## Key Components and Their Relationships

The PINDER API is organized around three layers of abstraction, each building on the previous:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Data Access Layer"
        IndexEntry["IndexEntry<br/>pinder.core.index.utils<br/>Pydantic model with 58 fields"]
        Structure["Structure<br/>pinder.core.loader.structure<br/>Wraps biotite.AtomArray"]
        PinderSystem["PinderSystem<br/>pinder.core.index.system<br/>Manages all structure variants"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Iteration Layer"
        PinderLoader["PinderLoader<br/>pinder.core.loader<br/>Iterator with filtering"]
        BaseFilters["base_filters<br/>System-level checks"]
        SubFilters["sub_filters<br/>Monomer-level checks"]
        StructFilters["structure_transforms<br/>Atom-level operations"]
    end
    
    subgraph "ML Integration Layer"
        PinderDataset["PinderDataset<br/>torch.utils.data.Dataset<br/>Returns dict of tensors"]
        PPIDataset["PPIDataset<br/>torch_geometric.data.Dataset<br/>Returns HeteroData"]
        TorchLoader["torch.DataLoader<br/>Batching & collation"]
    end
    
    IndexEntry -->|"validates row"| PinderSystem
    PinderSystem -->|"contains"| Structure
    Structure -->|"wraps"| AtomArray["biotite.structure.AtomArray"]
    
    PinderLoader -->|"yields"| PinderSystem
    PinderLoader -->|"yields"| Structure
    BaseFilters -->|"applied by"| PinderLoader
    SubFilters -->|"applied by"| PinderLoader
    StructFilters -->|"applied by"| PinderLoader
    
    PinderLoader -->|"powers"| PinderDataset
    PinderLoader -->|"powers"| PPIDataset
    PinderDataset -->|"feeds"| TorchLoader
    PPIDataset -->|"feeds"| TorchLoader
    
    style PinderSystem fill:#f9f9f9
    style PinderLoader fill:#f9f9f9
    style PinderDataset fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Architecture: Three-Layer API Design**

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:876-922](), [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:1036-1071]()

## Essential Code Patterns

### Loading the Index and Filtering by Split

The index is the entry point to all PINDER data. It contains metadata for all systems and their available structure types:

```python
from pinder.core import get_index

# Load the full index (2.4M+ entries)
index = get_index()

# Filter to training split only
train = index.query('split == "train"').reset_index(drop=True)
val = index.query('split == "val"').reset_index(drop=True)

# Check what structure types are available
systems_with_apo = train.query('apo_R and apo_L')
systems_with_pred = train.query('predicted_R and predicted_L')
```

The index provides boolean columns (`holo_R`, `holo_L`, `apo_R`, `apo_L`, `predicted_R`, `predicted_L`) that indicate which structure types are available for each system.

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:134-197]()

### Creating a PinderSystem

A `PinderSystem` object provides access to all structural variants of a protein complex:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderSystem

# Load a system by ID
system = PinderSystem("8phr__X4_UNDEFINED--8phr__W4_UNDEFINED")

# Access different structure types
native = system.native              # Ground-truth complex
holo_receptor = system.holo_receptor    # Receptor from complex
holo_ligand = system.holo_ligand       # Ligand from complex
apo_receptor = system.apo_receptor     # Unbound receptor (may be None)
apo_ligand = system.apo_ligand         # Unbound ligand (may be None)
pred_receptor = system.pred_receptor   # AF2 prediction (may be None)
pred_ligand = system.pred_ligand       # AF2 prediction (may be None)
```

Each of these properties returns a `Structure` object (or `None` if unavailable), which provides access to coordinates, sequences, and atomic properties.

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:518-707](), [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:736-773]()

### Working with Structure Objects

The `Structure` class wraps biotite's `AtomArray` with convenient property accessors:

```python
# Access atomic properties
coords = holo_receptor.coords           # numpy array of xyz coordinates
sequence = holo_receptor.sequence       # amino acid sequence string
fasta = holo_receptor.fasta            # FASTA format with header
atom_array = holo_receptor.atom_array  # biotite.AtomArray

# Filter structures by chain
receptor = native.filter("chain_id", ["R"])
ligand = native.filter("chain_id", ["L"])

# Write to PDB file
receptor.to_pdb("receptor.pdb")
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:391-473](), [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:779-869]()

## Creating Training-Ready DataLoaders

The most common use case is creating a PyTorch DataLoader for model training. The following diagram shows the data flow:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Index["index.parquet<br/>Filter by split"]
    Loader["PinderLoader<br/>base_filters<br/>sub_filters<br/>monomer_priority"]
    Dataset["PinderDataset<br/>structure_transforms<br/>transform/target_transform"]
    TorchDL["torch.DataLoader<br/>batch_size<br/>collate_fn"]
    Batch["Batch dict<br/>target_complex<br/>feature_complex<br/>id"]
    
    Index -->|"system IDs"| Loader
    Loader -->|"yields (system, feature, target)"| Dataset
    Dataset -->|"returns dict of tensors"| TorchDL
    TorchDL -->|"batched tensors"| Batch
    
    style Loader fill:#f9f9f9
    style Dataset fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Data Flow: From Index to Batched Tensors**

### Quick Start with Defaults

The simplest way to get started:

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PinderDataset, get_torch_loader

# Create dataset with defaults (holo monomers only)
train_dataset = PinderDataset(split="train")
val_dataset = PinderDataset(split="val")

# Wrap in DataLoader
train_loader = get_torch_loader(train_dataset, batch_size=2, shuffle=True)
val_loader = get_torch_loader(val_dataset, batch_size=2)

# Iterate over batches
for batch in train_loader:
    target = batch["target_complex"]["atom_coordinates"]  # Shape: (B, N, 3)
    feature = batch["feature_complex"]["atom_coordinates"]
    # ... train model
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:112-115]()

### With Filters and Transforms

For production use, apply quality filters and data augmentation:

```python
from pinder.core.loader import filters, transforms
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PinderDataset

# Define system-level filters
base_filters = [
    filters.FilterDetachedHolo(radius=12, max_components=2),
    filters.FilterByResidueCount(min_residue_count=10, max_residue_count=2000),
]

# Define monomer-level filters
sub_filters = [
    filters.FilterSubByAtomTypes(min_atom_types=4),
    filters.FilterByHoloSeqIdentity(min_sequence_identity=0.8),
]

# Define structure transformations
target_transforms = [
    transforms.SelectAtomTypes(atom_types=["CA", "N", "C", "O"]),
]

feature_transforms = [
    transforms.SelectAtomTypes(atom_types=["CA", "N", "C", "O"]),
    transforms.RandomLigandTransform(max_translation=10.0),
]

# Create dataset with all configurations
train_dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    monomer_priority="random_mixed",  # Sample from holo/apo/pred
    base_filters=base_filters,
    sub_filters=sub_filters,
    structure_transforms_target=target_transforms,
    structure_transforms_feature=feature_transforms,
)
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:1036-1071]()

## Understanding Batch Structure

Each batch returned by `PinderDataset` contains:

| Key | Type | Description |
|-----|------|-------------|
| `target_complex` | `dict` | Ground-truth structure properties as tensors |
| `feature_complex` | `dict` | Input structure properties as tensors |
| `id` | `str` or `list[str]` | System ID(s) |
| `target_id` | `str` or `list[str]` | Monomer IDs used in target |
| `sample_id` | `str` or `list[str]` | Monomer IDs used in feature |

Each `*_complex` dictionary contains:

| Key | Shape | Description |
|-----|-------|-------------|
| `atom_coordinates` | `(batch, atoms, 3)` | XYZ coordinates |
| `atom_types` | `(batch, atoms, 1)` | Atom type indices |
| `element_types` | `(batch, atoms, 1)` | Element type indices |
| `residue_types` | `(batch, atoms, 1)` | Residue type indices |
| `residue_coordinates` | `(batch, residues, 3)` | Per-residue coordinates |
| `residue_ids` | `(batch, atoms)` | Residue numbering |
| `chain_ids` | `(batch, atoms)` | Chain identifiers |

Padding values of `-100.0` (coordinates) and `-1` (indices) are used for variable-length sequences in batches.

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:1074-1099](), [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:1838-1887]()

## Monomer Selection Strategies

The `monomer_priority` parameter controls which structure types are selected as input features:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Priority["monomer_priority parameter"]
    
    Holo["holo<br/>Always use holo monomers<br/>Skip if unavailable"]
    Apo["apo<br/>Always use apo monomers<br/>Skip if unavailable"]
    Pred["pred<br/>Always use predicted monomers<br/>Skip if unavailable"]
    Random["random<br/>Pick one type available in both R and L<br/>Same type for R and L"]
    Mixed["random_mixed<br/>Pick independently for R and L<br/>Different types allowed"]
    
    Priority --> Holo
    Priority --> Apo
    Priority --> Pred
    Priority --> Random
    Priority --> Mixed
    
    style Random fill:#f9f9f9
    style Mixed fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Monomer Selection Strategies**

The `random_mixed` strategy is recommended for training to expose models to all structure types:

```python
train_dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    monomer_priority="random_mixed",  # Maximum diversity
)
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:931-945]()

## File Path-Based Access

For custom workflows that don't use `PinderLoader`, you can directly construct file paths from the index:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from pinder.core import get_pinder_location
from pinder.core.loader.structure import Structure

# Get base directory
pinder_dir = get_pinder_location()  # ~/.local/share/pinder/2024-02/

# Construct paths from index row
row = train.sample(1).squeeze()
native_path = pinder_dir / "pdbs" / f"{row.id}.pdb"
holo_R_path = pinder_dir / "pdbs" / row.holo_R_pdb
holo_L_path = pinder_dir / "pdbs" / row.holo_L_pdb

# Load structures directly
receptor = Structure(holo_R_path)
coords = receptor.coords
sequence = receptor.sequence
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-mlsb.ipynb:204-350]()
