# Page: Index and Metadata

# Index and Metadata

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py)

</details>



This page documents the `IndexEntry` and `MetadataEntry` data schemas that form the annotation layer of the PINDER dataset. These schemas define the 58 primary fields in `index.parquet` and 45+ detailed fields in `metadata.parquet`, providing comprehensive structural and biological annotations for each protein-protein interaction system.

For information about how these entries are used within the data loading pipeline, see [PinderLoader](#4.1). For details on the actual protein structures represented by these entries, see [PinderSystem](#3.1).

## Overview

The PINDER dataset maintains two complementary annotation files:

- **index.parquet**: Contains the master index with essential metadata for all 2.4M+ training pairs and test systems
- **metadata.parquet**: Provides detailed structural and biophysical properties for each system

These files are the foundation of the dataset filtering and sampling system, exposing annotations through the `IndexEntry` and `MetadataEntry` dataclasses.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Dataset Files"
        INDEX_FILE["index.parquet<br/>2.4M+ rows"]
        META_FILE["metadata.parquet<br/>Detailed annotations"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Schema Classes"
        INDEX_ENTRY["IndexEntry<br/>58 fields<br/>Primary annotations"]
        META_ENTRY["MetadataEntry<br/>45+ fields<br/>Structural properties"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Access Functions"
        GET_INDEX["get_index()<br/>Returns DataFrame"]
        GET_META["get_metadata()<br/>Returns DataFrame"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Usage in Code"
        PINDER_SYS["PinderSystem<br/>.entry property<br/>.metadata property"]
        FILTERS["Filter classes<br/>FilterMetadataFields<br/>Query annotations"]
    end
    
    INDEX_FILE --> GET_INDEX
    META_FILE --> GET_META
    
    GET_INDEX --> INDEX_ENTRY
    GET_META --> META_ENTRY
    
    INDEX_ENTRY --> PINDER_SYS
    META_ENTRY --> PINDER_SYS
    
    INDEX_ENTRY --> FILTERS
    META_ENTRY --> FILTERS
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:1-26](), [README.md:163-176]()

## Data Structure Relationship

The index and metadata files maintain a one-to-one relationship through the shared `id` field, which uniquely identifies each protein-protein interaction system.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "IndexEntry Primary Keys"
        ID["id<br/>e.g. '1an1__A1_P00761--1an1__B1_P80424'"]
        PDB_ID["pdb_id<br/>e.g. '1an1'"]
        CLUSTER["cluster_id<br/>Interface cluster ID"]
    end
    
    subgraph "IndexEntry Structure Flags"
        HOLO_R["holo_R: bool"]
        HOLO_L["holo_L: bool"]
        APO_R["apo_R: bool"]
        APO_L["apo_L: bool"]
        PRED_R["predicted_R: bool"]
        PRED_L["predicted_L: bool"]
    end
    
    subgraph "IndexEntry File References"
        HOLO_R_PDB["holo_R_pdb: str"]
        HOLO_L_PDB["holo_L_pdb: str"]
        APO_R_PDB["apo_R_pdb: str"]
        APO_L_PDB["apo_L_pdb: str"]
        PRED_R_PDB["predicted_R_pdb: str"]
        PRED_L_PDB["predicted_L_pdb: str"]
    end
    
    ID -.->|"Links to"| META_ID["MetadataEntry.id<br/>Same system ID"]
    
    HOLO_R --> HOLO_R_PDB
    APO_R --> APO_R_PDB
    PRED_R --> PRED_R_PDB
```

**Sources:** [README.md:529-567](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:110-161]()

## IndexEntry Schema

The `IndexEntry` dataclass contains 58 fields organized into several functional categories. Each row in `index.parquet` represents a single protein-protein interaction system with its associated structural variants and annotations.

### Primary Identifiers

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `id` | string | Unique identifier following format `<pdb_id>__<chain_R>_<uniprot_R>--<pdb_id>__<chain_L>_<uniprot_L>` |
| `pdb_id` | string | PDB identifier for the entry |
| `cluster_id` | string | Interface cluster identifier from FoldSeek clustering |
| `cluster_id_R` | string | Cluster ID for receptor dimer body |
| `cluster_id_L` | string | Cluster ID for ligand dimer body |

### Split Assignments

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `split` | string | Dataset split: 'train', 'val', 'test', or 'invalid' |
| `pinder_s` | boolean | True if system is in PINDER-S test subset (250 diverse systems) |
| `pinder_xl` | boolean | True if system is in PINDER-XL test set (1,955 systems) |
| `pinder_af2` | boolean | True if system is in PINDER-AF2 test set (180 AF2MM-deleaked systems) |

### UniProt Identifiers

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `uniprot_R` | string | UniProt accession for receptor protein |
| `uniprot_L` | string | UniProt accession for ligand protein |

### Structure Availability Flags

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `holo_R` | boolean | True if holo (bound) receptor structure is available |
| `holo_L` | boolean | True if holo (bound) ligand structure is available |
| `apo_R` | boolean | True if apo (unbound) receptor structure is available |
| `apo_L` | boolean | True if apo (unbound) ligand structure is available |
| `predicted_R` | boolean | True if predicted receptor structure (AlphaFold2) is available |
| `predicted_L` | boolean | True if predicted ligand structure (AlphaFold2) is available |

### Structure File References

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `holo_R_pdb` | string | Filename for holo receptor PDB |
| `holo_L_pdb` | string | Filename for holo ligand PDB |
| `apo_R_pdb` | string | Filename for canonical apo receptor PDB |
| `apo_L_pdb` | string | Filename for canonical apo ligand PDB |
| `predicted_R_pdb` | string | Filename for predicted receptor PDB |
| `predicted_L_pdb` | string | Filename for predicted ligand PDB |
| `apo_R_pdbs` | string | Comma-delimited list of all alternative apo receptor PDBs |
| `apo_L_pdbs` | string | Comma-delimited list of all alternative apo ligand PDBs |

### Apo Pairing Quality

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `apo_R_quality` | string | Classification: 'high', 'low', or '' (empty). Test/val are 'high', train split includes both based on pairing confidence |
| `apo_L_quality` | string | Classification: 'high', 'low', or '' (empty). Test/val are 'high', train split includes both based on pairing confidence |

### Evolutionary Information

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `chain1_neff` | number | Effective number of sequences (Neff) for first chain, indicating MSA depth |
| `chain2_neff` | number | Effective number of sequences (Neff) for second chain, indicating MSA depth |

### Chain Identifiers

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `chain_R` | string | Chain identifier for receptor in native structure |
| `chain_L` | string | Chain identifier for ligand in native structure |

### Biological Annotations

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `contains_antibody` | boolean | True if complex contains antibody (from SAbDab annotation) |
| `contains_antigen` | boolean | True if complex contains antigen (from SAbDab annotation) |
| `contains_enzyme` | boolean | True if complex contains enzyme (from EC number annotation) |

**Sources:** [README.md:529-567](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:132-133]()

## MetadataEntry Schema

The `MetadataEntry` dataclass contains 45+ fields providing detailed structural and biophysical properties for each system. This data is derived from RCSB PDB annotations, PRODIGY-cryst predictions, and computational analyses.

### Core Identifiers

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `id` | string | Unique PINDER system identifier (matches IndexEntry.id) |
| `entry_id` | string | RCSB PDB entry identifier |
| `chain1_id` | string | Receptor chain ID (always 'R' in processed structures) |
| `chain2_id` | string | Ligand chain ID (always 'L' in processed structures) |

### Experimental Details

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `method` | string | Structure determination method (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, CRYO-EM, NMR, etc.) |
| `date` | string | Deposition date in RCSB PDB |
| `release_date` | string | Initial public release date |
| `resolution` | number | Experimental resolution in Ångströms |

### Biological Assembly

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `assembly` | integer | Bioassembly number (1, 2, 3, etc.) used to derive structure |
| `assembly_details` | string | Source of bioassembly information (author-defined vs other) |
| `oligomeric_details` | string | Description of oligomeric state |
| `oligomeric_count` | integer | Number of chains in the oligomer |
| `biol_details` | string | Biological assembly details |
| `complex_type` | string | 'homomer' or 'heteromer' |

### Chain Mapping

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `chain_1` | string | Post-bioassembly chain ID for receptor |
| `asym_id_1` | string | Author chain ID (original asymmetric unit) for receptor |
| `chain_2` | string | Post-bioassembly chain ID for ligand |
| `asym_id_2` | string | Author chain ID (original asymmetric unit) for ligand |

### Sequence Properties

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `length1` | integer | Total amino acid length of receptor chain |
| `length2` | integer | Total amino acid length of ligand chain |
| `length_resolved_1` | integer | Structurally resolved (Cα) residues in receptor |
| `length_resolved_2` | integer | Structurally resolved (Cα) residues in ligand |
| `number_of_components_1` | integer | Number of connected structural fragments in receptor |
| `number_of_components_2` | integer | Number of connected structural fragments in ligand |

### Interface Characterization (PRODIGY-cryst)

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `label` | string | Classification as biological interaction or crystal contact |
| `probability` | number | Probability that the complex is a true biological interaction |
| `link_density` | number | Interfacial contact density (contacts / max possible contacts) |
| `planarity` | number | Deviation of interface Cα atoms from fitted plane (shape complementarity) |

### Structural Quality Metrics

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `max_var_1` | number | Maximum variance on principal component (detects elongation) for receptor |
| `max_var_2` | number | Maximum variance on principal component (detects elongation) for ligand |
| `num_atom_types` | integer | Number of unique atom types (detects Cα-only or backbone-only structures) |

### Interface Properties

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `n_residue_pairs` | integer | Number of residue pairs at the interface |
| `n_residues` | integer | Total number of residues at the interface |
| `buried_sasa` | number | Buried solvent-accessible surface area upon complex formation (Ų) |
| `intermolecular_contacts` | integer | Total intermolecular contacts (residue pairs within 5Å) |

### Contact Type Classification

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `charged_charged_contacts` | integer | Contacts between charged residues (E, D, H, K, R) |
| `charged_polar_contacts` | integer | Contacts between charged (E, D, H, K, R) and polar (N, Q, S, T) |
| `charged_apolar_contacts` | integer | Contacts between charged and apolar (A, C, G, F, I, M, L, P, W, V, Y) |
| `polar_polar_contacts` | integer | Contacts between polar residues (N, Q, S, T) |
| `apolar_polar_contacts` | integer | Contacts between apolar and polar residues |
| `apolar_apolar_contacts` | integer | Contacts between apolar residues |

### Structural Gaps

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `interface_atom_gaps_4A` | integer | Interface atoms within 4Å of a residue gap |
| `missing_interface_residues_4A` | integer | Interface residues within 4Å of a gap |
| `interface_atom_gaps_8A` | integer | Interface atoms within 8Å of a residue gap |
| `missing_interface_residues_8A` | integer | Interface residues within 8Å of a gap |

### Entity and Domain Annotations

| Field | Type | Description |
|:------|:-----|:------------|
| `entity_id_R` | integer | RCSB entity_id for receptor chain |
| `entity_id_L` | integer | RCSB entity_id for ligand chain |
| `pdb_strand_id_R` | string | RCSB pdb_strand_id (author chain) for receptor |
| `pdb_strand_id_L` | string | RCSB pdb_strand_id (author chain) for ligand |
| `ECOD_names_R` | string | ECOD domain family names for receptor (comma-delimited if multiple) |
| `ECOD_names_L` | string | ECOD domain family names for ligand (comma-delimited if multiple) |

**Sources:** [README.md:569-624](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:675-693]()

## Accessing Index and Metadata

### Loading the Complete DataFrames

The dataset provides utility functions to load the complete index and metadata as pandas DataFrames:

```python
from pinder.core.index.utils import get_index, get_metadata

# Load complete index (2.4M+ rows)
index_df = get_index()

# Load complete metadata 
metadata_df = get_metadata()

# Query for specific systems
system_ids = ['1an1__A1_P00761--1an1__B1_P80424']
system_index = index_df.query('id in @system_ids')
system_metadata = metadata_df.query('id in @system_ids')
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:15-16](), [README.md:137-140]()

### Accessing via PinderSystem

The `PinderSystem` class provides convenient property accessors for the entry and metadata:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "PinderSystem Initialization"
        INIT["PinderSystem(entry='1an1__A1_P00761--1an1__B1_P80424')"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Property Access"
        ENTRY_PROP[".entry property<br/>Returns IndexEntry"]
        META_PROP[".metadata property<br/>Returns MetadataEntry"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Lazy Loading"
        CACHED["_metadata<br/>cached after first access"]
        QUERY["Query metadata.parquet<br/>on first access"]
    end
    
    INIT --> ENTRY_PROP
    INIT --> META_PROP
    
    META_PROP --> QUERY
    QUERY --> CACHED
    META_PROP -.->|"Subsequent calls"| CACHED
```

```python
from pinder.core import PinderSystem

# Initialize system
system = PinderSystem(entry='1an1__A1_P00761--1an1__B1_P80424')

# Access IndexEntry
entry = system.entry
print(f"PDB ID: {entry.pdb_id}")
print(f"Split: {entry.split}")
print(f"Has apo receptor: {entry.apo_R}")
print(f"Cluster: {entry.cluster_id}")

# Access MetadataEntry (lazy-loaded on first access)
metadata = system.metadata
print(f"Resolution: {metadata.resolution}Å")
print(f"Method: {metadata.method}")
print(f"Interface contacts: {metadata.intermolecular_contacts}")
print(f"Buried SASA: {metadata.buried_sasa}Ų")
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:110-161](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:675-693]()

## Usage in Filtering

### System-Level Filtering

The `FilterMetadataFields` filter class enables filtering based on any field in `MetadataEntry`:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader
from pinder.core.loader import filters

# Create filters using metadata fields
base_filters = [
    # Filter antibody-containing systems
    filters.FilterMetadataFields(contains_antibody=('', False)),
    
    # Filter by resolution
    filters.FilterMetadataFields(resolution=('<=', 3.5)),
    
    # Filter by experimental method
    filters.FilterMetadataFields(method=('==', 'X-RAY DIFFRACTION')),
    
    # Combine multiple criteria
    filters.FilterMetadataFields(
        contains_enzyme=('is not', True),
        num_atom_types=('>=', 4),
        intermolecular_contacts=('>=', 10),
    ),
]

# Use in loader
loader = PinderLoader(
    split='train',
    base_filters=base_filters,
)
```

### Query Operations

Direct DataFrame queries provide flexible filtering:

```python
from pinder.core.index.utils import get_index, get_metadata

index = get_index()
metadata = get_metadata()

# Find high-resolution heterodimers
high_res_systems = metadata.query(
    'resolution <= 2.0 and complex_type == "heteromer"'
)

# Find systems with apo structures
apo_systems = index.query('apo_R == True and apo_L == True')

# Find test systems with good interface quality
good_interfaces = metadata.query(
    'probability > 0.8 and planarity < 5.0 and buried_sasa > 1000'
)

# Join for combined queries
joined = index.merge(metadata, on='id')
filtered = joined.query(
    'split == "test" and resolution <= 3.0 and apo_R == True'
)
```

**Sources:** [README.md:625-669](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:686-687]()

## File Locations and Storage

The index and metadata files are stored at the root of the PINDER dataset directory:

```
<PINDER_BASE_DIR>/<release_version>/
├── index.parquet          # Master index (2.4M+ rows, 58 fields)
├── metadata.parquet       # Detailed metadata (45+ fields)
├── pdbs/                  # Structure files referenced by *_pdb fields
├── test_set_pdbs/        # Test set holo structures
└── mappings/             # UniProt mapping files
```

The default location is `~/.local/share/pinder/2024-02/` but can be customized via the `PINDER_BASE_DIR` environment variable.

**Sources:** [README.md:163-176](), [README.md:125-144]()

## Special Fields and Conventions

### System ID Format

The `id` field follows a strict naming convention:
```
<pdb_id>__<chain_R>_<uniprot_R>--<pdb_id>__<chain_L>_<uniprot_L>
```

Example: `1an1__A1_P00761--1an1__B1_P80424`

This format encodes:
- PDB ID: `1an1`
- Receptor chain: `A1`
- Receptor UniProt: `P00761`
- Ligand chain: `B1`
- Ligand UniProt: `P80424`

### Alternative Apo Structures

The `apo_R_pdbs` and `apo_L_pdbs` fields contain comma-delimited lists of alternative apo structures beyond the canonical pairing specified in `apo_R_pdb` and `apo_L_pdb`. These alternatives can be loaded using the `apo_receptor_pdb_code` and `apo_ligand_pdb_code` parameters when initializing `PinderSystem`.

### Test System Flag

The `test_system` property (derived from the `split` field) determines whether holo structures are loaded from `pdbs/` or `test_set_pdbs/`:

```python
# In PinderSystem.__init__
holo_pdb_path = (
    self.test_pdbs_path if self.entry.test_system else self.pdbs_path
)
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:132-153](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py:200-241](), [README.md:573]()

# Page: Data Loading System

# Data Loading System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/utils/timer.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/utils/timer.py)

</details>



The Data Loading System provides the infrastructure for loading PINDER protein systems and converting them into ML-ready data structures. This system bridges the gap between raw PDB files stored in the PINDER dataset and batched tensors or graphs consumable by PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric models.

The system is organized around three core components: **PinderLoader** for system iteration and filtering, **PinderDataset** for tensor-based workflows, and **PPIDataset** for graph neural network workflows. All three leverage a common filtering and transformation pipeline.

For details on the underlying data structures, see [Core Data Structures](#3). For information on specific filter implementations, see [Filtering System](#4.4). For evaluation workflows, see [Evaluation](#6).

## System Architecture

The data loading pipeline consists of multiple layers that progressively transform raw structural data into ML-ready batches:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Storage["Storage Layer"]
        INDEX["index.parquet<br/>2.4M+ entries"]
        METADATA["metadata.parquet<br/>Annotations"]
        PDBS["pdbs/<br/>Structural files"]
    end
    
    subgraph Orchestration["Orchestration Layer"]
        LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>System iteration & filtering"]
        MONOMER_SEL["select_monomer()<br/>Monomer selection logic"]
        CREATE_COMPLEX["_create_target_feature_complex()<br/>Complex construction"]
    end
    
    subgraph Filtering["Filtering Pipeline"]
        BASE_FILT["PinderFilterBase<br/>System-level filters"]
        SUB_FILT["PinderFilterSubBase<br/>Monomer-level filters"]
        STRUCT_FILT["StructureFilter<br/>Atomic-level filters"]
    end
    
    subgraph Datasets["Dataset Layer"]
        PINDER_DS["PinderDataset<br/>torch.utils.data.Dataset"]
        PPI_DS["PPIDataset<br/>torch_geometric.data.Dataset"]
    end
    
    subgraph DataLoaders["DataLoader Layer"]
        TORCH_DL["torch.utils.data.DataLoader<br/>collate_batch()"]
        GEO_DL["torch_geometric.loader.DataLoader"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Output Format"]
        TENSORS["Dict[str, Tensor]<br/>atom_coordinates<br/>atom_types<br/>residue_types"]
        HETERO["HeteroData<br/>ligand_atom<br/>receptor_atom<br/>edges"]
    end
    
    INDEX --> LOADER
    METADATA --> LOADER
    PDBS --> LOADER
    
    LOADER --> MONOMER_SEL
    MONOMER_SEL --> CREATE_COMPLEX
    
    BASE_FILT --> LOADER
    SUB_FILT --> LOADER
    STRUCT_FILT --> LOADER
    
    LOADER --> PINDER_DS
    LOADER --> PPI_DS
    
    PINDER_DS --> TORCH_DL
    PPI_DS --> GEO_DL
    
    TORCH_DL --> TENSORS
    GEO_DL --> HETERO
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:1-655](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:1-439]()

## Data Flow Pipeline

The following diagram illustrates how a single system progresses through the loading pipeline, from index entry to batched output:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Input["Input"]
        ROW["pd.Series<br/>Index row"]
    end
    
    subgraph PinderLoader["PinderLoader.__getitem__()"]
        LOAD_SYS["PinderSystem(row.id)"]
        APPLY_DIMER["apply_dimer_filters()<br/>base_filters + sub_filters"]
        SELECT["select_monomer()<br/>Choose apo/holo/pred"]
        CREATE["_create_target_feature_complex()<br/>Build complexes"]
        APPLY_STRUCT["apply_structure_filters()<br/>structure_filters"]
        TRANSFORM["Apply transforms<br/>structure_transforms_*"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Output"]
        TUPLE["(PinderSystem,<br/>Structure feature,<br/>Structure target)"]
    end
    
    ROW --> LOAD_SYS
    LOAD_SYS --> APPLY_DIMER
    APPLY_DIMER --> SELECT
    SELECT --> CREATE
    CREATE --> APPLY_STRUCT
    APPLY_STRUCT --> TRANSFORM
    TRANSFORM --> TUPLE
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:357-405]()

### Pipeline Stages

The loading pipeline executes the following stages for each system:

| Stage | Component | Purpose | Can Filter? |
|-------|-----------|---------|-------------|
| **System Loading** | `PinderSystem(row.id)` | Load system from disk | No |
| **Dimer Filtering** | `apply_dimer_filters()` | Apply base and sub filters | Yes |
| **Monomer Selection** | `select_monomer()` | Choose monomer types (apo/holo/pred) | No |
| **Complex Creation** | `_create_target_feature_complex()` | Build target and feature complexes | No |
| **Structure Filtering** | `apply_structure_filters()` | Apply structure-level filters | Yes |
| **Transformation** | `structure_transforms_*` | Apply augmentations | No |

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:357-405]()

## Core Components

### PinderLoader

The `PinderLoader` class is the central orchestrator of the loading pipeline. It implements the iterator protocol and provides indexed access to filtered and transformed systems.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Initialization["PinderLoader Initialization"]
        PARAMS["Constructor Parameters"]
        SPLIT["split: str<br/>train/val/test"]
        IDS["ids: list[str]<br/>Specific system IDs"]
        FILTERS["Filters<br/>base/sub/structure"]
        MONOMER_PRIORITY["monomer_priority: str<br/>apo/holo/pred/random"]
        QUERIES["index_query<br/>metadata_query"]
    end
    
    subgraph State["Internal State"]
        INDEX_DF["self.index: pd.DataFrame<br/>Filtered index"]
        METADATA_DF["self.metadata: pd.DataFrame<br/>Filtered metadata"]
        BASE_FILTERS["self.base_filters<br/>list[PinderFilterBase]"]
        SUB_FILTERS["self.sub_filters<br/>list[PinderFilterSubBase]"]
        STRUCT_FILTERS["self.structure_filters<br/>list[StructureFilter]"]
        TRANSFORMS["self.structure_transforms_*<br/>list[StructureTransform]"]
    end
    
    subgraph Methods["Key Methods"]
        LEN["__len__()<br/>Returns len(self.index)"]
        GETITEM["__getitem__(idx)<br/>Returns (system, feature, target)"]
        ITER["__iter__()<br/>Yields tuples"]
        APPLY_DIMER_FILTERS["apply_dimer_filters()<br/>Static method"]
        APPLY_STRUCT_FILTERS["apply_structure_filters()<br/>Instance method"]
    end
    
    PARAMS --> INDEX_DF
    PARAMS --> METADATA_DF
    PARAMS --> BASE_FILTERS
    PARAMS --> SUB_FILTERS
    PARAMS --> STRUCT_FILTERS
    PARAMS --> TRANSFORMS
    
    INDEX_DF --> LEN
    INDEX_DF --> GETITEM
    BASE_FILTERS --> APPLY_DIMER_FILTERS
    SUB_FILTERS --> APPLY_DIMER_FILTERS
    STRUCT_FILTERS --> APPLY_STRUCT_FILTERS
    TRANSFORMS --> GETITEM
```

**Key Parameters:**

- `split` (str): Dataset split to load (train/val/test)
- `monomer_priority` (str): Strategy for selecting monomers (holo/apo/pred/random/random_mixed)
- `base_filters` (list[PinderFilterBase]): System-level filters
- `sub_filters` (list[PinderFilterSubBase]): Monomer-level filters  
- `structure_filters` (list[StructureFilter]): Structure-level filters
- `crop_equal_monomer_shapes` (bool): Whether to crop target and feature to same shape
- `fallback_to_holo` (bool): Whether to fall back to holo when preferred monomer unavailable
- `max_load_attempts` (int): Maximum retries when system fails filters (default: 10)

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:192-265]()

### Monomer Selection Logic

The `select_monomer()` function determines which monomer type (holo/apo/pred) to use for receptor and ligand based on availability and priority:

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["select_monomer(row, monomer_priority)"]
    GET_AVAILABLE["get_available_monomers(row)<br/>Returns available types per side"]
    
    PRIORITY_CHECK{"monomer_priority?"}
    RANDOM_MIXED["random_mixed<br/>Random for R and L separately"]
    RANDOM["random<br/>Same random for both"]
    SPECIFIC["apo/holo/pred<br/>Use specified type"]
    
    PAIRED_CHECK{"Type available<br/>for both sides?"}
    FALLBACK_CHECK{"fallback_to_holo?"}
    USE_HOLO["Use holo for both"]
    ERROR["Raise ValueError"]
    
    APO_CHECK{"Selection == apo<br/>and not canonical?"}
    GET_ALT["get_alternate_apo_codes()<br/>Get non-canonical apo"]
    RANDOM_ALT["Randomly select alternate"]
    
    RESULT["Return dict[str, str]<br/>R and L selections"]
    
    START --> GET_AVAILABLE
    GET_AVAILABLE --> PRIORITY_CHECK
    
    PRIORITY_CHECK -->|"random_mixed"| RANDOM_MIXED
    PRIORITY_CHECK -->|"random"| RANDOM
    PRIORITY_CHECK -->|"apo/holo/pred"| SPECIFIC
    
    RANDOM_MIXED --> APO_CHECK
    RANDOM --> APO_CHECK
    
    SPECIFIC --> PAIRED_CHECK
    PAIRED_CHECK -->|"Yes"| APO_CHECK
    PAIRED_CHECK -->|"No"| FALLBACK_CHECK
    FALLBACK_CHECK -->|"True"| USE_HOLO
    FALLBACK_CHECK -->|"False"| ERROR
    USE_HOLO --> RESULT
    
    APO_CHECK -->|"Yes"| GET_ALT
    APO_CHECK -->|"No"| RESULT
    GET_ALT --> RANDOM_ALT
    RANDOM_ALT --> RESULT
```

**Monomer Priority Modes:**

| Mode | Behavior | Use Case |
|------|----------|----------|
| `holo` | Always use bound structures | Baseline performance, fastest loading |
| `apo` | Use unbound structures when available | Realistic docking scenario |
| `pred` | Use AlphaFold predictions when available | Evaluate prediction quality |
| `random` | Randomly select same type for R and L | Diverse training with consistent pairs |
| `random_mixed` | Randomly select types independently | Maximum diversity |

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:81-149](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:23]()

## Dataset Implementations

### PinderDataset

`PinderDataset` is a PyTorch `Dataset` implementation that yields dictionary-based tensor structures suitable for standard neural networks:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Initialization["PinderDataset"]
        LOADER_INIT["self.loader = PinderLoader(...)"]
        TRANSFORM["self.transform<br/>Structure -> Tensor"]
        TARGET_TRANSFORM["self.target_transform<br/>Structure -> Tensor"]
    end
    
    subgraph GetItem["__getitem__(idx)"]
        GET_FROM_LOADER["system, feature, target = self.loader[idx]"]
        APPLY_TRANSFORM["transform(feature)<br/>target_transform(target)"]
        BUILD_DICT["Build output dict"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Output Dictionary"]
        TARGET_COMPLEX["target_complex:<br/>dict[str, Tensor]"]
        FEATURE_COMPLEX["feature_complex:<br/>dict[str, Tensor]"]
        IDS["id: str<br/>sample_id: str<br/>target_id: str"]
    end
    
    subgraph TensorStructure["Tensor Dictionary Keys"]
        ATOM_COORDS["atom_coordinates<br/>(N_atoms, 3)"]
        ATOM_TYPES["atom_types<br/>(N_atoms,)"]
        ELEMENT_TYPES["element_types<br/>(N_atoms,)"]
        RES_COORDS["residue_coordinates<br/>(N_residues, 3)"]
        RES_TYPES["residue_types<br/>(N_residues,)"]
        RES_IDS["residue_ids<br/>(N_residues,)"]
        CHAIN_IDS["chain_ids<br/>(N_residues,)"]
    end
    
    LOADER_INIT --> GET_FROM_LOADER
    GET_FROM_LOADER --> APPLY_TRANSFORM
    APPLY_TRANSFORM --> BUILD_DICT
    BUILD_DICT --> TARGET_COMPLEX
    BUILD_DICT --> FEATURE_COMPLEX
    BUILD_DICT --> IDS
    
    TARGET_COMPLEX --> ATOM_COORDS
    TARGET_COMPLEX --> ATOM_TYPES
    TARGET_COMPLEX --> ELEMENT_TYPES
    TARGET_COMPLEX --> RES_COORDS
    TARGET_COMPLEX --> RES_TYPES
    TARGET_COMPLEX --> RES_IDS
    TARGET_COMPLEX --> CHAIN_IDS
```

**Default Transform:** The `structure2tensor_transform()` function converts a `Structure` object into a dictionary of tensors using `structure2tensor()` from the geodata module.

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:246-318](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:55-66]()

### PPIDataset

`PPIDataset` is a PyTorch Geometric `Dataset` that creates heterogeneous graph representations (`HeteroData`) suitable for graph neural networks:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Initialization["PPIDataset"]
        NODE_TYPES["node_types:<br/>set[NodeRepresentation]"]
        MONOMER_SPEC["monomer1: str<br/>monomer2: str"]
        LOADER_INIT["self.loader = PinderLoader"]
        PARALLEL["parallel: bool<br/>max_workers: int"]
    end
    
    subgraph Processing["process() / process_parallel()"]
        ITERATE["Iterate over loader"]
        CREATE_PAIRED["PairedPDB.from_pinder_system()"]
        APPLY_PRE_TRANSFORM["Apply pre_transform"]
        SAVE_PT["torch.save(data, .pt file)"]
        TRACK_FILES["Track filenames"]
    end
    
    subgraph Storage["Processed Files"]
        PROCESSED_DIR["processed/<br/>*.pt files"]
        FILENAMES_TXT["filenames/filenames.txt"]
    end
    
    subgraph GetItem["get(idx)"]
        LOAD_PT["torch.load(filename.pt)"]
        PAIRED_PDB["Returns PairedPDB"]
    end
    
    subgraph HeteroData["HeteroData Structure"]
        LIGAND_ATOM["ligand_atom<br/>Node features"]
        RECEPTOR_ATOM["receptor_atom<br/>Node features"]
        LIGAND_RES["ligand_residue<br/>Node features"]
        RECEPTOR_RES["receptor_residue<br/>Node features"]
        EDGES["Edge indices<br/>k-NN connections"]
    end
    
    NODE_TYPES --> CREATE_PAIRED
    MONOMER_SPEC --> CREATE_PAIRED
    LOADER_INIT --> ITERATE
    
    ITERATE --> CREATE_PAIRED
    CREATE_PAIRED --> APPLY_PRE_TRANSFORM
    APPLY_PRE_TRANSFORM --> SAVE_PT
    SAVE_PT --> PROCESSED_DIR
    TRACK_FILES --> FILENAMES_TXT
    
    PROCESSED_DIR --> LOAD_PT
    LOAD_PT --> PAIRED_PDB
    
    PAIRED_PDB --> LIGAND_ATOM
    PAIRED_PDB --> RECEPTOR_ATOM
    PAIRED_PDB --> LIGAND_RES
    PAIRED_PDB --> RECEPTOR_RES
    PAIRED_PDB --> EDGES
```

**Key Features:**

- **Preprocessing:** Converts all systems to `.pt` files during initialization
- **Caching:** Reuses processed files across runs when `use_cache=True`
- **Parallel Processing:** Supports multiprocessing via `parallel=True`
- **Node Types:** Supports atom-level and residue-level representations
- **Edges:** Automatically adds k-NN edges between nodes when `add_edges=True`

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:320-623]()

## Filtering Architecture

The filtering system operates at three distinct levels:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Level1["Level 1: Base Filters"]
        BASE_DESC["System-level properties<br/>Applied to PinderSystem"]
        BASE_EXAMPLES["Examples:<br/>- Cluster size<br/>- Quality metrics<br/>- Missing structures"]
    end
    
    subgraph Level2["Level 2: Sub Filters"]
        SUB_DESC["Monomer-level properties<br/>Modifies PinderSystem"]
        SUB_EXAMPLES["Examples:<br/>- Sequence length<br/>- Resolution<br/>- Completeness"]
        SUB_ACTION["Can set monomers to None"]
    end
    
    subgraph Level3["Level 3: Structure Filters"]
        STRUCT_DESC["Atomic-level properties<br/>Applied to Structure"]
        STRUCT_EXAMPLES["Examples:<br/>- Atom count<br/>- Coordinate validity<br/>- Clashes"]
    end
    
    subgraph Application["Filter Application"]
        LOADER_APPLY["PinderLoader.__getitem__()"]
        STEP1["1. apply_dimer_filters()"]
        STEP2["2. select_monomer()"]
        STEP3["3. apply_structure_filters()"]
    end
    
    BASE_DESC --> BASE_EXAMPLES
    SUB_DESC --> SUB_EXAMPLES
    SUB_EXAMPLES --> SUB_ACTION
    STRUCT_DESC --> STRUCT_EXAMPLES
    
    LOADER_APPLY --> STEP1
    STEP1 --> STEP2
    STEP2 --> STEP3
    
    BASE_EXAMPLES -.->|"Input to"| STEP1
    SUB_EXAMPLES -.->|"Input to"| STEP1
    STRUCT_EXAMPLES -.->|"Input to"| STEP3
```

**Filter Behavior:**

| Filter Type | Input | Output | Modifies System? |
|-------------|-------|--------|------------------|
| `PinderFilterBase` | `PinderSystem` | `bool` | No |
| `PinderFilterSubBase` | `PinderSystem` | `PinderSystem` | Yes (can set monomers to None) |
| `StructureFilter` | `Structure` | `bool` | No |

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:415-435](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:407-413]()

## Complex Construction

The `_create_target_feature_complex()` function builds the target (ground truth holo) and feature (potentially apo/pred) complexes:

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["_create_target_feature_complex()"]
    INPUTS["Inputs:<br/>system: PinderSystem<br/>selected_monomers: dict<br/>crop_equal_monomer_shapes: bool"]
    
    GET_HOLO["holo_R = system.aligned_holo_R<br/>holo_L = system.aligned_holo_L"]
    
    CHECK_ALT{"Selected monomer<br/>is PDB code?"}
    SET_APO_CODE["system.apo_receptor_pdb_code = code<br/>selected_monomers[side] = 'apo'"]
    
    GET_DECOY["decoy_R = getattr(system, monomer + '_receptor')<br/>decoy_L = getattr(system, monomer + '_ligand')"]
    
    CHECK_NULL{"decoy is None?"}
    FALLBACK{"fallback_to_holo?"}
    SET_HOLO["decoy = holo monomer"]
    RAISE_ERROR["Raise ValueError"]
    
    BOTH_HOLO{"Both selections<br/>are holo?"}
    CROP{"crop_equal_<br/>monomer_shapes?"}
    ALIGN_CROP["_align_monomers_with_mask()<br/>Crop to common atoms"]
    
    BUILD_COMPLEXES["target = holo_R + holo_L<br/>feature = decoy_R + decoy_L"]
    RETURN["Return (target, feature)"]
    
    START --> INPUTS
    INPUTS --> GET_HOLO
    GET_HOLO --> CHECK_ALT
    
    CHECK_ALT -->|"Yes"| SET_APO_CODE
    CHECK_ALT -->|"No"| GET_DECOY
    SET_APO_CODE --> GET_DECOY
    
    GET_DECOY --> CHECK_NULL
    CHECK_NULL -->|"Yes"| FALLBACK
    CHECK_NULL -->|"No"| BOTH_HOLO
    
    FALLBACK -->|"True"| SET_HOLO
    FALLBACK -->|"False"| RAISE_ERROR
    SET_HOLO --> BOTH_HOLO
    
    BOTH_HOLO -->|"No"| CROP
    BOTH_HOLO -->|"Yes"| BUILD_COMPLEXES
    
    CROP -->|"True"| ALIGN_CROP
    CROP -->|"False"| BUILD_COMPLEXES
    
    ALIGN_CROP --> BUILD_COMPLEXES
    BUILD_COMPLEXES --> RETURN
```

**Shape Alignment:** When `crop_equal_monomer_shapes=True`, the function uses `_align_monomers_with_mask()` to crop holo and decoy structures to matching atom sets based on sequence alignment. This ensures the target and feature complexes have identical shapes, which is required by many loss functions.

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:152-189]()

## Batching and Collation

### Padding Strategy

Variable-sized protein structures are padded to a uniform size within each batch using the `pad_and_stack()` and `collate_complex()` functions:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Input["Batch Input"]
        LIST["list[dict[str, Tensor]]<br/>Variable sizes"]
    end
    
    subgraph CollateComplex["collate_complex()"]
        EXTRACT["Extract tensors:<br/>atom_coordinates<br/>atom_types<br/>residue_coordinates<br/>etc."]
        
        PAD_STACK["For each tensor type:<br/>pad_and_stack()"]
    end
    
    subgraph PadAndStack["pad_and_stack()"]
        FIND_MAX["Find max shape:<br/>shapes.max(dim=0)"]
        PAD_EACH["For each tensor:<br/>pad_to_max_length()"]
        STACK["torch.stack()"]
    end
    
    subgraph PadToMaxLength["pad_to_max_length()"]
        CALC_PAD["Calculate padding:<br/>max_length - current_length"]
        APPLY_PAD["torch.nn.functional.pad()"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Batch Output"]
        PADDED["dict[str, Tensor]<br/>Uniform shape (B, N, ...)"]
    end
    
    LIST --> EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> PAD_STACK
    PAD_STACK --> FIND_MAX
    FIND_MAX --> PAD_EACH
    PAD_EACH --> CALC_PAD
    CALC_PAD --> APPLY_PAD
    APPLY_PAD --> STACK
    STACK --> PADDED
```

**Padding Values:**

| Tensor Type | Padding Value | Purpose |
|-------------|---------------|---------|
| `atom_coordinates` | -100 | Distinguishable from valid coordinates |
| `residue_coordinates` | -100 | Distinguishable from valid coordinates |
| `atom_types` | -1 | Invalid atom type index |
| `element_types` | -1 | Invalid element type index |
| `residue_types` | -1 | Invalid residue type index |
| `residue_ids` | -99 | Invalid residue ID |
| `chain_ids` | -1 | Invalid chain ID |

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:69-163](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:165-202](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:205-243]()

### Collation Functions

The `collate_batch()` function merges a list of dataset items into a single batch:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph BatchInput["Batch Input"]
        ITEMS["list[dict]<br/>Each dict has:<br/>- id<br/>- sample_id<br/>- target_id<br/>- target_complex<br/>- feature_complex"]
    end
    
    subgraph Processing["collate_batch()"]
        SEPARATE["Separate into lists:<br/>ids<br/>sample_ids<br/>target_ids<br/>target_structures<br/>feature_structures"]
        
        COLLATE_TARGET["collate_complex(<br/>target_structures)"]
        COLLATE_FEATURE["collate_complex(<br/>feature_structures)"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Batch Output"]
        BATCH["dict:<br/>- target_complex: dict[str, Tensor]<br/>- feature_complex: dict[str, Tensor]<br/>- id: list[str]<br/>- sample_id: list[str]<br/>- target_id: list[str]"]
    end
    
    ITEMS --> SEPARATE
    SEPARATE --> COLLATE_TARGET
    SEPARATE --> COLLATE_FEATURE
    COLLATE_TARGET --> BATCH
    COLLATE_FEATURE --> BATCH
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:205-243]()

## DataLoader Construction

### PyTorch DataLoader

The `get_torch_loader()` function creates a standard PyTorch `DataLoader` for `PinderDataset`:

```python
def get_torch_loader(
    dataset: PinderDataset,
    batch_size: int = 2,
    shuffle: bool = True,
    sampler: Sampler | None = None,
    num_workers: int = 1,
    collate_fn: Callable = collate_batch,
    **kwargs
) -> DataLoader[PinderDataset]:
    return DataLoader(
        dataset,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=shuffle,
        num_workers=num_workers,
        sampler=sampler,
        collate_fn=collate_fn,
        **kwargs,
    )
```

**Key Parameters:**
- `collate_fn`: Defaults to `collate_batch()` which handles variable-sized structures
- `sampler`: Can provide custom sampling logic (e.g., diversity sampling)
- `num_workers`: Number of subprocesses for data loading

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:637-655]()

### PyTorch Geometric DataLoader

The `get_geo_loader()` function creates a PyTorch Geometric `DataLoader` for `PPIDataset`:

```python
def get_geo_loader(
    dataset: PPIDataset,
    batch_size: int = 2,
    num_workers: int = 1
) -> TorchGeoDataLoader:
    return TorchGeoDataLoader(
        dataset,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=True,
        drop_last=True,
        num_workers=num_workers,
    )
```

**Graph Batching:** PyTorch Geometric's `DataLoader` automatically handles batching of `HeteroData` objects by concatenating node features and adjusting edge indices with offsets.

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:625-634]()

## Usage Patterns

### Basic PinderDataset Example

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PinderDataset, get_torch_loader

# Create dataset
dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    monomer_priority="apo",
    fallback_to_holo=True,
)

# Create dataloader
loader = get_torch_loader(
    dataset,
    batch_size=4,
    shuffle=True,
    num_workers=2
)

# Iterate
for batch in loader:
    target = batch["target_complex"]  # Ground truth
    feature = batch["feature_complex"]  # Apo structures
    ids = batch["id"]  # System IDs
    # Train model...
```

### Basic PPIDataset Example

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PPIDataset, get_geo_loader
from pinder.core.loader.geodata import NodeRepresentation

# Create dataset
dataset = PPIDataset(
    node_types={NodeRepresentation.ATOM},
    split="train",
    monomer1="apo_receptor",
    monomer2="apo_ligand",
    add_edges=True,
    k=10,  # 10-NN edges
)

# Create dataloader
loader = get_geo_loader(dataset, batch_size=4, num_workers=2)

# Iterate
for batch in loader:
    receptor_feats = batch["receptor_atom"]
    ligand_feats = batch["ligand_atom"]
    # Train GNN model...
```

### Advanced: Custom Filtering and Transforms

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PinderDataset
from pinder.core.loader.filters import PinderFilterBase, StructureFilter
from pinder.core.loader.transforms import SelectAtomTypes

# Define custom filters
class MinAtomFilter(StructureFilter):
    def __init__(self, min_atoms: int):
        self.min_atoms = min_atoms
    
    def __call__(self, structure: Structure) -> bool:
        return len(structure.atom_array) >= self.min_atoms

# Create dataset with filters and transforms
dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    structure_filters=[MinAtomFilter(min_atoms=100)],
    structure_transforms_feature=[
        SelectAtomTypes(atom_types=["CA"])  # Use only alpha carbons
    ],
    monomer_priority="random_mixed",
    crop_equal_monomer_shapes=True,
)
```

## Retry Logic and Error Handling

When a system fails filters or cannot be loaded, `PinderLoader` automatically retries with a random index:

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["__getitem__(idx)"]
    INIT["valid_idx = False<br/>attempts = 0"]
    
    LOOP_START{"valid_idx or<br/>attempts >= max?"}
    INCREMENT["attempts += 1"]
    LOAD["Load row at idx<br/>Create PinderSystem"]
    
    APPLY_FILTERS["apply_dimer_filters()"]
    CHECK_SYSTEM{"Is valid<br/>PinderSystem?"}
    RANDOM_IDX["idx = random.choice(range(len(self)))"]
    
    BUILD["select_monomer()<br/>_create_target_feature_complex()"]
    APPLY_STRUCT["apply_structure_filters()"]
    CHECK_VALID{"Pass filters?"}
    
    APPLY_TRANSFORMS["Apply structure_transforms_*"]
    RETURN["Return (system, feature, target)"]
    ERROR["Raise IndexError"]
    
    START --> INIT
    INIT --> LOOP_START
    
    LOOP_START -->|"Continue"| INCREMENT
    LOOP_START -->|"Stop - valid"| APPLY_TRANSFORMS
    LOOP_START -->|"Stop - exceeded"| ERROR
    
    INCREMENT --> LOAD
    LOAD --> APPLY_FILTERS
    APPLY_FILTERS --> CHECK_SYSTEM
    
    CHECK_SYSTEM -->|"No"| RANDOM_IDX
    CHECK_SYSTEM -->|"Yes"| BUILD
    
    BUILD --> APPLY_STRUCT
    APPLY_STRUCT --> CHECK_VALID
    
    CHECK_VALID -->|"No"| RANDOM_IDX
    CHECK_VALID -->|"Yes"| LOOP_START
    
    RANDOM_IDX --> LOOP_START
    APPLY_TRANSFORMS --> RETURN
```

**Configurable Retry:** The `max_load_attempts` parameter (default: 10) controls how many times the loader will retry before raising an `IndexError`.

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:357-405]()

## Performance Considerations

### Caching Strategies

| Strategy | Dataset | Benefit | Cost |
|----------|---------|---------|------|
| **Index Filtering** | Both | Pre-filter index to reduce iteration | Higher memory for large filters |
| **Processed Files** | PPIDataset | Avoid repeated graph construction | Disk space (~1-2 MB per system) |
| **Multiprocessing** | PPIDataset | Parallel preprocessing | CPU and memory overhead |
| **DataLoader Workers** | Both | Parallel batch preparation | Memory per worker |

### Memory Optimization

**PinderDataset:**
- Loads structures on-demand (no caching)
- Memory scales with batch size and number of workers
- Use `num_workers=0` for low-memory environments

**PPIDataset:**
- Preprocesses all systems to disk once
- Memory usage during iteration is low
- Set `use_cache=True` to skip reprocessing

### Parallel Processing

`PPIDataset` supports parallel preprocessing via multiprocessing:

```python
dataset = PPIDataset(
    ...,
    parallel=True,
    max_workers=8,  # Number of parallel workers
    force_reload=False,  # Skip existing processed files
)
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:511-541]()

## Integration with Training Loops

The data loading system integrates seamlessly with standard PyTorch training patterns:

```python
# Standard PyTorch training loop
model = MyModel()
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters())

for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    for batch in train_loader:
        target = batch["target_complex"]
        feature = batch["feature_complex"]
        
        # Forward pass
        pred = model(feature)
        loss = criterion(pred, target)
        
        # Backward pass
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
```

**Batch Structure:** Both `PinderDataset` and `PPIDataset` return batches with consistent keys, making it easy to switch between tensor-based and graph-based models with minimal code changes.

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:1-19]()

# Page: PinderLoader

# PinderLoader

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb](examples/pinder-loader.ipynb)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/utils/timer.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/utils/timer.py)

</details>



`PinderLoader` is the core iterator class in PINDER that orchestrates loading, filtering, and transforming protein systems for machine learning workflows. It serves as the central orchestration layer between the raw PINDER dataset and downstream dataset implementations.

For information about the downstream PyTorch-compatible datasets that use PinderLoader, see [PinderDataset](#4.2) and [PPIDataset](#4.3). For details on the filtering system, see [Filtering System](#4.4). For information about structure transformations, see [Transforms and Augmentation](#4.5).

## Overview

`PinderLoader` provides an iterable interface that:
- Loads `PinderSystem` objects from the PINDER index
- Applies multi-stage filtering (base, sub, structure)
- Selects monomers according to configurable priority strategies
- Creates target and feature complexes with optional cropping and alignment
- Applies structure-level transformations
- Optionally writes processed structures to disk

The loader returns tuples of `(PinderSystem, Structure, Structure)` representing the original system metadata, the feature complex (potentially with apo/predicted monomers), and the target complex (ground truth).

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:192-439]()

## Architecture

### High-Level Data Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Sources"
        INDEX["Index DataFrame<br/>pinder.index"]
        METADATA["Metadata DataFrame<br/>pinder.metadata"]
        IDS["System IDs<br/>list[str]"]
        SPLIT["Split Name<br/>train/val/test"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PinderLoader Initialization"
        QUERY["Index/Metadata Queries<br/>Optional filtering"]
        SUBSET["Test Subset<br/>pinder_xl/s/af2"]
        PARAMS["Configuration<br/>monomer_priority<br/>fallback_to_holo<br/>crop_equal_monomer_shapes"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Filter Configuration"
        BASE_F["base_filters<br/>list[PinderFilterBase]<br/>System-level"]
        SUB_F["sub_filters<br/>list[PinderFilterSubBase]<br/>Monomer-level"]
        STRUCT_F["structure_filters<br/>list[StructureFilter]<br/>Atom-level"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transform Configuration"
        TRANS_T["structure_transforms_target<br/>list[StructureTransform]"]
        TRANS_F["structure_transforms_feature<br/>list[StructureTransform]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PinderLoader Instance"
        LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>__getitem__<br/>__iter__<br/>__len__"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        OUTPUT["tuple[PinderSystem,<br/>Structure,<br/>Structure]<br/>(system, feature, target)"]
    end
    
    INDEX --> QUERY
    METADATA --> QUERY
    IDS --> QUERY
    SPLIT --> QUERY
    SUBSET --> QUERY
    
    QUERY --> LOADER
    PARAMS --> LOADER
    BASE_F --> LOADER
    SUB_F --> LOADER
    STRUCT_F --> LOADER
    TRANS_T --> LOADER
    TRANS_F --> LOADER
    
    LOADER --> OUTPUT
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:192-346]()

### Item Retrieval Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["__getitem__(idx)"]
    
    LOAD["Load system<br/>PinderSystem(row.id)"]
    
    BASE_FILT["Apply base_filters<br/>apply_dimer_filters()"]
    SUB_FILT["Apply sub_filters<br/>apply_dimer_filters()"]
    
    CHECK1{"Pass<br/>filters?"}
    
    SELECT["Select monomers<br/>select_monomer()<br/>or pre_specified_monomers"]
    
    CREATE["Create complexes<br/>_create_target_feature_complex()"]
    
    STRUCT_FILT["Apply structure_filters<br/>apply_structure_filters()"]
    
    CHECK2{"Pass<br/>filters?"}
    
    TRANS_T["Apply structure_transforms_target"]
    TRANS_F["Apply structure_transforms_feature"]
    
    WRITE{"writer<br/>defined?"}
    WRITE_OP["writer.write(system)"]
    
    RETURN["Return<br/>(system, feature, target)"]
    
    RANDOM["Select random idx<br/>Retry"]
    MAX_CHECK{"Attempts <<br/>max_load_attempts?"}
    ERROR["Raise IndexError"]
    
    START --> LOAD
    LOAD --> BASE_FILT
    BASE_FILT --> SUB_FILT
    SUB_FILT --> CHECK1
    
    CHECK1 -->|No| MAX_CHECK
    CHECK1 -->|Yes| SELECT
    
    SELECT --> CREATE
    CREATE --> STRUCT_FILT
    STRUCT_FILT --> CHECK2
    
    CHECK2 -->|No| MAX_CHECK
    CHECK2 -->|Yes| TRANS_T
    
    MAX_CHECK -->|Yes| RANDOM
    MAX_CHECK -->|No| ERROR
    RANDOM --> LOAD
    
    TRANS_T --> TRANS_F
    TRANS_F --> WRITE
    
    WRITE -->|Yes| WRITE_OP
    WRITE -->|No| RETURN
    WRITE_OP --> RETURN
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:357-405]()

## Initialization Parameters

The `PinderLoader.__init__` method accepts the following parameter groups:

### Data Selection Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `split` | `str \| None` | `None` | Dataset split: `"train"`, `"val"`, or `"test"` |
| `ids` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Explicit list of PINDER system IDs to load |
| `index` | `pd.DataFrame \| None` | `None` | Custom index DataFrame (retrieved via `get_index()` if not provided) |
| `metadata` | `pd.DataFrame \| None` | `None` | Custom metadata DataFrame (retrieved via `get_metadata()` if not provided) |
| `subset` | `DatasetName \| None` | `None` | Test subset: `"pinder_xl"`, `"pinder_s"`, or `"pinder_af2"` |
| `index_query` | `str \| None` | `None` | Pandas query string to filter index |
| `metadata_query` | `str \| None` | `None` | Pandas query string to filter metadata |

### Filtering Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `base_filters` | `list[PinderFilterBase]` | `[]` | System-level filters (e.g., `FilterByMissingHolo`) |
| `sub_filters` | `list[PinderFilterSubBase]` | `[]` | Monomer-level filters (e.g., `FilterByHoloSeqIdentity`) |
| `structure_filters` | `list[StructureFilter]` | `[]` | Atom-level filters applied to complexes |

### Transformation Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `structure_transforms_target` | `list[StructureTransform]` | `[]` | Transforms applied to target complex |
| `structure_transforms_feature` | `list[StructureTransform]` | `[]` | Transforms applied to feature complex |

### Monomer Selection Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `monomer_priority` | `str` | `"holo"` | Priority strategy: `"holo"`, `"apo"`, `"pred"`, `"random"`, `"random_mixed"` |
| `fallback_to_holo` | `bool` | `True` | Fallback to holo when requested monomer unavailable |
| `use_canonical_apo` | `bool` | `True` | Use canonical apo monomer (vs. alternates) |
| `pre_specified_monomers` | `dict \| pd.DataFrame \| None` | `None` | Explicit monomer selection per system |

### Other Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `crop_equal_monomer_shapes` | `bool` | `True` | Crop holo/decoy complexes to common shape |
| `max_load_attempts` | `int` | `10` | Max retries before raising `IndexError` |
| `writer` | `PinderWriterBase \| None` | `None` | Optional writer for persisting structures |

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:193-264]()

## Monomer Selection

### Selection Strategies

The `monomer_priority` parameter controls which monomer types are used to construct the feature complex:

| Strategy | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `"holo"` | Use bound (holo) monomers for both receptor and ligand |
| `"apo"` | Use unbound (apo) monomers for both receptor and ligand |
| `"pred"` | Use predicted (AlphaFold2) monomers for both receptor and ligand |
| `"random"` | Randomly select from available types, same for both R and L |
| `"random_mixed"` | Independently random selection for receptor and ligand |

### Monomer Selection Process

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["select_monomer(row)"]
    
    GET_AVAIL["get_available_monomers(row)<br/>Returns: dict[str, list[str]]"]
    
    PAIRED["Compute paired_monomers<br/>Intersection of R and L"]
    
    CHECK_PRIORITY{"monomer_priority"}
    
    RANDOM_MIXED["Random R: choice(avail_R)<br/>Random L: choice(avail_L)"]
    RANDOM["Random pair: choice(paired)"]
    SPECIFIC["Use specified priority<br/>if in paired_monomers"]
    
    CHECK_FALLBACK{"Priority<br/>in paired?"}
    
    FALLBACK_CHECK{"fallback_to_holo<br/>enabled?"}
    
    USE_HOLO["R_selection = 'holo'<br/>L_selection = 'holo'"]
    ERROR["Raise ValueError"]
    
    CHECK_CANON{"use_canonical_apo<br/>== False?"}
    
    GET_ALT_R["get_alternate_apo_codes(row, 'R')"]
    GET_ALT_L["get_alternate_apo_codes(row, 'L')"]
    
    SELECT_ALT_R["R_selection = random.choice(alt_R)"]
    SELECT_ALT_L["L_selection = random.choice(alt_L)"]
    
    RETURN["Return selected_monomers<br/>dict[str, str]"]
    
    START --> GET_AVAIL
    GET_AVAIL --> PAIRED
    PAIRED --> CHECK_PRIORITY
    
    CHECK_PRIORITY -->|"random_mixed"| RANDOM_MIXED
    CHECK_PRIORITY -->|"random"| RANDOM
    CHECK_PRIORITY -->|"holo/apo/pred"| CHECK_FALLBACK
    
    CHECK_FALLBACK -->|Yes| SPECIFIC
    CHECK_FALLBACK -->|No| FALLBACK_CHECK
    
    FALLBACK_CHECK -->|Yes| USE_HOLO
    FALLBACK_CHECK -->|No| ERROR
    
    RANDOM_MIXED --> CHECK_CANON
    RANDOM --> CHECK_CANON
    SPECIFIC --> CHECK_CANON
    USE_HOLO --> CHECK_CANON
    
    CHECK_CANON -->|Yes, R='apo'| GET_ALT_R
    CHECK_CANON -->|Yes, L='apo'| GET_ALT_L
    CHECK_CANON -->|No| RETURN
    
    GET_ALT_R --> SELECT_ALT_R
    GET_ALT_L --> SELECT_ALT_L
    
    SELECT_ALT_R --> RETURN
    SELECT_ALT_L --> RETURN
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:81-149](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:37-78]()

### Creating Target and Feature Complexes

The `_create_target_feature_complex` function constructs the two Structure objects returned by the loader:

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["_create_target_feature_complex()"]
    
    GET_HOLO["Get aligned holos<br/>holo_R = system.aligned_holo_R<br/>holo_L = system.aligned_holo_L"]
    
    CHECK_ALT_R{"selected_R not in<br/>[holo, apo, pred]?"}
    CHECK_ALT_L{"selected_L not in<br/>[holo, apo, pred]?"}
    
    SET_ALT_R["system.apo_receptor_pdb_code = selected_R<br/>selected_R = 'apo'"]
    SET_ALT_L["system.apo_ligand_pdb_code = selected_L<br/>selected_L = 'apo'"]
    
    GET_DECOY["Get selected monomers<br/>decoy_R = getattr(system, selected_R + '_receptor')<br/>decoy_L = getattr(system, selected_L + '_ligand')"]
    
    CHECK_NONE_R{"decoy_R<br/>is None?"}
    CHECK_NONE_L{"decoy_L<br/>is None?"}
    
    FALLBACK_R["Fallback if enabled<br/>decoy_R = holo_receptor"]
    FALLBACK_L["Fallback if enabled<br/>decoy_L = holo_ligand"]
    
    VALIDATE{"decoy_R and decoy_L<br/>both valid?"}
    
    ERROR["Raise ValueError"]
    
    CHECK_BOTH_HOLO{"Both selected<br/>monomers == 'holo'?"}
    
    CROP{"crop_equal_monomer_shapes<br/>enabled?"}
    
    ALIGN["Crop and align<br/>holo_R, decoy_R = _align_monomers_with_mask()<br/>holo_L, decoy_L = _align_monomers_with_mask()"]
    
    CREATE["Create complexes<br/>target_complex = holo_R + holo_L<br/>feature_complex = decoy_R + decoy_L"]
    
    RETURN["Return<br/>(target_complex, feature_complex)"]
    
    START --> GET_HOLO
    GET_HOLO --> CHECK_ALT_R
    
    CHECK_ALT_R -->|Yes| SET_ALT_R
    CHECK_ALT_R -->|No| CHECK_ALT_L
    SET_ALT_R --> CHECK_ALT_L
    
    CHECK_ALT_L -->|Yes| SET_ALT_L
    CHECK_ALT_L -->|No| GET_DECOY
    SET_ALT_L --> GET_DECOY
    
    GET_DECOY --> CHECK_NONE_R
    
    CHECK_NONE_R -->|Yes| FALLBACK_R
    CHECK_NONE_R -->|No| CHECK_NONE_L
    FALLBACK_R --> CHECK_NONE_L
    
    CHECK_NONE_L -->|Yes| FALLBACK_L
    CHECK_NONE_L -->|No| VALIDATE
    FALLBACK_L --> VALIDATE
    
    VALIDATE -->|No| ERROR
    VALIDATE -->|Yes| CHECK_BOTH_HOLO
    
    CHECK_BOTH_HOLO -->|Yes| CREATE
    CHECK_BOTH_HOLO -->|No| CROP
    
    CROP -->|Yes| ALIGN
    CROP -->|No| CREATE
    ALIGN --> CREATE
    
    CREATE --> RETURN
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:152-189]()

## Filtering System

`PinderLoader` applies filters in three stages, each operating at a different granularity:

### Filter Stages

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Stage 1: Base Filters"
        BASE["PinderFilterBase<br/>System-level validation<br/>e.g., FilterByMissingHolo"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Sub Filters"
        SUB["PinderFilterSubBase<br/>Monomer-level validation<br/>e.g., FilterByHoloSeqIdentity"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Structure Filters"
        STRUCT["StructureFilter<br/>Atom-level validation<br/>Applied to target_complex"]
    end
    
    SYSTEM["PinderSystem"] --> BASE
    BASE --> SUB
    SUB --> STRUCT
    STRUCT --> VALID["Valid System"]
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:415-435](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:407-413]()

### Filter Application

The `apply_dimer_filters` static method handles base and sub filter stages:

```python
# From loader.py:415-435
@staticmethod
def apply_dimer_filters(
    dimer: PinderSystem,
    base_filters: list[PinderFilterBase] | list[None] = [],
    sub_filters: list[PinderFilterSubBase] | list[None] = [],
) -> PinderSystem | bool:
    for sub_filter in sub_filters:
        if isinstance(sub_filter, PinderFilterSubBase):
            try:
                dimer = sub_filter(dimer)
            except Exception as e:
                log.error(f"Failed to apply sub_filter={sub_filter} on {dimer.entry.id}: {e}")
                return False
    for base_filter in base_filters:
        if isinstance(base_filter, PinderFilterBase):
            if not base_filter(dimer):
                return False
    return dimer
```

Note that sub filters can modify the `PinderSystem` object (e.g., setting monomer attributes to `None`), while base filters return boolean values without modification.

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:415-435]()

## Usage Examples

### Basic Usage with Split

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

# Load training set with holo monomers
train_loader = PinderLoader(split="train", monomer_priority="holo")

# Iterate over systems
for system, feature_complex, target_complex in train_loader:
    # system: PinderSystem with metadata
    # feature_complex: Structure with selected monomers
    # target_complex: Structure with ground truth holo dimer
    print(f"System ID: {system.entry.id}")
    print(f"Feature atoms: {len(feature_complex.coords)}")
    print(f"Target atoms: {len(target_complex.coords)}")
```

**Sources:** [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:438-480]()

### Usage with Filters

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader
from pinder.core.loader import filters

base_filters = [
    filters.FilterByMissingHolo(),
    filters.FilterSubByContacts(min_contacts=5, radius=10.0, calpha_only=True),
    filters.FilterDetachedHolo(radius=12, max_components=2),
]
sub_filters = [
    filters.FilterSubByAtomTypes(min_atom_types=4),
    filters.FilterByHoloOverlap(min_overlap=5),
    filters.FilterByHoloSeqIdentity(min_sequence_identity=0.8),
    filters.FilterSubRmsds(rmsd_cutoff=7.5),
    filters.FilterDetachedSub(radius=12, max_components=2),
]

loader = PinderLoader(
    split="test",
    subset="pinder_af2",
    monomer_priority="holo",
    base_filters=base_filters,
    sub_filters=sub_filters,
)

print(f"Systems after filtering: {len(loader)}")
```

**Sources:** [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:438-480]()

### Usage with Specific System IDs

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

systems = [
    "1df0__A1_Q07009--1df0__B1_Q64537",
    "117e__A1_P00817--117e__B1_P00817",
]

loader = PinderLoader(
    ids=systems,
    monomer_priority="pred",  # Use AlphaFold2 predictions
    fallback_to_holo=True,
)

# Access by index
system, feature, target = loader[0]
```

**Sources:** [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:584-600]()

### Usage with Transforms

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader
from pinder.core.loader import transforms

structure_transforms = [
    transforms.SelectAtomTypes(atom_types=["CA", "N", "C", "O"])
]

loader = PinderLoader(
    split="train",
    monomer_priority="random_mixed",
    structure_transforms_target=structure_transforms,
    structure_transforms_feature=structure_transforms,
)

# Transforms are applied before returning structures
system, feature, target = loader[0]
# feature and target now only contain CA, N, C, O atoms
```

**Sources:** [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:766-803]()

### Usage with Writer

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader
from pinder.core.loader.writer import PinderDefaultWriter
from pathlib import Path

output_dir = Path("/path/to/output")
writer = PinderDefaultWriter(output_dir)

loader = PinderLoader(
    ids=systems,
    monomer_priority="pred",
    writer=writer,
)

# Structures are written to disk during iteration
for system, feature, target in loader:
    system_dir = writer.output_path / system.entry.id
    # PDB files written to system_dir
```

**Sources:** [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:640-673]()

### Usage with Pre-Specified Monomers

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

# Specify exact monomer types for each system
pre_specified = {
    "1df0__A1_Q07009--1df0__B1_Q64537": "apo",
    "117e__A1_P00817--117e__B1_P00817": "pred",
}

loader = PinderLoader(
    ids=list(pre_specified.keys()),
    pre_specified_monomers=pre_specified,
)

# Each system uses its pre-specified monomer type
```

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:327-346]()

## Integration with Datasets

`PinderLoader` serves as the foundation for higher-level dataset implementations:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "PinderLoader"
        LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>Iterator interface<br/>Returns: tuple[PinderSystem, Structure, Structure]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PyTorch Dataset"
        PINDER_DS["PinderDataset<br/>torch.utils.data.Dataset<br/>Returns: dict[str, Tensor]"]
        COLLATE["PinderDataset.collate_fn<br/>Pad and batch tensors"]
        DL["torch.utils.data.DataLoader"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PyTorch Geometric Dataset"
        PPI_DS["PPIDataset<br/>torch_geometric.data.Dataset<br/>Returns: HeteroData"]
        GEO_DL["torch_geometric.loader.DataLoader"]
    end
    
    LOADER --> PINDER_DS
    LOADER --> PPI_DS
    
    PINDER_DS --> COLLATE
    COLLATE --> DL
    
    PPI_DS --> GEO_DL
```

`PinderDataset` and `PPIDataset` both internally use `PinderLoader` to handle system loading, filtering, and monomer selection, while adding their own transformation logic to produce ML-ready data structures.

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:1-439]()

## Iterator Protocol

`PinderLoader` implements the standard Python iterator protocol:

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| `__len__()` | `int` | Number of systems in filtered index |
| `__iter__()` | `Generator` | Yields items by calling `__getitem__` for each index |
| `__getitem__(idx)` | `tuple[PinderSystem, Structure, Structure]` | Loads, filters, and returns system at index |

The `__getitem__` method includes retry logic controlled by `max_load_attempts`. If a system fails filters, a random index is selected and retried up to `max_load_attempts` times before raising an `IndexError`.

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:348-405]()

## Key Functions Reference

### Helper Functions

| Function | Location | Purpose |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `get_systems` | [loader.py:27-34]() | Generator that yields `PinderSystem` objects from ID list |
| `get_available_monomers` | [loader.py:37-53]() | Returns available monomer types for receptor and ligand |
| `get_alternate_apo_codes` | [loader.py:56-78]() | Gets list of alternate apo PDB codes for a dimer side |
| `select_monomer` | [loader.py:81-149]() | Selects monomer types based on priority strategy |
| `_create_target_feature_complex` | [loader.py:152-189]() | Creates target and feature Structure complexes |

### Class Methods

| Method | Location | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `__init__` | [loader.py:193-346]() | Initialize loader with configuration |
| `__len__` | [loader.py:348-349]() | Return number of systems |
| `__iter__` | [loader.py:351-355]() | Iterator protocol implementation |
| `__getitem__` | [loader.py:357-405]() | Load system by index with filtering |
| `apply_structure_filters` | [loader.py:407-413]() | Apply structure-level filters |
| `apply_dimer_filters` | [loader.py:415-435]() | Static method for base/sub filtering |

**Sources:** [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:1-439]()
