# pinder.core.loader

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/geodata.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/geodata.py)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/transforms.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/transforms.py)
- [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/utils/timer.py](src/pinder-core/pinder/core/utils/timer.py)
- [tests/core/loader/test_transforms.py](tests/core/loader/test_transforms.py)

</details>



The `pinder.core.loader` module provides the data loading infrastructure for the PINDER dataset, bridging raw protein structure files to ML-ready tensors and graphs. This module contains iterator classes, PyTorch dataset implementations, filtering utilities, data transformations, and collation functions for batch processing.

For high-level data loading workflows and tutorials, see [Data Loading System](#4). For information about the core data structures that loaders operate on (PinderSystem, Structure), see [Core Data Structures](#3).

## Module Structure

The `pinder.core.loader` package consists of five main modules that work together to provide flexible data loading capabilities:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "pinder.core.loader"
        LOADER["loader.py<br/>PinderLoader iterator<br/>Filtering & sampling"]
        DATASET["dataset.py<br/>PinderDataset (PyTorch)<br/>PPIDataset (PyG)<br/>Collation functions"]
        STRUCTURE["structure.py<br/>Structure wrapper<br/>Atomic operations"]
        TRANSFORMS["transforms.py<br/>SelectAtomTypes<br/>RandomLigandTransform<br/>SuperposeToReference"]
        GEODATA["geodata.py<br/>PairedPDB (HeteroData)<br/>structure2tensor<br/>NodeRepresentation"]
        FILTERS["filters.py<br/>PinderFilterBase<br/>PinderFilterSubBase<br/>StructureFilter"]
        WRITER["writer.py<br/>PinderWriterBase<br/>Output handling"]
    end
    
    LOADER --> FILTERS
    LOADER --> STRUCTURE
    LOADER --> TRANSFORMS
    LOADER --> WRITER
    DATASET --> LOADER
    DATASET --> GEODATA
    DATASET --> STRUCTURE
    GEODATA --> STRUCTURE
    TRANSFORMS --> STRUCTURE
```

**Module Responsibilities:**

| Module | Purpose | Key Classes |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `loader.py` | Core iterator with filtering and monomer selection | `PinderLoader` |
| `dataset.py` | PyTorch/PyG dataset implementations and collation | `PinderDataset`, `PPIDataset` |
| `structure.py` | Structure wrapper and atomic operations | `Structure` |
| `transforms.py` | Data augmentation and preprocessing | `SelectAtomTypes`, `RandomLigandTransform`, `SuperposeToReference` |
| `geodata.py` | Graph representations for GNNs | `PairedPDB`, `NodeRepresentation` |
| `filters.py` | System and structure filtering logic | Multiple filter classes |
| `writer.py` | Output and persistence utilities | `PinderWriterBase` |

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:1-19](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:1-24](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/geodata.py:1-28]()

## PinderLoader

`PinderLoader` is the core orchestration class that manages iterating over PINDER systems, applying filters, selecting monomers, and creating target/feature complex pairs.

```mermaid
graph TB
    INDEX["index.parquet<br/>2.4M+ systems"]
    METADATA["metadata.parquet<br/>Annotations"]
    
    subgraph "PinderLoader Configuration"
        SPLIT["split filter"]
        IDS["id filter"]
        QUERIES["index/metadata queries"]
        MONOMER_PRI["monomer_priority<br/>holo/apo/pred/random"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Filtering Pipeline"
        BASE_FILT["base_filters<br/>PinderFilterBase<br/>System-level"]
        SUB_FILT["sub_filters<br/>PinderFilterSubBase<br/>Monomer-level"]
        STRUCT_FILT["structure_filters<br/>StructureFilter<br/>Atom/residue-level"]
    end
    
    subgraph "System Processing"
        PINDER_SYS["PinderSystem<br/>Load structures"]
        SELECT_MON["select_monomer()<br/>Choose R/L monomers"]
        CREATE_PAIR["_create_target_feature_complex()<br/>target: holo R+L<br/>feature: selected R+L"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transform Pipeline"
        TARGET_TRANS["structure_transforms_target"]
        FEATURE_TRANS["structure_transforms_feature"]
    end
    
    OUTPUT["tuple[PinderSystem, Structure, Structure]<br/>system, feature_complex, target_complex"]
    
    INDEX --> SPLIT
    METADATA --> QUERIES
    SPLIT --> IDS
    IDS --> QUERIES
    
    QUERIES --> BASE_FILT
    BASE_FILT --> SUB_FILT
    SUB_FILT --> STRUCT_FILT
    
    STRUCT_FILT --> PINDER_SYS
    MONOMER_PRI --> SELECT_MON
    PINDER_SYS --> SELECT_MON
    SELECT_MON --> CREATE_PAIR
    
    CREATE_PAIR --> TARGET_TRANS
    CREATE_PAIR --> FEATURE_TRANS
    
    TARGET_TRANS --> OUTPUT
    FEATURE_TRANS --> OUTPUT
```

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:192-439]()

### Initialization Parameters

The `PinderLoader.__init__()` method accepts extensive configuration for filtering and processing:

**Core Parameters:**
- `split` (str): Dataset split - "train", "val", "test" 
- `ids` (list[str]): Specific system IDs to load
- `index` (pd.DataFrame): Pre-filtered index (default: loads via `get_index()`)
- `metadata` (pd.DataFrame): Pre-filtered metadata (default: loads via `get_metadata()`)
- `subset` (DatasetName): Test subset - pinder_xl, pinder_s, or pinder_af2

**Filtering Parameters:**
- `base_filters` (list[PinderFilterBase]): System-level filters
- `sub_filters` (list[PinderFilterSubBase]): Monomer-level filters  
- `structure_filters` (list[StructureFilter]): Structure-level filters
- `index_query` (str): Pandas query string for index
- `metadata_query` (str): Pandas query string for metadata

**Monomer Selection Parameters:**
- `monomer_priority` (str): "holo", "apo", "pred", "random", or "random_mixed"
- `fallback_to_holo` (bool): Fall back to holo when priority unavailable (default: True)
- `use_canonical_apo` (bool): Use canonical vs alternate apo (default: True)
- `pre_specified_monomers` (dict | DataFrame): Override monomer selection per system

**Processing Parameters:**
- `crop_equal_monomer_shapes` (bool): Crop to common atoms (default: True)
- `max_load_attempts` (int): Retries before IndexError (default: 10)
- `structure_transforms_target` (list[StructureTransform]): Target transformations
- `structure_transforms_feature` (list[StructureTransform]): Feature transformations
- `writer` (PinderWriterBase): Optional output writer

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:193-265]()

### Monomer Selection Logic

The `select_monomer()` function implements flexible monomer selection strategies:

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["select_monomer(row, monomer_priority)"]
    GET_AVAIL["get_available_monomers(row)<br/>Returns available types per side"]
    
    CHECK_PRIORITY{"monomer_priority?"}
    
    RANDOM_MIXED["random_mixed<br/>Independent random<br/>for R and L"]
    RANDOM["random<br/>Same random type<br/>for R and L"]
    SPECIFIED["holo/apo/pred<br/>Use specified type<br/>for both R and L"]
    
    CHECK_AVAIL{"Type available<br/>for both R/L?"}
    FALLBACK{"fallback_to_holo?"}
    USE_HOLO["Use holo for both"]
    ERROR["Raise ValueError"]
    
    CHECK_CANONICAL{"use_canonical_apo?"}
    SELECT_ALT["get_alternate_apo_codes()<br/>Select random alternate"]
    USE_CANONICAL["Use canonical apo"]
    
    RETURN["Return dict[str, str]<br/>{R: type, L: type}"]
    
    START --> GET_AVAIL
    GET_AVAIL --> CHECK_PRIORITY
    
    CHECK_PRIORITY -->|random_mixed| RANDOM_MIXED
    CHECK_PRIORITY -->|random| RANDOM
    CHECK_PRIORITY -->|holo/apo/pred| SPECIFIED
    
    RANDOM_MIXED --> RETURN
    RANDOM --> RETURN
    
    SPECIFIED --> CHECK_AVAIL
    CHECK_AVAIL -->|Yes| RETURN
    CHECK_AVAIL -->|No| FALLBACK
    
    FALLBACK -->|True| USE_HOLO
    FALLBACK -->|False| ERROR
    
    USE_HOLO --> CHECK_CANONICAL
    SPECIFIED --> CHECK_CANONICAL
    
    CHECK_CANONICAL -->|False| SELECT_ALT
    CHECK_CANONICAL -->|True| USE_CANONICAL
    
    SELECT_ALT --> RETURN
    USE_CANONICAL --> RETURN
```

**Monomer Priority Options:**

| Priority | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `"holo"` | Use bound (holo) structures for both receptor and ligand |
| `"apo"` | Use unbound (apo) structures; fallback to holo if unavailable |
| `"pred"` | Use AlphaFold predicted structures; fallback to holo if unavailable |
| `"random"` | Randomly select same type (holo/apo/pred) for both receptor and ligand |
| `"random_mixed"` | Independently select random types for receptor and ligand |

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:81-149](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:37-78]()

### Indexing and Iteration

The `PinderLoader` implements both indexing (`__getitem__`) and iteration (`__iter__`) protocols:

**Indexing Protocol (`__getitem__`):**
```python
def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> tuple[PinderSystem, Structure, Structure]:
    # Returns: (system, feature_complex, target_complex)
```

The method performs the following sequence:
1. Load system at index with retry logic (up to `max_load_attempts`)
2. Apply `base_filters` and `sub_filters` to PinderSystem
3. Select monomers based on `monomer_priority` or `pre_specified_monomers`
4. Create target (holo R+L) and feature (selected R+L) complexes
5. Apply `structure_filters` to validate complexes
6. Apply `structure_transforms_target` and `structure_transforms_feature`
7. Optionally write to `writer` if configured

If filters reject a system, a random index is selected and the process repeats until a valid system is found or `max_load_attempts` is exhausted.

**Iteration Protocol (`__iter__`):**
```python
def __iter__(self) -> Generator[tuple[PinderSystem, Structure, Structure], None, None]:
    for idx in range(len(self)):
        yield self[idx]
```

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:357-405](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:351-355]()

## PinderDataset

`PinderDataset` is a PyTorch `Dataset` implementation that wraps `PinderLoader` and converts protein structures to dictionary-based tensor representations.

```mermaid
graph TB
    LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>Configured iterator"]
    
    subgraph "PinderDataset"
        GETITEM["__getitem__(idx)<br/>Fetch from loader"]
        TRANSFORM["transform()<br/>Structure → dict[str, Tensor]"]
        TARGET_TRANSFORM["target_transform()<br/>Structure → dict[str, Tensor]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "structure2tensor_transform"
        FILTER_CA["Filter CA atoms<br/>for residue coords"]
        TENSOR_CONV["structure2tensor()<br/>Convert arrays to tensors"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Dictionary"
        FEAT_COMPLEX["feature_complex<br/>Dict of tensors"]
        TARG_COMPLEX["target_complex<br/>Dict of tensors"]
        SYSTEM_ID["id: str<br/>sample_id: str<br/>target_id: str"]
    end
    
    LOADER --> GETITEM
    GETITEM --> TRANSFORM
    GETITEM --> TARGET_TRANSFORM
    
    TRANSFORM --> FILTER_CA
    TARGET_TRANSFORM --> FILTER_CA
    
    FILTER_CA --> TENSOR_CONV
    
    TENSOR_CONV --> FEAT_COMPLEX
    TENSOR_CONV --> TARG_COMPLEX
    
    FEAT_COMPLEX --> SYSTEM_ID
    TARG_COMPLEX --> SYSTEM_ID
```

### Default Transform: structure2tensor_transform

The default transform converts `Structure` objects to dictionaries of tensors containing atomic and residue-level information:

**Output Dictionary Keys:**
- `atom_coordinates`: (N_atoms, 3) - XYZ coordinates of all atoms
- `atom_types`: (N_atoms, 1) - Atom name indices (CA, CB, N, etc.)
- `element_types`: (N_atoms, 1) - Chemical element indices (C, N, O, etc.)
- `residue_coordinates`: (N_residues, 3) - CA atom coordinates  
- `residue_types`: (N_residues, 1) - Amino acid type indices
- `residue_ids`: (N_residues, 1) - Residue numbering
- `chain_ids`: (N_residues, 1) - Chain identifiers (0 for R, 1 for L)

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:55-66](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/geodata.py:30-70]()

### Batching and Collation

`PinderDataset` uses the `collate_batch()` function to merge variable-sized proteins into padded mini-batches:

```mermaid
graph TB
    BATCH_LIST["List of batch items<br/>Each: dict with<br/>target_complex, feature_complex, ids"]
    
    subgraph "collate_batch()"
        SEPARATE["Separate into lists:<br/>target_structures<br/>feature_structures<br/>ids"]
        
        subgraph "collate_complex()"
            EXTRACT["Extract tensors:<br/>atom_coords, atom_types<br/>res_coords, res_types, etc."]
            PAD_STACK["pad_and_stack()<br/>Pad to max length<br/>Stack into batch"]
        end
        
        MERGE["Merge into batch dict"]
    end
    
    OUTPUT["Batch dict:<br/>target_complex: dict[str, Tensor]<br/>feature_complex: dict[str, Tensor]<br/>id, sample_id, target_id: list[str]"]
    
    BATCH_LIST --> SEPARATE
    SEPARATE --> EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> PAD_STACK
    PAD_STACK --> MERGE
    MERGE --> OUTPUT
```

**Padding Values:**

| Tensor Type | Pad Value | Constant |
|-------------|-----------|----------|
| Coordinates | -100 | `COORDS_PAD_VALUE` |
| Atom types | -1 | `ATOM_TYPE_PAD_VALUE` |
| Element types | -1 | `ELEMENT_TYPE_PAD_VALUE` |
| Residue IDs | -99 | `RES_IDX_PAD_VALUE` |
| Chain IDs | -1 | `CHAIN_ID_PAD_VALUE` |

The `pad_and_stack()` function pads each tensor dimension to the maximum observed in the batch, then stacks them along a new batch dimension.

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:205-243](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:122-162](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:165-202]()

### Creating DataLoader

The `get_torch_loader()` helper function creates a configured PyTorch `DataLoader`:

```python
def get_torch_loader(
    dataset: PinderDataset,
    batch_size: int = 2,
    shuffle: bool = True,
    sampler: Sampler[PinderDataset] | None = None,
    num_workers: int = 1,
    collate_fn: Callable = collate_batch,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> DataLoader[PinderDataset]:
```

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:637-654]()

## PPIDataset

`PPIDataset` is a PyTorch Geometric `Dataset` implementation that creates heterogeneous graph representations (`PairedPDB`) for graph neural networks.

```mermaid
graph TB
    PINDER_LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>System iterator"]
    
    subgraph "PPIDataset Processing"
        PROCESS["process() or<br/>process_parallel()"]
        
        subgraph "Per-System Processing"
            FETCH["Fetch system from loader"]
            PRE_FILTER["Apply pre_filter"]
            CREATE_PAIRED["PairedPDB.from_pinder_system()<br/>Create HeteroData"]
            PRE_TRANSFORM["Apply pre_transform"]
            SAVE["torch.save()<br/>Save to processed_dir"]
        end
        
        TRACK["Track processed filenames"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PairedPDB.from_pinder_system"
        GET_MONOMERS["getattr(system, monomer1)<br/>getattr(system, monomer2)"]
        FILTER_H["Filter hydrogen atoms"]
        STRUCTURE_PAIR["from_structure_pair()<br/>Create graph"]
        
        subgraph "Graph Construction"
            CREATE_NODES["Create node features<br/>per NodeRepresentation"]
            ADD_EDGES["knn_graph()<br/>Add edges if enabled"]
        end
    end
    
    GET_ITEM["__getitem__(idx)<br/>torch.load() from cache"]
    
    PINDER_LOADER --> FETCH
    FETCH --> PRE_FILTER
    PRE_FILTER --> CREATE_PAIRED
    
    CREATE_PAIRED --> GET_MONOMERS
    GET_MONOMERS --> FILTER_H
    FILTER_H --> STRUCTURE_PAIR
    STRUCTURE_PAIR --> CREATE_NODES
    CREATE_NODES --> ADD_EDGES
    
    ADD_EDGES --> PRE_TRANSFORM
    PRE_TRANSFORM --> SAVE
    SAVE --> TRACK
    
    TRACK --> GET_ITEM
```

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:320-623](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/geodata.py:79-176]()

### NodeRepresentation Types

The `NodeRepresentation` enum defines three node types for graph construction:

```python
class NodeRepresentation(Enum):
    Surface = "surface"
    Atom = "atom"  
    Residue = "residue"
```

**Graph Structure by Node Type:**

| Node Type | Node Store | Position | Features | Edges (if add_edges=True) |
|-----------|------------|----------|----------|---------------------------|
| Atom | `ligand_atom`, `receptor_atom` | `pos`: (N_atoms, 3) | `x`: atom type indices | k-NN graph (k=10) |
| Residue | `ligand_residue`, `receptor_residue` | `pos`: (N_residues, 3) | `residueid`: amino acid indices | k-NN graph (k=10) |

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/geodata.py:73-76](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/geodata.py:109-176]()

### PairedPDB Structure

`PairedPDB` is a `HeteroData` object containing separate node stores for receptor and ligand:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "PairedPDB (HeteroData)"
        subgraph "Receptor Nodes"
            REC_ATOM["receptor_atom<br/>x: atom types<br/>pos: coordinates<br/>edge_index: k-NN"]
            REC_RES["receptor_residue<br/>residueid: AA types<br/>pos: CA coordinates<br/>edge_index: k-NN<br/>chain: tensor([R_id])"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Ligand Nodes"
            LIG_ATOM["ligand_atom<br/>x: atom types<br/>pos: coordinates<br/>edge_index: k-NN"]
            LIG_RES["ligand_residue<br/>residueid: AA types<br/>pos: CA coordinates<br/>edge_index: k-NN<br/>chain: tensor([L_id])"]
        end
        
        PDB_META["pdb metadata<br/>id: batch index<br/>num_nodes: 1"]
    end
```

The k-NN graph construction uses the `torch_cluster.knn_graph()` function to connect each node to its k nearest neighbors (default k=10).

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/geodata.py:79-176]()

### Processing Modes

`PPIDataset` supports three processing modes:

**Sequential Processing:**
```python
dataset = PPIDataset(
    node_types={NodeRepresentation.Atom, NodeRepresentation.Residue},
    split="train",
    parallel=False,
)
```

**Parallel Processing:**
```python
dataset = PPIDataset(
    node_types={NodeRepresentation.Atom, NodeRepresentation.Residue},
    split="train", 
    parallel=True,
    max_workers=4,
)
```

**Using Cache:**
```python
dataset = PPIDataset(
    node_types={NodeRepresentation.Atom, NodeRepresentation.Residue},
    split="train",
    use_cache=True,  # Load from existing processed files
)
```

When `use_cache=True`, the dataset reads filenames from `filenames_dir/filenames.txt` instead of reprocessing systems.

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:511-594]()

### Creating Geometric DataLoader

The `get_geo_loader()` helper function creates a PyTorch Geometric `DataLoader`:

```python
def get_geo_loader(
    dataset: PPIDataset,
    batch_size: int = 2,
    num_workers: int = 1,
) -> TorchGeoDataLoader:
```

PyTorch Geometric handles batching of heterogeneous graphs automatically by concatenating node/edge tensors and maintaining batch indices.

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:625-634]()

## Transform System

The transform system provides data augmentation and preprocessing capabilities through the `StructureTransform` base class.

```mermaid
graph TB
    BASE["StructureTransform<br/>Abstract base class"]
    
    subgraph "Transform Implementations"
        SELECT["SelectAtomTypes<br/>Filter to specific atoms"]
        RANDOM["RandomLigandTransform<br/>Random rotation/translation"]
        SUPERPOSE["SuperposeToReference<br/>Align to reference"]
    end
    
    subgraph "SelectAtomTypes Usage"
        ATOMS_IN["Structure<br/>All atoms"]
        FILTER_OP["filter('atom_name', atom_types)"]
        ATOMS_OUT["Structure<br/>Filtered atoms"]
    end
    
    subgraph "RandomLigandTransform Usage"
        COMPLEX_IN["Structure<br/>R chain + L chain"]
        SPLIT["Split by chain_id"]
        ROT_TRANS["Random rotation matrix<br/>Random translation vector"]
        TRANSFORM_L["Transform L chain only"]
        RECOMBINE["Combine R + L"]
        COMPLEX_OUT["Structure<br/>R (unchanged) + L (transformed)"]
    end
    
    BASE --> SELECT
    BASE --> RANDOM
    BASE --> SUPERPOSE
    
    SELECT --> ATOMS_IN
    ATOMS_IN --> FILTER_OP
    FILTER_OP --> ATOMS_OUT
    
    RANDOM --> COMPLEX_IN
    COMPLEX_IN --> SPLIT
    SPLIT --> ROT_TRANS
    ROT_TRANS --> TRANSFORM_L
    TRANSFORM_L --> RECOMBINE
    RECOMBINE --> COMPLEX_OUT
```

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/transforms.py:20-95]()

### SelectAtomTypes

Filters structures to specific atom types (e.g., CA, backbone, heavy atoms):

```python
class SelectAtomTypes(StructureTransform):
    def __init__(self, atom_types: list[str] = ["CA"]) -> None:
        self.atom_types = atom_types
    
    def transform(self, structure: Structure) -> Structure:
        return structure.filter("atom_name", self.atom_types)
```

**Common Use Cases:**
- `atom_types=["CA"]`: C-alpha only representation
- `atom_types=["CA", "N", "C", "O"]`: Backbone atoms
- `atom_types=["C", "N", "O", "S"]`: Heavy atoms only

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/transforms.py:31-36]()

### RandomLigandTransform

Applies random rigid-body transformations to the ligand chain for data augmentation:

```python
class RandomLigandTransform(StructureTransform):
    def __init__(self, max_translation: float = 10.0) -> None:
        self.max_translation = max_translation
    
    def transform(self, structure: Structure) -> Structure:
        # Applies random rotation + translation to chain L
        # Keeps chain R unchanged
```

The transformation process:
1. Extract ligand atoms (chain_id == "L")
2. Generate random rotation matrix via `scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation.random()`
3. Generate random translation vector scaled by `max_translation`
4. Apply transformation: `coords = (rotation @ (coords - centroid).T).T + centroid + translation`
5. Recombine with unchanged receptor atoms

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/transforms.py:66-95]()

### SuperposeToReference

Aligns apo and predicted structures to holo reference structures:

```python
class SuperposeToReference(TransformBase):
    def __init__(self, reference_type: str = "holo") -> None:
        # reference_type: "holo" or "native"
    
    def transform(self, ppi: PinderSystem) -> PinderSystem:
        # Superimposes apo_receptor/ligand and pred_receptor/ligand
        # to holo_receptor/ligand using structure.superimpose()
```

This transform operates on `PinderSystem` objects rather than individual `Structure` objects, ensuring all unbound structures are aligned to their bound references before complex formation.

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/transforms.py:39-63]()

## Structure Class

The `Structure` class wraps biotite's `AtomArray` with additional functionality for filtering, alignment, and property access. For complete API documentation, see [Structure Class](#3.2).

### Key Properties and Methods

**Properties:**
- `coords`: NDArray - Atomic coordinates (N, 3)
- `atom_array`: AtomArray - Underlying biotite structure
- `atom_names`: list[str] - Atom names (CA, CB, etc.)
- `pinder_id`: str - Associated system identifier

**Methods:**
- `filter(property, mask, negate, copy)`: Filter atoms by property
- `superimpose(reference)`: Align to reference structure via RMSD minimization
- `ca_alignment(reference)`: Align C-alpha atoms only
- `match_length(reference)`: Crop to common atom set

The `Structure` class is instantiated by `PinderSystem` when loading protein structures from PDB files.

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/structure.py:1-500]() (file not provided but referenced in imports)

## Usage Examples

### Basic PinderDataset

```python
from pinder.core.loader import PinderDataset, get_torch_loader

# Create dataset
dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    monomer_priority="apo",
    fallback_to_holo=True,
)

# Create dataloader  
loader = get_torch_loader(
    dataset,
    batch_size=8,
    num_workers=4,
)

# Iterate
for batch in loader:
    target = batch["target_complex"]  # dict of tensors
    feature = batch["feature_complex"]  # dict of tensors
    ids = batch["id"]  # list of system IDs
```

### Dataset with Filtering

```python
from pinder.core.loader import PinderDataset
from pinder.core.loader.filters import FilterByMissingHolo

dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    base_filters=[FilterByMissingHolo()],
    index_query='cluster_id_R != cluster_id_L',  # Remove self-interactions
)
```

### Dataset with Transforms

```python
from pinder.core.loader import PinderDataset
from pinder.core.loader.transforms import SelectAtomTypes, RandomLigandTransform

dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    structure_transforms_target=[SelectAtomTypes(["CA"])],
    structure_transforms_feature=[
        SelectAtomTypes(["CA"]),
        RandomLigandTransform(max_translation=5.0),
    ],
)
```

### Graph Dataset for GNNs

```python
from pinder.core.loader import PPIDataset, get_geo_loader
from pinder.core.loader.geodata import NodeRepresentation

dataset = PPIDataset(
    node_types={NodeRepresentation.Atom, NodeRepresentation.Residue},
    split="train",
    monomer1="apo_receptor",
    monomer2="apo_ligand",
    add_edges=True,
    k=10,
)

loader = get_geo_loader(dataset, batch_size=16)

for batch in loader:
    # Access graph components
    receptor_pos = batch["receptor_atom"].pos
    ligand_pos = batch["ligand_atom"].pos  
    edges = batch["receptor_atom"].edge_index
```

### Direct PinderLoader Usage

```python  
from pinder.core.loader import PinderLoader

loader = PinderLoader(
    split="val",
    monomer_priority="pred",
)

for system, feature_complex, target_complex in loader:
    # system: PinderSystem object
    # feature_complex: Structure with pred monomers
    # target_complex: Structure with holo monomers
    pass
```

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:246-318](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py:320-404](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py:192-439]()

# Page: pinder.data

# pinder.data

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)
- [src/pinder-data/pinder/data/pipeline/tasks.py](src/pinder-data/pinder/data/pipeline/tasks.py)
- [tests/data/test_get_data.py](tests/data/test_get_data.py)
- [tests/data/test_graphql.py](tests/data/test_graphql.py)
- [tests/data/test_tasks.py](tests/data/test_tasks.py)

</details>



The `pinder.data` package is responsible for generating the PINDER dataset from raw RCSB PDB data. It orchestrates the download of mmCIF files, processes biological assemblies, identifies interacting chains, annotates structures with domain and functional information, and produces the curated index and metadata files that power the core PINDER system.

For information about using the generated dataset, see [pinder.core](#9.1). For evaluation tools, see [pinder.eval](#9.4).

## Purpose and Scope

The `pinder.data` pipeline transforms raw PDB structures into a structured dataset suitable for protein-protein docking research. Key responsibilities include:

- **Data acquisition** from RCSB PDB via rsync
- **Biological assembly generation** from mmCIF coordinate files
- **Interacting chain identification** based on spatial proximity and buried surface area
- **Metadata extraction** including resolution, method, oligomeric state
- **Annotation enrichment** with Pfam, ECOD, SCOP, and CATH domain classifications
- **Task orchestration** for parallel processing of thousands of structures
- **Quality control** and dataset curation

This package is typically used by PINDER maintainers to regenerate the dataset rather than by end users who consume the pre-generated data.

Sources: [pyproject.toml:38-47](), [tests/data/test_get_data.py:1-368]()

## Architecture Overview

The pipeline follows a multi-stage architecture where each stage processes inputs from the previous stage and produces outputs consumed by the next.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Stage 1: Download"
        RSYNC["rcsb_rsync.download_two_char_codes()"]
        MMCIF["mmCIF Files<br/>*_xyz-enrich.cif.gz"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Process"
        PROCESS["get_data.process_mmcif()"]
        BIOASM["generate_bio_assembly()"]
        ENTITIES["get_entities()"]
        CHAINS["get_interacting_chains()"]
        METADATA["get_metadata()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Annotate"
        GRAPHQL["graphql.fetch_entry_annotations()"]
        PFAM["Pfam domains"]
        FEATURES["Structural features"]
        ANNOTS["ECOD/SCOP/CATH"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 4: Aggregate"
        COLLECT["graphql.collect_rcsb_annotations()"]
        INDEX["index.parquet"]
        META["metadata.parquet"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task Orchestration"
        TASKS["tasks.get_stage_tasks()"]
        CACHE["cache.get_uningested_mmcif()"]
        SCATTER["scatter.chunk_collection()"]
        RUN["tasks.run_task()"]
    end
    
    RSYNC --> MMCIF
    MMCIF --> PROCESS
    PROCESS --> BIOASM
    BIOASM --> ENTITIES
    BIOASM --> CHAINS
    PROCESS --> METADATA
    
    ENTITIES --> GRAPHQL
    GRAPHQL --> PFAM
    GRAPHQL --> FEATURES
    GRAPHQL --> ANNOTS
    
    PFAM --> COLLECT
    FEATURES --> COLLECT
    ANNOTS --> COLLECT
    METADATA --> COLLECT
    
    COLLECT --> INDEX
    COLLECT --> META
    
    TASKS --> CACHE
    CACHE --> SCATTER
    SCATTER --> RUN
    RUN --> PROCESS
```

Sources: [tests/data/test_get_data.py:12-368](), [tests/data/test_graphql.py:1-100]()

## Data Acquisition from RCSB

The pipeline downloads mmCIF files from RCSB PDB using rsync, organizing them by two-character codes derived from PDB IDs.

### Two-Character Code Organization

RCSB organizes structures using the middle two characters of the PDB ID. For example, PDB entry `7cm8` is stored under directory `cm/pdb_00007cm8/`.

```mermaid
graph LR
    RCSB["RCSB PDB<br/>rsync server"]
    DIRS["rsync directories<br/>get_rsync_directories()"]
    CODES["two_char_codes<br/>['1a', 'cm', 'fa', ...]"]
    DOWNLOAD["download_two_char_codes()"]
    LOCAL["local filesystem<br/>nextgen_rcsb/cm/pdb_00007cm8/"]
    
    RCSB --> DIRS
    DIRS --> CODES
    CODES --> DOWNLOAD
    DOWNLOAD --> LOCAL
```

### Key Functions

| Function | Purpose | Location |
|----------|---------|----------|
| `get_rsync_directories()` | Lists available two-character codes on RCSB server | [rcsb_rsync module]() |
| `get_rsync_two_char_pdb_entries()` | Lists PDB entries for a specific two-character code | [rcsb_rsync module]() |
| `download_two_char_codes()` | Downloads all mmCIF files for specified codes | [rcsb_rsync module]() |
| `get_two_char_codes_not_downloaded()` | Identifies missing two-character codes | [rcsb_rsync module]() |

Sources: [tests/data/test_get_data.py:12-38](), [src/pinder-data/pinder/data/pipeline/tasks.py:36-41]()

## mmCIF Processing Pipeline

The core processing logic extracts biological assemblies, identifies entities, and detects interacting chains from mmCIF coordinate files.

### Biological Assembly Generation

The `generate_bio_assembly()` function reads the `_pdbx_struct_assembly*` categories from mmCIF files and applies transformation matrices to create the biological assembly.

```mermaid
graph TB
    MMCIF["mmCIF file<br/>_xyz-enrich.cif.gz"]
    READ["read_mmcif_file()"]
    PDBX["pdbx_file object"]
    BIOASM["generate_bio_assembly()"]
    ASSEMBLY["bio_asm: AtomArray"]
    ENTITY_MAP["entity_map: DataFrame"]
    
    MMCIF --> READ
    READ --> PDBX
    PDBX --> BIOASM
    BIOASM --> ASSEMBLY
    BIOASM --> ENTITY_MAP
    
    ENTITY_MAP --> |"chain_id -> asym_id"| MAPPING["chain/asym_id mapping"]
    ENTITY_MAP --> |"asym_id -> entity_id"| ENTITIES["entity assignments"]
```

The `entity_map` DataFrame maps assembly chains to asymmetric unit IDs and entity IDs, which is crucial for tracking chains across transformations.

Sources: [tests/data/test_get_data.py:242-362]()

### Entity Extraction

The `get_entities()` function extracts information about molecular entities from the mmCIF file, including chain assignments, entity types, and sequence information.

```mermaid
graph LR
    PDBX["pdbx_file"]
    ENTITIES["get_entities()"]
    DF["DataFrame"]
    
    PDBX --> ENTITIES
    ENTITIES --> DF
    
    DF --> COLS["Columns:<br/>entity_id<br/>asym_id<br/>pdb_strand_id<br/>chain<br/>entry_id"]
```

Sources: [tests/data/test_get_data.py:107-149]()

### Interacting Chain Detection

The `get_interacting_chains()` function identifies pairs of chains that interact based on spatial proximity and calculates buried surface area (SASA).

```mermaid
graph TB
    BIOASM["bio_asm: AtomArray"]
    ENTITIES["entities: DataFrame"]
    PARAMS["Parameters:<br/>contact_threshold=5.0<br/>backbone_only=False"]
    
    INTERACTING["get_interacting_chains()"]
    
    CONTACTS["Contact Detection<br/>atom pairs within threshold"]
    SASA["SASA Calculation<br/>buried_sasa"]
    RESIDUES["Residue Counting<br/>n_residue_pairs"]
    
    OUTPUT["DataFrame:<br/>chain_1, chain_2<br/>asym_id_1, asym_id_2<br/>pdb_strand_id_1/2<br/>n_residue_pairs<br/>n_residues<br/>buried_sasa<br/>chain_1/2_residues"]
    
    BIOASM --> INTERACTING
    ENTITIES --> INTERACTING
    PARAMS --> INTERACTING
    
    INTERACTING --> CONTACTS
    INTERACTING --> SASA
    INTERACTING --> RESIDUES
    
    CONTACTS --> OUTPUT
    SASA --> OUTPUT
    RESIDUES --> OUTPUT
```

The function supports two modes:
- **`backbone_only=False`**: Considers all atoms for contact detection
- **`backbone_only=True`**: Only considers backbone atoms (CA, C, N, O)

Sources: [tests/data/test_get_data.py:40-163]()

### Complete Processing Workflow

The `process_mmcif()` function orchestrates the complete processing of a single mmCIF file.

| Step | Function | Output |
|------|----------|--------|
| 1. Read file | `read_mmcif_file()` | `pdbx_file` object |
| 2. Generate assembly | `generate_bio_assembly()` | `bio_asm` AtomArray, `entity_map` |
| 3. Extract entities | `get_entities()` | Entity DataFrame |
| 4. Map sequences | `sequence_mapping()` | Residue-level mapping |
| 5. Find interactions | `get_interacting_chains()` | Interacting chain pairs |
| 6. Extract metadata | `get_metadata()` | Resolution, method, dates |
| 7. Write outputs | File I/O | `{pdb_id}-metadata.tsv`, `{pdb_id}-assembly.cif` |

Sources: [tests/data/test_get_data.py:217-240](), [tests/data/test_get_data.py:364-368]()

## Annotation Pipeline

The annotation system enriches structures with domain classifications and functional information from RCSB using GraphQL queries.

### GraphQL Data Fetching

The `fetch_entry_annotations()` function queries the RCSB GraphQL API to retrieve comprehensive annotations for a PDB entry.

```mermaid
graph TB
    PDB_ID["pdb_id: '6Q0R'"]
    GRAPHQL["graphql.fetch_entry_annotations()"]
    API["RCSB GraphQL API<br/>data.rcsb.org/graphql"]
    JSON["annotation JSON file"]
    
    PARSE["parse_annotation_data()"]
    
    PFAM["pfam_df<br/>Domain annotations<br/>19 columns"]
    FEATURES["feature_df<br/>Structural features<br/>14 columns<br/>ASA, HELIX_P, SHEET, BINDING_SITE"]
    ANNOTS["annotation_df<br/>ECOD/SCOP/CATH<br/>12 columns"]
    EC["ec_df<br/>EC numbers"]
    
    PDB_ID --> GRAPHQL
    GRAPHQL --> API
    API --> JSON
    JSON --> PARSE
    
    PARSE --> PFAM
    PARSE --> FEATURES
    PARSE --> ANNOTS
    PARSE --> EC
```

### Annotation Types

| Annotation Type | Description | Column Count | Example Fields |
|-----------------|-------------|--------------|----------------|
| Pfam | Protein family domains | 19 | `rcsb_id`, `rcsb_pfam_identifier`, `pfam_accession` |
| Features | Structural features | 14 | `type`, `asym_id`, `beg_seq_id`, `end_seq_id` |
| Annotations | Domain classifications | 12 | `annotation_id`, `name`, `type`, `provenance_source` |
| EC | Enzyme classifications | Variable | `ec_number`, `enzyme_name` |

**Feature Types** include:
- `ASA` - Accessible surface area
- `HELIX_P`, `SHEET` - Secondary structure
- `BINDING_SITE` - Ligand binding sites
- `SCOP`, `SCOP2B_SUPERFAMILY`, `CATH`, `ECOD` - Domain classifications
- `UNOBSERVED_RESIDUE_XYZ`, `UNOBSERVED_ATOM_XYZ` - Missing coordinates
- `CIS-PEPTIDE` - Unusual peptide bonds

Sources: [tests/data/test_graphql.py:13-64]()

### Batch Annotation Processing

The `populate_rcsb_annotations()` function processes multiple PDB entries in parallel.

```mermaid
graph LR
    PDB_IDS["pdb_ids: list<br/>['6Q0R', '2A79', ...]"]
    POPULATE["populate_rcsb_annotations()"]
    WORKERS["parallel=True<br/>max_workers=2"]
    
    DIRS["Output directories:<br/>rcsb_annotations/pfam/<br/>rcsb_annotations/features/<br/>rcsb_annotations/annotations/"]
    
    FILES["Individual CSV files:<br/>{pdb_id}.csv.gz"]
    
    COLLECT["collect_rcsb_annotations()"]
    
    AGGREGATED["Aggregated files:<br/>pfam.csv.gz<br/>annotations_ecod.csv.gz<br/>annotations_scop.csv.gz<br/>annotations_cath.csv.gz<br/>features_*.csv.gz"]
    
    PDB_IDS --> POPULATE
    WORKERS --> POPULATE
    POPULATE --> DIRS
    DIRS --> FILES
    FILES --> COLLECT
    COLLECT --> AGGREGATED
```

Sources: [tests/data/test_graphql.py:66-100]()

## Task Orchestration System

The task orchestration system manages the parallel processing of thousands of structures through a batching and caching mechanism.

### Task Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    INPUT["Input Type<br/>'cif', 'dimers', 'pdb_ids'"]
    
    GLOB["get_stage_inputs()<br/>DATA_GLOBS[input_type]"]
    
    GLOBS["Available glob functions:<br/>cif_glob()<br/>dimer_glob()<br/>entry_glob()<br/>pdb_id_glob()<br/>foldseek_pdb_glob()<br/>graph_type_glob()"]
    
    INPUTS["inputs: list<br/>Paths or strings"]
    
    CACHE["cache_func()<br/>Filter already processed"]
    
    REMAINING["remaining: list<br/>Unprocessed inputs"]
    
    SCATTER["scatter_method()<br/>chunk_collection()"]
    
    BATCHES["batches: list[list]<br/>batch_size groups"]
    
    RUN["run_task()<br/>task_func(**task_input)"]
    
    INPUT --> GLOB
    GLOB --> GLOBS
    GLOBS --> INPUTS
    INPUTS --> CACHE
    CACHE --> REMAINING
    REMAINING --> SCATTER
    SCATTER --> BATCHES
    BATCHES --> RUN
```

### Stage Task Generation

The `get_stage_tasks()` function orchestrates the creation of task batches for a pipeline stage.

| Parameter | Type | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `data_dir` | `Path` | Root directory for data files |
| `input_type` | `str` | Type of input: 'cif', 'dimers', 'pdb_ids', etc. |
| `batch_size` | `int` | Number of inputs per batch |
| `cache_func` | `Callable` | Function to filter processed inputs |
| `cache_kwargs` | `dict` | Arguments for cache function |
| `scatter_method` | `Callable` | Function to split into batches (default: `chunk_collection`) |
| `scatter_kwargs` | `dict` | Arguments for scatter function |

Sources: [src/pinder-data/pinder/data/pipeline/tasks.py:117-138]()

### Task Execution

The `run_task()` function validates and executes a task function with proper error handling.

```mermaid
graph TB
    FUNC["task_func: Callable"]
    INPUT["task_input: dict"]
    ITER["iterable_kwarg: str | None"]
    
    INSPECT["Inspect function signature"]
    VALIDATE["Validate required arguments"]
    
    CHECK["Check iterable_kwarg length"]
    SKIP["Skip if empty"]
    
    EXECUTE["Execute task_func(**task_input)"]
    
    FUNC --> INSPECT
    INPUT --> INSPECT
    INSPECT --> VALIDATE
    VALIDATE --> CHECK
    ITER --> CHECK
    CHECK --> SKIP
    CHECK --> EXECUTE
```

The function performs signature validation to ensure all required parameters are provided before execution.

Sources: [src/pinder-data/pinder/data/pipeline/tasks.py:141-182](), [tests/data/test_tasks.py:95-104]()

### Available Input Types

The `DATA_GLOBS` dictionary maps input type names to glob functions:

```python
DATA_GLOBS = {
    "cif": cif_glob,                    # mmCIF files: */*/*enrich.cif.gz
    "dimers": dimer_glob,               # Dimer PDB files: */*/*__*--*__*.pdb
    "entries": entry_glob,              # Entry directories
    "two_char_codes": two_char_code_rsync,  # RCSB two-char codes to download
    "pdb_ids": pdb_id_glob,            # PDB IDs from entry directories
    "foldseek": foldseek_pdb_glob,     # Foldseek input PDBs: *.pdb
    "graph_types": graph_type_glob,    # Alignment graph types
    "putative_apo_pairings": putative_apo_pairings,  # Apo/holo pairings
}
```

Sources: [src/pinder-data/pinder/data/pipeline/tasks.py:87-96]()

### Caching Mechanism

Cache functions filter out already-processed inputs to avoid redundant work. Example cache functions:

| Cache Function | Purpose | Module |
|----------------|---------|--------|
| `get_uningested_mmcif()` | Find mmCIF files not yet processed | `cache` module |
| `get_pisa_unannotated()` | Find structures missing PISA annotations | `cache` module |
| `get_rcsb_unannotated()` | Find structures missing RCSB annotations | `cache` module |

Sources: [tests/data/test_tasks.py:22-93]()

# Page: pinder.eval

# pinder.eval

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)

</details>



The `pinder.eval` package provides a complete evaluation harness for assessing protein-protein docking methods against the PINDER benchmark datasets. It implements community-standard CAPRI metrics and provides both programmatic APIs and command-line tools for computing docking quality scores.

For information about using the evaluation harness in practice, see [Evaluation](#6). For details on the CAPRI metrics themselves, see [Metrics](#6.2). For information about the benchmark test sets being evaluated against, see [Benchmark Test Sets](#6.3).

## Package Structure

The `pinder.eval` package is organized as a separate namespace package under the `pinder` umbrella. It contains modules for:

- **Evaluation orchestration**: Running evaluation pipelines over predicted structures
- **Metrics calculation**: Computing CAPRI metrics (DockQ, iRMS, LRMS, Fnat)
- **Method scoring**: Aggregating metrics across systems for leaderboard generation
- **Submission creation**: Utilities for preparing method predictions in the expected format

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "pinder.eval Package"
        RUN["pinder.eval.run<br/>Evaluation orchestration"]
        DOCKQ["pinder.eval.dockq<br/>DockQ implementation"]
        METHOD["pinder.eval.dockq.method<br/>MethodMetrics class"]
        SUBMIT["pinder.eval.create_submission<br/>Submission utilities"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CLI Entry Points"
        EVAL_CLI["pinder_eval<br/>Main evaluation CLI"]
        SUBMIT_CLI["pinder_create_submission<br/>Submission creation CLI"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Concepts"
        DECOYS["Decoy Structures<br/>Predicted complexes"]
        NATIVE["Native Structures<br/>Ground truth from PINDER"]
        METRICS["CAPRI Metrics<br/>iRMS, LRMS, Fnat, DockQ"]
    end
    
    EVAL_CLI -->|"calls"| RUN
    SUBMIT_CLI -->|"calls"| SUBMIT
    
    RUN -->|"uses"| DOCKQ
    RUN -->|"uses"| METHOD
    
    DOCKQ -->|"compares"| DECOYS
    DOCKQ -->|"against"| NATIVE
    DOCKQ -->|"produces"| METRICS
    
    METHOD -->|"aggregates"| METRICS
    METHOD -->|"generates"| LEADERBOARD["Leaderboard Results"]
```

**Sources**: [README.md:300-380](), [pyproject.toml:41-42]()

## Core Components

### Evaluation Workflow

The evaluation system follows a structured workflow for processing method predictions and computing scores:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Structure"
        EVAL_DIR["Evaluation Directory<br/>method_name/system_id/monomer_type_decoys/"]
        INDEX["PINDER Index<br/>Ground truth reference"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        LOAD["Load Predictions<br/>Parse decoy PDB files"]
        EXTRACT["Extract Chains<br/>R=Receptor, L=Ligand"]
        ALIGN["Structure Alignment<br/>Superpose to native"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Metrics Computation"
        IRMS["Interface RMSD<br/>iRMS calculation"]
        LRMS["Ligand RMSD<br/>LRMS calculation"]
        FNAT["Fraction Native<br/>Fnat calculation"]
        DOCKQ_CALC["DockQ Score<br/>Combined metric"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        CAPRI["CAPRI Classification<br/>Incorrect/Acceptable/Medium/High"]
        RANKINGS["Per-System Rankings<br/>Best model selection"]
        AGGREGATE["Aggregated Metrics<br/>Leaderboard-ready CSV"]
    end
    
    EVAL_DIR --> LOAD
    INDEX --> LOAD
    
    LOAD --> EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> ALIGN
    
    ALIGN --> IRMS
    ALIGN --> LRMS
    ALIGN --> FNAT
    
    IRMS --> DOCKQ_CALC
    LRMS --> DOCKQ_CALC
    FNAT --> DOCKQ_CALC
    
    DOCKQ_CALC --> CAPRI
    DOCKQ_CALC --> RANKINGS
    RANKINGS --> AGGREGATE
```

**Sources**: [README.md:300-327]()

### Directory Structure Requirements

The evaluation harness expects a specific directory organization for method predictions:

| Level | Component | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| Root | `eval_dir/` | Top-level evaluation directory |
| Method | `method_name/` | Subdirectory for each method being evaluated |
| System | `system_id/` | Subdirectory for each PINDER system (e.g., `1an1__A1_P00761--1an1__B1_P80424`) |
| Monomer Type | `holo_decoys/`, `apo_decoys/`, `predicted_decoys/` | Predictions grouped by input monomer type |
| Decoys | `model_<rank>.pdb` | Individual predicted structures with extractable rank |

**Sources**: [README.md:328-363]()

### Chain Naming Convention

All decoy models must follow a strict chain naming convention:

- **Chain R**: Receptor protein
- **Chain L**: Ligand protein

Each decoy PDB file must contain exactly two chains with these identifiers. The evaluation system uses these chain IDs to map predictions to ground truth structures.

**Sources**: [README.md:362]()

## CLI Tools

### pinder_eval

The main evaluation command-line interface for scoring method predictions:

```bash
pinder_eval --eval_dir <path> \
    --method_name <name> \
    --serial \
    --allow_missing \
    --custom_index <index_path> \
    --max_workers <n>
```

**Arguments**:

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `--eval_dir`, `-f` | path | Yes | Path to evaluation directory containing method predictions |
| `--method_name`, `-m`, `-n` | string | No | Optional name for output CSV file |
| `--serial`, `-s` | flag | No | Disable parallel evaluation over systems (use single process) |
| `--allow_missing`, `-a` | flag | No | Allow missing systems without failing (applies penalty scores) |
| `--custom_index`, `-c` | path | No | Path to custom index with non-PINDER splits (must follow PINDER schema) |
| `--max_workers`, `-w` | int | No | Maximum number of processes for multiprocessing (default: all cores) |

**Entry Point**: [pyproject.toml:41]() - `pinder.eval.run:main`

**Sources**: [README.md:307-326]()

### pinder_create_submission

Utility for creating properly formatted submission directories:

```bash
pinder_create_submission [options]
```

**Entry Point**: [pyproject.toml:42]() - `pinder.eval.create_submission:main`

**Sources**: [pyproject.toml:42]()

## Metrics Implementation

### CAPRI Metrics

The evaluation harness implements the following community-standard CAPRI metrics:

| Metric | Name | Description | Range |
|--------|------|-------------|-------|
| iRMS | Interface RMSD | Root-mean-square deviation of interface residues | 0-100Å |
| LRMS | Ligand RMSD | RMSD of ligand after superposing receptor | 0-100Å |
| Fnat | Fraction of Native contacts | Proportion of native interface contacts recovered | 0-1 |
| DockQ | DockQ Score | Combined quality score derived from iRMS, LRMS, Fnat | 0-1 |
| CAPRI | CAPRI Classification | Qualitative assessment: Incorrect/Acceptable/Medium/High | categorical |

**Sources**: [README.md:304]()

### Missing System Penalty

To ensure fair comparison across methods, systems with missing predictions receive penalty scores:

```python
{
    "iRMS": 100.0,
    "LRMS": 100.0,
    "Fnat": 0.0,
    "DockQ": 0.0,
    "CAPRI": "Incorrect",
}
```

These penalty values are applied when a method fails to produce predictions for a system in the benchmark set. The `--allow_missing` flag controls whether missing systems cause evaluation to fail or are penalized.

**Sources**: [README.md:365-376]()

### Decoy Rank Extraction

The evaluation system extracts model ranking from decoy filenames using a regular expression pattern: `r"\d+(?=\D*$)"`. This pattern matches the last sequence of digits in the filename, allowing flexible naming schemes like:

- `model_1.pdb`, `model_2.pdb`, ... (simple ranking)
- `decoy_rank_001.pdb`, `decoy_rank_002.pdb`, ... (zero-padded ranking)
- `prediction_top1.pdb`, `prediction_top2.pdb`, ... (alternative naming)

**Sources**: [README.md:360]()

## Key Classes

### MethodMetrics

The `MethodMetrics` class aggregates per-system metrics into leaderboard-ready results. It is implemented in [src/pinder-eval/pinder/eval/dockq/method.py]() and handles:

- Loading evaluation results across all systems
- Computing summary statistics (mean, median, success rates)
- Generating leaderboard entries
- Handling missing predictions with penalty scores

**Sources**: [README.md:380]()

## Programmatic Usage

The evaluation harness can be used programmatically as an alternative to the CLI:

```python
from pinder.eval import evaluate_method

# Evaluate a method's predictions
results = evaluate_method(
    eval_dir="path/to/eval_dir",
    method_name="my_method",
    allow_missing=True,
    max_workers=8
)

# Results contain per-system metrics
for system_id, metrics in results.items():
    print(f"{system_id}: DockQ={metrics['DockQ']:.3f}")
```

**Note**: The exact API may vary. Refer to [pinder.eval.run]() for the current implementation details.

**Sources**: [README.md:378]()

## Evaluation Pipeline Integration

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Method Predictions"
        HOLO_PRED["Holo Decoys<br/>Predictions from bound monomers"]
        APO_PRED["Apo Decoys<br/>Predictions from unbound monomers"]
        PRED_PRED["Predicted Decoys<br/>Predictions from AF2 monomers"]
    end
    
    subgraph "pinder.eval"
        PARSER["Decoy Parser<br/>Load and validate structures"]
        METRIC_CALC["Metrics Calculator<br/>Compute CAPRI scores"]
        AGGREGATOR["Results Aggregator<br/>MethodMetrics class"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Outputs"
        SYSTEM_CSV["System-level CSV<br/>Per-system scores"]
        LEADERBOARD_CSV["Leaderboard CSV<br/>Aggregated statistics"]
        RANKINGS["Method Rankings<br/>Top-N performance"]
    end
    
    HOLO_PRED --> PARSER
    APO_PRED --> PARSER
    PRED_PRED --> PARSER
    
    PARSER --> METRIC_CALC
    METRIC_CALC --> AGGREGATOR
    
    AGGREGATOR --> SYSTEM_CSV
    AGGREGATOR --> LEADERBOARD_CSV
    AGGREGATOR --> RANKINGS
```

**Sources**: [README.md:288-298](), [README.md:300-380]()

## Test Set Compatibility

The evaluation harness supports all PINDER benchmark test sets:

| Test Set | Systems | Use Case |
|----------|---------|----------|
| PINDER-XL | 1,955 | Full benchmark evaluation |
| PINDER-S | 250 | Fast evaluation subset (diverse annotations) |
| PINDER-AF2 | 180 | AlphaFold2-deleaked subset for AF2-MM comparison |

Methods are evaluated separately on each test set, with results typically reported for all three benchmarks to allow comprehensive assessment across different evaluation scenarios.

**Sources**: [README.md:247-251]()

## Parallel Processing

The evaluation harness supports parallel processing of systems using Python's multiprocessing:

- **Default behavior**: Uses all available CPU cores
- **Custom workers**: Specify `--max_workers N` to limit parallelism
- **Serial mode**: Use `--serial` flag to disable multiprocessing (useful for debugging)

Parallel evaluation significantly speeds up scoring when evaluating methods on large test sets like PINDER-XL.

**Sources**: [README.md:324-325]()

## Custom Index Support

The evaluation harness can be used with custom dataset splits via the `--custom_index` option:

**Requirements**:
- Must follow PINDER index schema (same columns as standard index)
- Must define test holdout sets with `split` column
- Does not need to share the same systems as official PINDER splits

This feature enables evaluation on custom benchmark sets while leveraging the same metrics and infrastructure.

**Sources**: [README.md:322-323]()

# Page: Frequently Asked Questions

# Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb](examples/pinder-loader.ipynb)

</details>



This document addresses common questions about using the PINDER dataset, troubleshooting issues, and optimizing performance. For detailed tutorials on specific features, see [Quick Start Guide](#2), [Core Data Structures](#3), and [Data Loading System](#4).

## Installation and Setup

### How do I install PINDER?

The basic installation requires only `pinder-core`:

```bash
pip install pinder
```

For additional functionality, install with extras:

```bash
# For evaluation capabilities
pip install pinder[eval]

# For all features
pip install pinder[all]
```

Sources: [README.md:44-118]()

### Why does fastpdb installation fail on my system?

`fastpdb` is a Rust-based dependency that requires pre-built wheels or the Rust toolchain. Pre-built wheels are available for:
- Linux with glibc≥2.34 (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9+)
- MacOS Sierra (10.12) or newer
- Windows

If your platform doesn't match, install the Rust toolchain first:

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
```

Then install pinder.

Sources: [README.md:24-42]()

### How do I install torch-cluster for graph neural networks?

`torch-cluster` is optional and only needed for graph-based workflows with `PPIDataset`. Installation depends on your PyTorch and CUDA versions:

```bash
# Replace ${TORCH} and ${CUDA} with your versions
pip install torch-cluster -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html
```

For Apple Silicon Macs, install from source:

```bash
pip install torch
pip install torch-cluster
```

Sources: [README.md:70-91]()

## Dataset Management

### Where is the dataset stored?

By default, PINDER stores data in `~/.local/share/pinder/<release>`. You can customize this with the `PINDER_BASE_DIR` environment variable:

```bash
export PINDER_BASE_DIR=~/my-custom-location/pinder
```

Check the current location:

```python
from pinder.core import get_pinder_location
print(get_pinder_location())
```

Sources: [README.md:123-142]()

### How much disk space do I need?

The complete dataset requires approximately 700GB:

| Component | Compressed | Unpacked |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| pdbs.zip | 144GB | 672GB |
| test_set_pdbs.zip | 149MB | 705MB |
| mappings.zip | 6.8GB | 25GB |
| index.parquet | - | ~100MB |
| metadata.parquet | - | ~200MB |

Sources: [README.md:197-208]()

### Can I download only a subset of the data?

Yes. The index and metadata files can be used independently for exploration. Individual PDB files are downloaded on-demand by `PinderSystem` when accessed. You can also download specific splits:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

# Only test set will be downloaded as needed
loader = PinderLoader(split="test", subset="pinder_s")
```

Sources: [README.md:146-161](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py]()

### How do I update to a new dataset version?

For index/metadata updates without structure changes:

```bash
pinder_update_index
```

For structure file updates:

```bash
pinder_sync_data
```

The current release version is `2024-02`.

Sources: [README.md:210-239]()

## Data Loading and Filtering

### What's the difference between PinderSystem, PinderLoader, and PinderDataset?

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Data Access Hierarchy"
        SYSTEM["PinderSystem<br/>Single system<br/>Direct structure access"]
        LOADER["PinderLoader<br/>Iterator over systems<br/>Applies filters/transforms"]
        DATASET["PinderDataset<br/>PyTorch Dataset<br/>Returns tensors"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Use Cases"
        UC1["Inspect single<br/>structure"]
        UC2["Iterate with<br/>filters"]
        UC3["Train ML<br/>models"]
    end
    
    UC1 --> SYSTEM
    UC2 --> LOADER
    UC3 --> DATASET
    
    SYSTEM --> LOADER
    LOADER --> DATASET
```

- **PinderSystem**: Load and inspect individual protein complexes with all associated structures (native, holo, apo, predicted)
- **PinderLoader**: Iterator that applies filters, transforms, and monomer selection strategies across multiple systems
- **PinderDataset**: PyTorch-compatible dataset that converts structures to tensors for training

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py]()

### How do I filter systems by quality criteria?

PINDER provides three filter levels:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader
from pinder.core.loader import filters

# System-level filters
base_filters = [
    filters.FilterByMissingHolo(),
    filters.FilterSubByContacts(min_contacts=5, radius=10.0),
    filters.FilterDetachedHolo(radius=12, max_components=2),
]

# Monomer-level filters
sub_filters = [
    filters.FilterSubByAtomTypes(min_atom_types=4),
    filters.FilterByHoloOverlap(min_overlap=5),
    filters.FilterByHoloSeqIdentity(min_sequence_identity=0.8),
]

# Structure-level filters
structure_filters = [
    filters.MinAtomTypesFilter(),
]

loader = PinderLoader(
    split="train",
    base_filters=base_filters,
    sub_filters=sub_filters,
    structure_filters=structure_filters,
)
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:438-477](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/filters.py]()

### How do I filter by metadata annotations?

Use the `FilterMetadataFields` filter or pandas queries on the index/metadata:

```python
from pinder.core.loader import filters

# Method 1: Using FilterMetadataFields
base_filters = [
    filters.FilterMetadataFields(
        contains_antibody=('', False),
        resolution=('<=', 2.75),
        method=('!=', 'X-RAY DIFFRACTION'),
    ),
]

# Method 2: Query index directly
from pinder.core import get_index, PinderLoader

index = get_index()
filtered_ids = index.query(
    'split == "train" and chain1_neff > 10 and chain2_neff > 10'
).id.tolist()

loader = PinderLoader(ids=filtered_ids)
```

Sources: [README.md:626-667](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/filters.py]()

## Monomer Selection and Structure Types

### What are holo, apo, and predicted monomers?

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Structure Types"
        NATIVE["native<br/>Ground-truth complex"]
        HOLO_R["holo_receptor<br/>Bound receptor from native"]
        HOLO_L["holo_ligand<br/>Bound ligand from native"]
        APO_R["apo_receptor<br/>Unbound receptor structure"]
        APO_L["apo_ligand<br/>Unbound ligand structure"]
        PRED_R["pred_receptor<br/>AlphaFold2 predicted"]
        PRED_L["pred_ligand<br/>AlphaFold2 predicted"]
    end
    
    NATIVE -->|extract| HOLO_R
    NATIVE -->|extract| HOLO_L
    
    HOLO_R -.->|paired via<br/>UniProt| APO_R
    HOLO_L -.->|paired via<br/>UniProt| APO_L
    
    HOLO_R -.->|paired via<br/>UniProt| PRED_R
    HOLO_L -.->|paired via<br/>UniProt| PRED_L
```

- **holo**: Monomers extracted from the native bound complex (always available)
- **apo**: Unbound monomers from separate PDB structures (available for ~17% of systems)
- **predicted**: AlphaFold2 predicted structures (available for ~25% of systems)

Sources: [README.md:398-406](), [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:246-269]()

### How do I control which monomer types are used?

Use the `monomer_priority` parameter:

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PinderDataset

# Use only holo monomers
dataset = PinderDataset(split="train", monomer_priority="holo")

# Use only apo monomers (falls back to holo if unavailable)
dataset = PinderDataset(split="train", monomer_priority="apo", fallback_to_holo=True)

# Use only predicted monomers
dataset = PinderDataset(split="train", monomer_priority="pred")

# Randomly select same type for both receptor and ligand
dataset = PinderDataset(split="train", monomer_priority="random")

# Randomly select types independently for receptor and ligand
dataset = PinderDataset(split="train", monomer_priority="random_mixed")
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:811-837](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py]()

### What does fallback_to_holo do?

When `fallback_to_holo=True` (default), if the requested monomer type (apo or predicted) is unavailable, the system will use the holo monomer instead. This allows training on all available systems while still incorporating unbound structures when possible.

When `fallback_to_holo=False`, systems without the requested monomer type will be skipped.

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:829-835](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py]()

### How do I check which systems have apo or predicted structures?

Use boolean columns in the index:

```python
from pinder.core import get_index

index = get_index()

# Systems with both apo monomers
apo_both = index.query('apo_R and apo_L')

# Systems with at least one apo monomer
apo_any = index.query('apo_R or apo_L')

# Systems with predicted structures
pred_both = index.query('predicted_R and predicted_L')

# Systems with apo receptor and predicted ligand
mixed = index.query('apo_R and predicted_L')
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:262-269](), [README.md:529-566]()

## PyTorch Integration

### How do I create a PyTorch DataLoader?

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PinderDataset, get_torch_loader

# Create dataset
dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    monomer_priority="random_mixed",
)

# Create dataloader
dataloader = get_torch_loader(
    dataset,
    batch_size=2,
    shuffle=True,
    num_workers=4,
)

# Get a batch
batch = next(iter(dataloader))
# batch is a dict with keys: target_complex, feature_complex, id, sample_id, target_id
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:1687-1749](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py]()

### How do I use PyTorch Geometric with PINDER?

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PPIDataset, get_geo_loader
from pinder.core.loader.geodata import NodeRepresentation

# Define node types
nodes = {
    NodeRepresentation("atom"),
    NodeRepresentation("residue")
}

# Create dataset
dataset = PPIDataset(
    node_types=nodes,
    split="train",
    monomer1="holo_receptor",
    monomer2="holo_ligand",
)

# Create dataloader
loader = get_geo_loader(dataset, batch_size=32)

# Get a batch (returns HeteroData)
batch = next(iter(loader))
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:1762-1816](), [README.md:466-515]()

### What's the structure of a PinderDataset batch?

A batch is a dictionary with the following structure:

```python
{
    'target_complex': {
        'atom_coordinates': Tensor[batch, atoms, 3],
        'atom_types': Tensor[batch, atoms, 1],
        'element_types': Tensor[batch, atoms, 1],
        'residue_types': Tensor[batch, atoms, 1],
        'residue_coordinates': Tensor[batch, residues, 3],
        'residue_ids': Tensor[batch, atoms],
        'chain_ids': Tensor[batch, atoms],
    },
    'feature_complex': {
        # Same structure as target_complex
    },
    'id': List[str],  # PINDER system IDs
    'sample_id': List[str],  # Selected monomer IDs
    'target_id': List[str],  # Holo monomer IDs
}
```

Tensors are padded to the maximum length in the batch.

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:722-804](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py]()

### How does batching handle variable-sized structures?

PINDER uses padding to create uniform batch sizes. The `collate_batch` function pads tensors to the maximum dimensions in the batch:

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import pad_and_stack

# Pad coordinates with value -100
coords_batch = pad_and_stack(
    [struct1.coords, struct2.coords],
    dim=0,
    value=-100
)
```

You can implement custom collation functions for different padding strategies.

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:2751-2872](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py]()

## Advanced Usage

### How do I implement custom transforms?

Transforms operate on `Structure` objects. Create a class inheriting from `StructureTransform`:

```python
from pinder.core.loader.transforms import StructureTransform
from pinder.core.loader.structure import Structure

class SelectAtomTypes(StructureTransform):
    def __init__(self, atom_types: list[str]):
        self.atom_types = atom_types
    
    def __call__(self, structure: Structure) -> Structure:
        mask = [atom in self.atom_types for atom in structure.atom_array.atom_name]
        structure.atom_array = structure.atom_array[mask]
        return structure

# Use in dataset
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PinderDataset

dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    structure_transforms_feature=[SelectAtomTypes(["CA", "N", "C", "O"])],
)
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:782-803](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/transforms.py]()

### How do I implement diversity sampling?

Use `torch.utils.data.WeightedRandomSampler` with inverse cluster size weights:

```python
from torch.utils.data import WeightedRandomSampler
import torch

def inverse_cluster_size_sampler(dataset):
    index = dataset.index
    cluster_counts = index["cluster_id"].value_counts()
    index = index.merge(
        cluster_counts.rename("cluster_count"),
        left_on="cluster_id",
        right_index=True
    )
    weights = 1.0 / torch.tensor(index.cluster_count.values)
    return WeightedRandomSampler(
        weights=weights,
        num_samples=len(cluster_counts),
        replacement=True,
    )

# Use with DataLoader
sampler = inverse_cluster_size_sampler(dataset)
loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=32, sampler=sampler)
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:2513-2563](), [README.md:391]()

### How do I use alternative apo structures?

By default, PINDER uses the canonical apo structure (highest quality) stored in `apo_R_pdb` and `apo_L_pdb` columns. To access alternative apo structures:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

loader = PinderLoader(
    split="train",
    monomer_priority="apo",
    use_canonical_apo=False,  # Use alternative apo structures
)
```

Alternative apo structures are listed in the `apo_R_pdbs` and `apo_L_pdbs` columns (comma-separated).

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:836](), [README.md:548-551]()

### How do I pre-specify which monomers to use for each system?

Pass a dictionary mapping system IDs to monomer filenames:

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import PinderDataset

monomer_spec = {
    "1df0__A1_Q07009--1df0__B1_Q64537": {
        "receptor": "1df0__A1_Q07009-R.pdb",
        "ligand": "6isu__A1_Q64537.pdb"  # Use apo ligand
    }
}

dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    pre_specified_monomers=monomer_spec,
)
```

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py]()

## Evaluation

### How do I use the evaluation harness?

Organize predictions in the required directory structure:

```
eval_dir/
└── method_name/
    └── system_id/
        ├── holo_decoys/
        │   ├── model_1.pdb
        │   └── model_2.pdb
        ├── apo_decoys/
        │   └── model_1.pdb
        └── predicted_decoys/
            └── model_1.pdb
```

Then run evaluation:

```bash
pinder_eval --eval_dir eval_dir --method_name my_method
```

Or use the Python API:

```python
from pinder.eval.dockq import MethodMetrics

metrics = MethodMetrics(
    eval_dir="eval_dir",
    method_name="my_method",
)
results = metrics.compute_metrics()
```

Sources: [README.md:307-380](), [src/pinder-eval/pinder/eval/dockq/method.py]()

### What metrics are computed?

PINDER uses standard CAPRI metrics:

| Metric | Description | Range |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| iRMS | Interface RMSD | 0-100Å |
| LRMS | Ligand RMSD | 0-100Å |
| Fnat | Fraction of native contacts | 0-1 |
| DockQ | Composite quality score | 0-1 |
| CAPRI | Classification (Incorrect, Acceptable, Medium, High) | Categorical |

For missing predictions, penalty values are assigned: iRMS=100, LRMS=100, Fnat=0, DockQ=0.

Sources: [README.md:365-376](), [src/pinder-eval/pinder/eval/dockq/]()

### How can I use the evaluation harness outside of a PINDER context?

The evaluation functions work with any PDB files:

```python
from pinder.eval.dockq import calculate_dockq

# Compare predicted vs native structure
metrics = calculate_dockq(
    predicted_pdb="prediction.pdb",
    native_pdb="ground_truth.pdb",
    receptor_chain="R",
    ligand_chain="L",
)

print(f"DockQ: {metrics['DockQ']:.3f}")
print(f"iRMS: {metrics['iRMS']:.3f}")
```

Sources: [README.md:378](), [src/pinder-eval/pinder/eval/dockq/dockq.py]()

## Performance Optimization

### How can I speed up data loading?

1. **Use multiple workers**:
```python
loader = get_torch_loader(dataset, num_workers=4)
```

2. **Cache processed systems** (for `PPIDataset`):
```python
dataset = PPIDataset(
    split="train",
    node_types=nodes,
    use_cache=True,
    force_reload=False,
)
```

3. **Limit dataset size during development**:
```python
dataset = PPIDataset(split="train", limit_by=100)
```

4. **Use `fastpdb` engine** (default, faster than biotite):
```python
from pinder.core.loader.structure import Structure
struct = Structure("path.pdb", pdb_engine="fastpdb")
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:1808](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/structure.py]()

### How much memory does the dataset require?

Memory usage depends on your workflow:

- **PinderSystem** (single system): ~10-50MB per system
- **PinderDataset** (in-memory index only): ~500MB for full training set
- **PPIDataset** (cached): ~1-2GB for processed graph files
- **DataLoader** with batching: Depends on batch size and workers

The index and structures are loaded lazily, so memory footprint stays manageable even with large datasets.

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/dataset.py]()

### Should I use PinderDataset or PPIDataset?

```mermaid
graph TB
    CHOICE{What type of<br/>model?}
    
    CHOICE -->|Standard NN<br/>CNNs, Transformers| PINDER["PinderDataset<br/>- Dict of tensors<br/>- Flexible structure<br/>- Easy customization"]
    
    CHOICE -->|Graph NN| PPI["PPIDataset<br/>- HeteroData graphs<br/>- Node/edge features<br/>- Caches to disk"]
    
    PINDER --> USE1["Use with<br/>torch.DataLoader"]
    PPI --> USE2["Use with<br/>torch_geometric.DataLoader"]
```

- **PinderDataset**: For standard neural networks. Returns dictionaries of tensors. More flexible for custom featurization.
- **PPIDataset**: For graph neural networks. Returns `HeteroData` objects with separate node/edge types. Caches processed graphs to disk.

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:694-714](), [README.md:433-514]()

## Troubleshooting

### Why do I get "FileNotFoundError" when loading systems?

The PDB file may not be downloaded yet. PINDER downloads files on-demand from Google Cloud Storage:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderSystem

# This automatically downloads if not present
system = PinderSystem("1df0__A1_Q07009--1df0__B1_Q64537")
```

If download fails, check:
1. Internet connectivity
2. Google Cloud Storage access (no authentication needed)
3. Disk space availability

Sources: [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/index/system.py](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/utils/cloud.py]()

### Why are my filters removing all systems?

Check filter criteria are not too strict:

```python
from pinder.core import PinderLoader

loader = PinderLoader(
    split="train",
    base_filters=base_filters,
)

print(f"Systems passing filters: {len(loader)}")

# Try removing filters one at a time to identify the issue
for filt in base_filters:
    test_loader = PinderLoader(split="train", base_filters=[filt])
    print(f"{filt.__class__.__name__}: {len(test_loader)} systems")
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:583-600]()

### Why do I get "RuntimeError: stack expects each tensor to be equal size"?

This happens when batching variable-sized structures without padding. Use the provided collation function:

```python
from pinder.core.loader.dataset import collate_batch, get_torch_loader

loader = get_torch_loader(
    dataset,
    batch_size=2,
    collate_fn=collate_batch,  # Handles padding
)
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:2740-2872]()

### What does "crop_equal_monomer_shapes" do?

When comparing holo vs apo/predicted structures, they may have different residues resolved. Setting `crop_equal_monomer_shapes=True` (default) crops both structures to common atoms:

```python
dataset = PinderDataset(
    split="train",
    crop_equal_monomer_shapes=True,  # Ensures target and feature have same shape
)
```

This is essential for models that expect fixed input/output dimensions.

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:1599-1606](), [src/pinder-core/pinder/core/loader/loader.py]()

### How do I debug which monomers are selected?

Check the `sample_id` field in the batch:

```python
batch = next(iter(dataloader))

for i, (pinder_id, sample_id, target_id) in enumerate(
    zip(batch['id'], batch['sample_id'], batch['target_id'])
):
    print(f"System: {pinder_id}")
    print(f"  Target (holo): {target_id}")
    print(f"  Sample: {sample_id}")
```

The monomer filenames indicate the type (holo/apo/pred) used.

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:1566-1578]()

### Why does PPIDataset processing take so long?

`PPIDataset` converts structures to graphs and caches them to disk. First-time processing is slow but subsequent loads are fast:

```python
# First run: slow (processes all systems)
dataset = PPIDataset(split="train", force_reload=True)

# Subsequent runs: fast (loads from cache)
dataset = PPIDataset(split="train", force_reload=False)
```

Use `limit_by` for faster iteration during development:

```python
dataset = PPIDataset(split="train", limit_by=100)
```

Sources: [examples/pinder-loader.ipynb:1776-1815]()

## Data Organization

### What's in the index vs metadata?

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "index.parquet"
        IDX_FIELDS["id, split, pdb_id<br/>cluster_id<br/>uniprot_R/L<br/>holo_R/L_pdb<br/>apo_R/L_pdb<br/>predicted_R/L_pdb<br/>apo/holo/pred flags<br/>chain_R/L<br/>contains_antibody/enzyme"]
    end
    
    subgraph "metadata.parquet"
        META_FIELDS["resolution, method<br/>buried_sasa<br/>intermolecular_contacts<br/>planarity, elongation<br/>interface_gaps<br/>ECOD/SCOP annotations<br/>oligomeric state<br/>complex_type"]
    end
    
    USAGE["Filter and select<br/>systems for loading"]
    
    IDX_FIELDS --> USAGE
    META_FIELDS --> USAGE
```

- **index.parquet**: System identifiers, split assignments, monomer availability, cluster IDs (58 fields)
- **metadata.parquet**: Detailed structural properties, quality metrics, annotations (45+ fields)

Use index for basic filtering and system selection. Use metadata for quality-based filtering.

Sources: [README.md:172-176](), [README.md:529-624]()

### How are systems split into train/val/test?

```mermaid
graph TD
    ALL["All PDB dimers<br/>~200K structures"]
    
    CLUSTER["FoldSeek clustering<br/>Interface similarity"]
    
    PROTO_TEST["Proto-test<br/>32,775 PPIs<br/>5,047 clusters"]
    
    DELEAK["Deleaking<br/>Transitive neighbor<br/>removal depth=2"]
    
    TEST["PINDER-XL<br/>1,955 systems"]
    VAL["PINDER-Val<br/>1,958 systems"]
    TRAIN["PINDER-Train<br/>2.4M+ pairs<br/>42,220 clusters"]
    
    ALL --> CLUSTER
    CLUSTER --> PROTO_TEST
    PROTO_TEST --> DELEAK
    DELEAK --> TEST
    DELEAK --> VAL
    DELEAK --> TRAIN
```

Systems are clustered by interface similarity, then cluster representatives are selected for test/val sets with strict deleaking to prevent data leakage.

Sources: [README.md:733-778](), [README.md:245-261]()

### What's the difference between PINDER-XL, PINDER-S, and PINDER-AF2?

| Test Set | Size | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| PINDER-XL | 1,955 | Full test set, includes all quality systems |
| PINDER-S | 250 | Fast subset for quick evaluation |
| PINDER-AF2 | 180 | Deleaked from AlphaFold-Multimer training data |

All are subsets of the same high-quality systems, just filtered for different use cases.

Sources: [README.md:245-251](), [README.md:783-785]()

## Miscellaneous

### Can I use PINDER for antibody-antigen docking?

Yes, but note that antibodies are included in the general dataset. Filter for them:

```python
index = get_index()

# Antibody-antigen systems
ab_systems = index.query('contains_antibody and contains_antigen')

# Exclude antibodies
no_ab_systems = index.query('not contains_antibody')
```

A dedicated `pinder-ab` benchmark is planned for future releases.

Sources: [README.md:564-566](), [README.md:683]()

### How do I cite PINDER?

When using PINDER in research, please cite the dataset and relevant tools. Citation information is available in the repository and will be updated with publication details.

Sources: [README.md:1-13]()

### What Python versions are supported?

PINDER supports Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12. Full test coverage is maintained for 3.10 and 3.11, with basic tests for 3.12.

Sources: [README.md:838-841](), [.github/workflows/pr.yaml]()

### Where can I get help?

- **Documentation**: See the [examples](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder/tree/main/examples) directory for notebooks
- **Issues**: Report bugs or request features on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder/issues)
- **Code**: Browse the source at [github.com/pinder-org/pinder](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder)

Sources: [README.md:803-870]()
